event.wren_heart10.outro: {if choice:wren.bag.go}I'm not leaving yet. But I wrote the map into the second verse.{else}{if choice:wren.bag.stay}I wrote the stay into the chorus. You'll hear it.{else}I wrote the quiet part for you. You'll know which.{/if}{/if}
event.wren_friend.intro: Friday means bingo. Not numbers. Gossip. Come and cross something off.
event.wren_friend.doing: Someone's cat is in love with the postal cart. I'm marking it.
event.wren_friend.wrap: No bingo today. Only a full house of nonsense. Wonderful.
event.hazel_heart4.intro: I'd like to swap something. (A book for a book.) Is that odd?
event.hazel_heart4.after: Thank you. (I'll look after it.) I always do.
event.hazel_heart6.intro: Could you come to the back? (There's something I don't say out loud.)
event.hazel_heart6.after: Thank you for not laughing. (I checked your face.) It stayed kind.
event.hazel_heart8.intro: Would you hear a thing I wrote? (Only one of you. Just one.)
event.hazel_heart8.after: I'll read it properly, one day. (To more than one.)
event.hazel_heart10.intro: I'll read for you. (Just you. The shelves don't count.)
event.hazel_heart10.outro: {if choice:hazel.rehearsal.critique}I cut the middle. (You were right.) Thank you.{else}I kept the lamp. (And you.) Thank you.{/if}
event.hazel_friend.ask: Do you have blackberries? (I'm baking a peace offering for an overdue book.)
event.hazel_friend.success: Perfect. (He'll forgive me. Or at least eat.) Thank you.
event.hazel_friend.fallback: Come back with blackberries? (It's a small crisis. A quiet one.)
event.bram_heart4.intro: Hm. Come here. I need a second pair of hands.
event.bram_heart4.after: Hm. Good enough. Better than good.
event.bram_heart6.intro: Hm. Sit. I've got something to say. It'll be long for me.
event.bram_heart6.after: Hm. That's all of it. Don't ask me to repeat it.
event.bram_heart8.intro: Hm. Juno made something. I want you to look at it. Tell me true.
event.bram_heart8.after: Hm. Thanks. I'll tell her. Maybe.
event.bram_heart10.intro: Hm. I made you something. Don't speak. Just take it.
event.bram_heart10.give: Gold. Soft. Not for work. For you. Hm.
event.bram_heart10.thanks: {if choice:bram.juno.ask}You asked what I see. I see you. Hm.{else}Hm. It's not much. It's all I could say.{/if}
event.bram_friend.intro: Hm. Marcus is closed. We sit. Come on.
event.bram_friend.doing: Hm. Good bench. Good silence. Don't spoil it.
event.bram_friend.wrap: Hm. That was nice. Don't tell anyone.
dlg.wren.openmic.0: Well? Be honest. A performer needs one honest face in the crowd.
dlg.wren.openmic.r0: Oh, I could live on that. Do it again, but louder.
dlg.wren.openmic.r1: A heckler! At last I'm somebody. I'll put you in the second verse.
dlg.wren.openmic.r2: Ha! Fair. I'd hide too. Come out, though. The second verse is better.
dlg.wren.kitchen.0: One more pinch of something. Pepper, cider, or leave it plain?
dlg.wren.kitchen.r0: Brave it is! If I weep, blame the pepper, not me.
dlg.wren.kitchen.r1: Cider. Sweet and a little sly. That's very you.
dlg.wren.kitchen.r2: Plain. Hm. You think it's already good? Nobody says that. I'm keeping you.
dlg.wren.bag.0: There's a bag under my bed. Packed since the day I arrived. I haven't opened it in years, and I haven't unpacked it either.
dlg.wren.bag.1: I came here to rest for a season. That was eight years ago. Tell me: should I go, stay, or just keep it under the bed?
dlg.wren.bag.r0: Go. Hm. You say it so plainly. I might. Someday. With a very good map.
dlg.wren.bag.r1: Stay. Oh. That's a nicer word than I expected.
dlg.wren.bag.r2: ...You didn't tell me what to do. That's the kindest thing anyone has done. Thank you.
dlg.hazel.swap.0: What would you swap? (I'm not choosing for you.)
dlg.hazel.swap.r0: Oh. (She holds it with both hands.) I'll read it twice.
dlg.hazel.swap.r1: A recipe. (A book without a spine.) I like that.
dlg.hazel.swap.r2: Thank you for saying so. (Most people pretend.) I'll pick something short.
dlg.hazel.hiding.0: I hide in the stacks when it's loud. (It's quieter between the books.) Is that strange?
dlg.hazel.hiding.r0: Pages turning, far away. (Someone else's thoughts, stored.) It's company.
dlg.hazel.hiding.r2: Ha. (A small one.) You're not wrong.
dlg.hazel.rehearsal.0: ...and so the lamp burned lower, and nobody minded. (That's the end.) What did you hear?
dlg.hazel.rehearsal.r0: Lovely. (I'll hold on to that word.) Thank you.
dlg.hazel.rehearsal.r1: The middle. (I knew it.) Thank you for saying so out loud.
dlg.hazel.rehearsal.r2: The lamp is a bit much. (It was supposed to be.) I'll keep it.
dlg.bram.repair.0: Hm. The handle's cracked. Hold, hammer, or watch?
dlg.bram.repair.r2: Hm. Watching's a skill. Few have it.
dlg.bram.long.0: I worked alone a long time, and I decided I liked it, and I was wrong about that, and I'm saying so because you came in and sat down.
dlg.bram.long.r1: Hm. Glad. Hm. Yes. Me too.
dlg.bram.juno.0: She made a horseshoe. Crooked. She's proud. What do I say?
dlg.bram.juno.r0: Hm. Wonderful. It's crooked. Still wonderful.
dlg.bram.juno.r1: Ha. Hm. I'll tease her. Gently. With a nail.
dlg.bram.juno.r2: ...Hm. Me. When I started. That's what I see.
dlg.hazel.hiding.c0: Ask what she hears in the quiet.
dlg.hazel.hiding.c2: Joke about hiding in a book.
dlg.bram.juno.c2: Ask what he sees in it.
letter.wren_bday.subject: Someone has a birthday coming
letter.wren_bday.body: Between us, I do hate fuss. But if you were to bring something wrapped, I would pretend to be surprised. Don't say I asked. -- Wren
letter.wren_thanks.subject: A song for you
letter.wren_thanks.body: That terrible song? I'm keeping the second verse. It's yours now. Come hear the third one when it exists. -- Wren
letter.hazel_bday.subject: A note, very small
letter.hazel_bday.body: My birthday is soon. (I don't mind if it passes quietly.) A book would not be unwelcome. -- Hazel
letter.hazel_thanks.subject: About the swap
letter.hazel_thanks.body: I read it twice. (As promised.) Come by when you have an opinion. -- Hazel
letter.bram_bday.subject: Hm
letter.bram_bday.body: Birthday soon. No fuss. Copper would be fine. -- Bram
letter.bram_thanks.subject: Handle
letter.bram_thanks.body: Handle held. Good work. Come by. -- Bram
dlg.react.wren.spring.d.0: Spring! The whole village smells like mud and good intentions. I love it. Don't tell the mud.
dlg.react.wren.winter.d.0: First snow, and my stove has already started a feud with the draft. Come in. Pick a side.
dlg.react.wren.harvest.d.0: I heard you harvested something! Everyone's talking. Mostly me. Show me what grew.
dlg.react.wren.coins.d.0: A little bird told me you found coins. The bird was me. I follow everything.
dlg.react.hazel.spring.d.0: The windows are open. (The pages like it.) Spring smells like paper.
dlg.react.hazel.winter.d.0: Snow. (The library is the warmest place in town.) Stay as long as you like.
dlg.react.hazel.harvest.d.0: You grew something. (I'm told that's a skill.) I'd like to read about it.
dlg.react.hazel.wren.d.0: I heard a song from the saloon. (Through three walls.) It was terrible. I think she knew.
dlg.react.bram.spring.d.0: Hm. Spring. Plows are coming. Bring yours early.
dlg.react.bram.winter.d.0: Hm. Snow. Forge is warm. Sit if you like.
dlg.react.bram.harvest.d.0: Hm. First harvest. Good. Your hoe held up. I noticed.
dlg.react.bram.wren.d.0: Hm. Wren sang. I heard. Don't tell her I listened.
dlg.wren.pie.1.0: Marcus and Odalys are not speaking over a pie. I'm running a betting pool. Don't tell them.
dlg.wren.pie.2.0: The pie feud's day nine. The pie is still on the windowsill. Nobody dares touch it.
dlg.wren.notes.1.0: Someone's leaving notes on doors. "Nice shoes," one said. I'm flattered. I wasn't wearing shoes.
dlg.wren.notes.2.0: I found a note that only said "Hello." It's the nicest thing that's happened this week.
dlg.hazel.pie.1.0: A pie, two neighbors. (I'm cataloguing the feud under "Domestic.") Nobody asked.
dlg.hazel.pie.2.0: The pie has gone stale. (The feud hasn't.) I find that instructive.
dlg.hazel.notes.1.0: Someone slipped a note into a book. (It said "Good choice.") I'm not sure which book.
dlg.hazel.notes.2.0: I think the notes are kind. (I'm trying not to look for the writer.) Looking spoils it.
dlg.bram.pie.1.0: Hm. Pie feud. Two fools, one crust. I'd fix it with a hammer.
dlg.bram.pie.2.0: Hm. Both sides asked me to make a pie plate. I made one. Gave it to Juno.
dlg.bram.notes.1.0: Hm. A note on my anvil. It said "Nice work." Hm. I read it twice.
dlg.bram.notes.2.0: Hm. I don't know who writes the notes. I'd like to say thanks.
dlg.wren.bark.1.0: Fresh cider, fresh gossip, fresh start every Tuesday!
dlg.wren.bark.2.0: Someone owes me a rhyme for "turnip".
dlg.wren.bark.3.0: I'm not eavesdropping. The walls are just very talkative.
dlg.wren.bark.4.0: Day four of asking Bram for four words. Progress: "Hm."
dlg.wren.bark.5.0: Hazel borrowed my notebook. I hope she returns the gossip.
dlg.wren.bark.6.0: If a story's too good, I only improve it slightly.
dlg.wren.bark.7.0: Does anyone else hear a lute? No? Just me?
dlg.wren.bark.8.0: I'm writing a song about weather. It's mostly sighing.
dlg.wren.bark.rain.1.0: Rain on the roof. Best band in the village.
dlg.wren.bark.rain.2.0: Drip, drip, drip. I can't rhyme this one.
dlg.wren.bark.storm.1.0: That thunder has terrible timing. I admire it.
dlg.wren.bark.snow.1.0: Snow! Everything looks like it's keeping a secret.
dlg.wren.bark.spring.1.0: Spring! Everyone's hopeful and slightly muddy. My favorite crowd.
dlg.wren.bark.summer.1.0: Hot day. Cold cider. Honest math.
dlg.wren.bark.fall.1.0: Fall smells like cinnamon and other people's secrets.
dlg.wren.bark.winter.1.0: Winter: the season of stew and over-sharing.
dlg.wren.bark.morning.1.0: Too early for jokes. I'll do a mild pun.
dlg.wren.bark.evening.1.0: Evening crowd's in. Everyone has a story. Some are even true.
dlg.wren.bark.here.1.0: Sit anywhere. Except Felix's stool. It remembers him.
dlg.wren.bark.here.2.0: House rule: no sad songs before the second cider.
dlg.wren.bark.tue.1.0: Tuesday. My day off, my favorite hammock.
dlg.wren.bark.fri.1.0: Friday! Gossip bingo, anyone? Free pencil!
dlg.wren.bark.rare.1.0: I'm going to be famous. Eventually. Maybe posthumously.
dlg.wren.bark.rare.2.0: Whoever's reading this: you're doing better than you think.
dlg.hazel.bark.1.0: (Quietly.) Please. This is a library. A small one.
dlg.hazel.bark.2.0: I've misplaced a bookmark. (It's in a book.) Somewhere.
dlg.hazel.bark.3.0: Wren borrowed a pencil. (That's three weeks ago.)
dlg.hazel.bark.4.0: (Reading.) Hm. The ending is better than the middle.
dlg.hazel.bark.5.0: The index is out of order. (It's me. I did it.)
dlg.hazel.bark.6.0: Overdue books come back smelling of cider. (I won't ask.)
dlg.hazel.bark.7.0: I like this quiet. (It has good margins.)
dlg.hazel.bark.8.0: Bram returned a book early. (Again.) I'm suspicious.
dlg.hazel.bark.rain.1.0: Rain on the window. (Best soundtrack for a chapter.)
dlg.hazel.bark.rain.2.0: The roof ticks in the rain. (Like a slow clock.)
dlg.hazel.bark.storm.1.0: (Reading by candle.) Storms improve every sentence.
dlg.hazel.bark.snow.1.0: Snow. (Everything is a footnote to it.)
dlg.hazel.bark.spring.1.0: Windows open. (Pages turning on their own.)
dlg.hazel.bark.summer.1.0: Warm. (The books are drowsy.) So am I.
dlg.hazel.bark.fall.1.0: Fall is the season for long sentences.
dlg.hazel.bark.winter.1.0: Winter. (Tea, a blanket, a thick book.)
dlg.hazel.bark.evening.1.0: Almost closing. (One more chapter. Always one more.)
dlg.hazel.bark.here.1.0: Take your time. (Not too much of mine.)
dlg.hazel.bark.here.2.0: The cat section is on the left. (There isn't a cat.)
dlg.hazel.bark.sat.1.0: Saturday. (The village is loud. I read louder.)
dlg.hazel.bark.wed.1.0: Wednesday. (Nothing happens on Wednesdays.) I like that.
dlg.hazel.bark.rare.1.0: I'm writing a book about bookmarks. (It's a very short book.)
dlg.hazel.bark.rare.2.0: Someone left a note in a book. (It said, "Good choice.")
dlg.bram.bark.3.0: Careful. It's hot. It's always hot.
dlg.bram.bark.4.0: Wren talks. I listen. It's a system.
dlg.bram.bark.5.0: Hm. Juno labeled the tongs again.
dlg.bram.bark.6.0: Someone put a rubber chicken on the anvil. Hm.
dlg.bram.bark.7.0: Returned Hazel's book. Early. She stared.
dlg.bram.bark.rain.1.0: Rain. Roof's holding. Fire's holding. Good.
dlg.bram.bark.wind.1.0: Wind blows the ash around. Hm.
dlg.bram.bark.winter.1.0: Winter. The best seat is the forge.
dlg.bram.bark.here.2.0: Hm. Mind the floor. It has opinions.
dlg.bram.bark.rare.2.0: A good tool. A good friend. Both take time.
quest.wren_stew.title: Stew for the Regulars
quest.wren_stew.desc: Wren needs three mushrooms for her stew pot.
quest.wren_cider.title: Hops for the Cider
quest.wren_cider.desc: Wren is planning a cider with ideas above its station.
quest.wren_full_house.title: A Full House
quest.wren_full_house.desc: Wren is planning a proper evening and needs a bottle to open it.
quest.wren_full_house.o0: Bring a bottle of wine to Wren
quest.hazel_shelf.title: A Shelf That Holds
quest.hazel_shelf.desc: The poetry shelf at the library is bowing.
quest.hazel_pressed.title: Pressed Flowers
quest.hazel_pressed.desc: Hazel wants to press sunflowers for a secret book.
quest.hazel_notes.title: The Field Notes
quest.hazel_notes.desc: Hazel is describing the smells of the woods.
quest.bram_copper.title: A Clean Pour
quest.bram_hooks.title: Juno's Hooks
quest.bram_hooks.desc: Bram is out of iron for Juno's hooks.
dlg.wren.stew.ask.0: The regulars want stew, and my pot wants mushrooms. Three would do it. Forest floor, near the damp bits.
dlg.wren.stew.ask.1: Would you? I'll pay in gold and in first pick of the good stool.
dlg.wren.stew.ask.r0: A dear. Come back when your pockets smell of the woods.
dlg.wren.stew.ask.r1: Fair! The regulars are patient. Mostly. Ask me again.
dlg.wren.stew.remind.0: Three mushrooms, damp bits of the forest. I believe in you, and so does the pot.
dlg.wren.stew.turnin.0: Mushrooms! Oh, you wonderful menace. The pot is blushing. Take this, and the stool.
dlg.wren.cider.ask.0: Summer's coming, and I'm out of hops. Four, if you've a green thumb. I'm trying a cider with ideas above its station.
dlg.wren.cider.ask.1: You grow hops, I'll make history. A small history. Of cider.
dlg.wren.cider.ask.r0: Splendid! Four hops. I'll name the cider after you. Probably a rude name.
dlg.wren.cider.ask.r1: Another time, then. The cider will wait. It's a patient drink.
dlg.wren.cider.remind.0: Four hops, and the cider's yours. Well, mine. You'll get a taste.
dlg.wren.cider.turnin.0: Hops! Look at them! They smell like the future. Here, for your trouble, and a glass for later.
dlg.wren.house.ask.0: Between us, I'm planning a full house. A real one. Music, food, nobody in a corner. I need one thing from you.
dlg.wren.house.ask.1: A bottle of wine. A good one, from your own cellar. Something to open the evening.
dlg.wren.house.ask.r0: You're the best audience a nervous host could ask for. One bottle. I'll hold the door.
dlg.wren.house.ask.r1: Think. The idea will keep. So will I, mostly.
dlg.wren.house.remind.0: One bottle of wine, and I can open the doors. No pressure. A little pressure. Lovely pressure.
dlg.wren.house.turnin.0: There it is. Oh, [player]. I'll open it on the night, and you'll be first at the bar. Thank you.
dlg.hazel.shelf.ask.0: One of the shelves is bowing. (It's the poetry shelf. Of course it is.) It needs five planks of wood.
dlg.hazel.shelf.ask.1: Could you bring them? (I'd ask someone else. I'm asking you.)
dlg.hazel.shelf.ask.r0: Thank you. (Five planks. I wrote it down.) I'll make tea.
dlg.hazel.shelf.ask.r1: That's all right. (The poetry will manage.) Ask me again.
dlg.hazel.shelf.remind.0: Five planks. (The poetry shelf is holding its breath.)
dlg.hazel.shelf.turnin.0: These are perfect. (I'll sand them myself.) Thank you. Here, for the planks. And the tea.
dlg.hazel.pressed.ask.0: I'd like to press some flowers. (For a book. A secret one.) Two sunflowers, if you have them.
dlg.hazel.pressed.ask.1: They flatten nicely. (A sunflower is almost a page already.)
dlg.hazel.pressed.ask.r1: Maybe later. (Maybe is a fine word.)
dlg.hazel.pressed.remind.0: Two sunflowers. (I cleared a page for them.)
dlg.hazel.pressed.turnin.0: They're beautiful. (I'll keep one for myself.) Thank you, [player]. Take this.
dlg.hazel.notes.ask.0: I'm filling a notebook about the woods. (Smells, mostly.) Three wild garlic would help. Fresh.
dlg.hazel.notes.ask.1: I'd like to describe it properly. (A smell deserves a paragraph.)
dlg.hazel.notes.ask.r0: Wild garlic. (Three.) Thank you. (I'll describe your face when you bring it.)
dlg.hazel.notes.ask.r1: That's fine. (Smells keep better than people think.)
dlg.hazel.notes.remind.0: Three wild garlic. (The notebook is open to a blank page.)
dlg.hazel.notes.turnin.0: Oh. (She holds it near her face.) It's exactly the right sharpness. Thank you. This is yours, for the walk.
dlg.bram.copper.ask.0: Hm. I need copper bars. Three. Clean ones.
dlg.bram.copper.ask.1: Smelt them yourself. Good practice. Bring them here.
dlg.bram.copper.remind.0: Three copper bars. Clean ones. Hm.
dlg.bram.copper.turnin.0: Hm. Clean pour. Even edges. ...Good work. Take this.
dlg.bram.hooks.ask.0: Juno wants hooks. Forty. I'm out of iron. Two bars would do.
dlg.bram.hooks.ask.1: She'll say thanks. Loudly. I'd appreciate not hearing it alone.
dlg.bram.hooks.ask.r0: Hm. Good. I'll hold the forge.
dlg.bram.hooks.ask.r1: Hm. Later. She'll wait. She won't be quiet.
dlg.bram.hooks.remind.0: Two iron bars. Juno's hooks. Hm.
dlg.bram.hooks.turnin.0: Hm. Iron. Two. ...Thanks. Juno will say it louder. Here. For you.
event.story_pie_payoff.intro: [player]. A word. You're good with a delivery, aren't you?
event.story_pie_payoff.after: {if choice:pie.honest}She said 'good'. Out loud. Do not repeat it.{else}{if choice:pie.improve}She sent back a note: 'Cinnamon? Cheek.' I'm delighted.{else}You ate it. Fair. Odalys is baking a second. So am I.{/if}{/if}
event.story_notes_dorian.intro: Oh. You weren't meant to see that. I... it's easier on paper.
event.story_notes_dorian.after: A note says what a face can't. Mine can't say much. Thank you for staying.
event.story_notes_juno.intro: Don't look! I mean, look. I can't stop myself. Encouragement leaks out of me.
event.story_notes_juno.after: I'll keep writing them. I tried to stop for a week. I cried at a turnip.
event.story_notes_tilda.intro: Ah. Caught. I tuck them in with the change. A kind word weighs nothing.
event.story_notes_tilda.after: I don't mean to be mysterious. It's just that signing them felt like showing off.
event.story_umbrella.intro: Wait. Stop. Is that my umbrella?
event.story_umbrella.after: {if choice:umbrella.return}Back where it belongs. It will be lost again by Thursday.{else}{if choice:umbrella.hang}A landmark. I'll look for it every rain.{else}Shared custody. I accept. Under protest.{/if}{/if}
event.story_scarecrows.intro: [player]! Just in time. You are my judge. Please be fair, which means pick mine.
event.story_scarecrows.after: {if choice:scarecrow.tilda}I won. I'm not smug. I'm radiant.{else}{if choice:scarecrow.dorian}He won. I'll say it once. Never again.{else}{if choice:scarecrow.tie}A tie. I'm not speaking to you, with love.{else}The crows chose. Wisely. They're furious with both of us.{/if}{/if}{/if}
event.story_whistler_bram.intro: {pause=0.5}...Hm. (A cheerful tune stops. Bram turns, very slowly.)
event.story_whistler_bram.after: Hm. That wrong note is my signature. I'll be hearing about it.
event.story_whistler_marcus.intro: (The whistling stops. Marcus puts a plank down, very carefully.) Ah. You've found me.
event.story_whistler_marcus.after: Tradition. A wrong note is only wrong if you apologize for it.
event.story_whistler_felix.intro: (The whistling stops. Felix, holding a fishing line, turns bright red.) Don't tell the fish.
event.story_whistler_felix.after: Between us, the fish like the wrong note. They bite more.
letter.notes_first.subject: A note, unsigned
letter.notes_first.body: Your corn is doing great. Keep going.
dlg.marcus.pie.1.0: I said "ambitious". It was a compliment. She heard what she wanted to hear.
dlg.marcus.pie.2.0: A crust like that deserves an apology. Not from me. In general.
dlg.marcus.pie.after.0: Odalys and I are speaking. Mostly about pastry. It's a start.
dlg.odalys.pie.1.0: Ambitious is what you call a house with no roof. I have thoughts, [player]. Sit.
dlg.odalys.pie.2.0: I'm not angry. I'm composing. There's a difference, and it takes a week.
dlg.odalys.pie.after.0: The pie was acceptable. I've told Marcus nothing. Naturally.
dlg.wren.pie.after.0: The pie feud's over! I paid out the bet. Everyone lost. Except the pie.
dlg.wren.notes.suspect.0: I think the notes are Felix. He signs nothing and smiles at everything.
dlg.wren.notes.dorian.0: Dorian! Of course. The quiet ones write the best notes.
dlg.wren.notes.juno.0: Juno! The notes! I should have guessed. She cheers at tools.
dlg.wren.notes.tilda.0: Tilda, tucking notes in the change. Of course. A saint with receipts.
dlg.wren.scare.1.0: Two scarecrows. One contest. I've got money on the quiet one.
dlg.wren.scare.after.0: The scarecrows are standing side by side now. Still competing. In silence.
dlg.wren.whistle.after.0: I'm humming the whistler's wrong note. Everyone will. It's the village song.
dlg.hazel.notes.suspect.0: I suspect Piper. (The handwriting loops like a person who reads.)
dlg.hazel.notes.after.0: The notes had a writer. (I'm glad. Mysteries are better with a person at the end.)
dlg.bram.notes.suspect.0: Hm. I thought it was me. I write one word. Hm.
dlg.bram.notes.after.0: Hm. The notes had a writer. Good. I'll write one back.
dlg.bram.pie.after.0: Hm. Pie feud's over. I kept the pie plate.
dlg.bram.scare.1.0: Hm. Two scarecrows. Both scare me. Neither scares crows.
dlg.tilda.notes.1.0: Somebody left a note in my till. "Nice shop." I'm suspicious and flattered.
dlg.tilda.scare.1.0: I've entered a scarecrow contest. Mine has a smile. Smiles scare crows.
dlg.tilda.scare.2.0: Judging is on a Saturday. Rest up. Be fair. Pick mine.
dlg.piper.umbrella.1.0: My red umbrella is gone. It's enormous. It cannot simply vanish. And yet.
dlg.piper.umbrella.2.0: If you see a red umbrella, don't touch it. Tell me. Then touch it.
dlg.piper.umbrella.after.0: I found my umbrella thanks to you. It will vanish again. I've made peace with that.
dlg.felix.umbrella.1.0: I returned Piper's umbrella. I remember because it dripped on my best boots.
dlg.felix.umbrella.2.0: A red umbrella went by on the pier. Nobody was holding it. I said nothing.
dlg.elara.umbrella.1.0: An umbrella. If it were mine, I would have named it.
dlg.elara.umbrella.2.0: I never had an umbrella. I'd remember. It's a red one. Someone said.
dlg.elara.umbrella.after.0: I never had that umbrella. I did borrow it once. For research.
dlg.dorian.scare.1.0: Mine is quiet. Quiet is unsettling. I did my research.
dlg.dorian.scare.2.0: The contest is soon. I hung my hat on the scarecrow. For authenticity.
dlg.dorian.scare.after.0: The contest is over. The scarecrows stay. We're both pleased. Silently.
dlg.ione.whistle.1.0: A tune with one wrong note. It lives in my head now. Thank you, whoever you are.
dlg.ione.whistle.2.0: Someone whistles at dusk. I keep checking the clinic windows. Nobody. Only the tune.
dlg.ione.whistle.after.0: Now I know who whistles. The wrong note sounds better. That's how mysteries work.
dlg.juno.whistle.1.0: It sounds like a kettle trying to be a flute. I love it. I'm furious.
dlg.juno.whistle.2.0: Dusk, quarry road, one wrong note. I'd know it anywhere. I don't know who it is.
dlg.bram.whistle.2.0: Hm. A rumor says someone whistles at dusk. Hm. Interesting.
dlg.bram.whistle.after.0: Hm. The village hums my wrong note now. I'm not speaking to it.
dlg.marcus.whistle.1.0: A tune? At dusk? I haven't heard a thing. I hum while I plane. Different matter.
dlg.marcus.whistle.after.0: The village whistles my grandfather's wrong note. He'd be insufferable.
dlg.felix.whistle.1.0: Whistling? Not me. The fish aren't listening. They're just very still.
dlg.felix.whistle.after.0: Now everyone whistles near the pier. The fish are baffled. I'm moved.
dlg.story.pie.talk.0: One slice of my pie. Her door. Don't say who sent it. If she asks, say a stranger with excellent taste.
dlg.story.pie.talk.r0: You carry the slice to Odalys's door. She reads the note, sighs, and takes a bite.
dlg.story.pie.talk.r0b: Ambitious. ...It's rather good. Tell him nothing.
dlg.story.pie.talk.r1: You add a pinch of cinnamon on the way. Odalys takes a bite and frowns for a long time.
dlg.story.pie.talk.r1b: Who touched this? It's better. I hate that.
dlg.story.pie.talk.r2: You eat the slice on the road. It is excellent. You now have two angry customers.
dlg.story.pie.talk.r2b: Marcus owes me an apology. And a pie. And, apparently, you.
dlg.story.notes.dorian.0: You catch Dorian slipping a folded note under a door. Neither of you moves.
dlg.story.notes.dorian.r0: ...You smiled. That's a lot of kindness for one smile.
dlg.story.notes.dorian.r1: Oh. Thank you. That's the whole reward. I'll go and be flustered somewhere.
dlg.story.notes.dorian.r2: A note, for me? ...I'm keeping it. In a drawer I've just invented.
dlg.story.notes.juno.0: You catch Juno slipping a folded note under a door. Neither of you moves.
dlg.story.notes.juno.r0: ...You smiled. That's a lot of kindness for one smile.
dlg.story.notes.juno.r1: Oh. Thank you. That's the whole reward. I'll go and be flustered somewhere.
dlg.story.notes.juno.r2: A note, for me? ...I'm keeping it. In a drawer I've just invented.
dlg.story.notes.tilda.0: You catch Tilda slipping a folded note under a door. Neither of you moves.
dlg.story.notes.tilda.r0: ...You smiled. That's a lot of kindness for one smile.
dlg.story.notes.tilda.r1: Oh. Thank you. That's the whole reward. I'll go and be flustered somewhere.
dlg.story.notes.tilda.r2: A note, for me? ...I'm keeping it. In a drawer I've just invented.
dlg.story.umbrella.talk.0: A large red umbrella hangs from the fence post, dripping with great dignity. Piper stares at it.
dlg.story.umbrella.talk.1: It's red. It's enormous. It cannot simply vanish and reappear, and yet. What do you suggest?
dlg.story.umbrella.talk.r0: Mine. At last. I was starting to take it personally.
dlg.story.umbrella.talk.r1: Leave it? ...A little red landmark. Yes. I like that.
dlg.story.umbrella.talk.r2: You'll keep it? That's theft, with excellent manners.
dlg.story.scarecrow.talk.0: Mine has a smile. Smiles scare crows. That is simply known.
dlg.story.scarecrow.talk.1: Mine is quiet. Quiet is unsettling. I did my research.
dlg.story.scarecrow.talk.2: Well? Which scarecrow rules the fields?
dlg.story.scarecrow.talk.r0: Ha! A person of taste. Take this one home. It's the runner-up. It's still excellent.
dlg.story.scarecrow.talk.r1: ...Oh. Thank you. Take the runner-up. It's very quiet company.
dlg.story.scarecrow.talk.r2: A tie. You coward. Take one anyway. Both of us will be wounded.
dlg.story.scarecrow.talk.r3: The crows? ...Brave. They landed on both. A tie, then. Take this.
dlg.story.whistler.bram.0: Hm. I whistle. Don't. Tell. Anyone.
dlg.story.whistler.bram.r0: Hello. Right. Good. Thank you for the normal approach.
dlg.story.whistler.bram.r1: You... got the wrong note exactly right. I'm moved and mortified.
dlg.story.whistler.bram.r2: You listened. To the whole thing. ...I may whistle again. Quietly.
dlg.story.whistler.marcus.0: It's a family tune. One note went wrong in my grandfather's time and we kept it.
dlg.story.whistler.marcus.r0: Hello. Right. Good. Thank you for the normal approach.
dlg.story.whistler.marcus.r1: You... got the wrong note exactly right. I'm moved and mortified.
dlg.story.whistler.marcus.r2: You listened. To the whole thing. ...I may whistle again. Quietly.
dlg.story.whistler.felix.0: I only whistle when I'm happy. Which is why the fish are always listening.
dlg.story.whistler.felix.r0: Hello. Right. Good. Thank you for the normal approach.
dlg.story.whistler.felix.r1: You... got the wrong note exactly right. I'm moved and mortified.
dlg.story.whistler.felix.r2: You listened. To the whole thing. ...I may whistle again. Quietly.
dlg.story.umbrella.talk.c1: Hang it where it was found.
event.story_band_battle.intro: Two bands, one square, one very polite war. Judge us, [player]. Be honest, and honest means fiddle.
event.story_band_battle.after: {if choice:band.piper}A fiddle wins! Of course. Juno took it well. She's inventing a louder anvil.{else}{if choice:band.juno}The forge band won! I'm thrilled. I'm furious. I'm writing a song about both.{else}A joint set! Fiddle, anvil, one very confused crowd. That's a chorus.{/if}{/if}
event.story_pumpkin_dorian.intro: ...I'll explain. The pumpkin was perfect for a mushroom experiment. I meant to ask. I forgot to ask.
event.story_pumpkin_dorian.after: He's returning it with a mushroom stew inside. Tilda forgives him on the spot. The pumpkin does not.
event.story_pumpkin_marcus.intro: Ah. You've found out. I was carving a practice lantern. A very large practice lantern.
event.story_pumpkin_marcus.after: He's returning it with a face carved in. Tilda says it's an improvement. Marcus will not stop smiling.
event.story_pumpkin_felix.intro: Oh no. Don't tell the fish. I wanted a picture of it next to the biggest carp. For comparison.
event.story_pumpkin_felix.after: He's returning it with a photograph. Tilda frames it. The carp has not forgiven anyone.
event.story_cat.intro: Don't move. A cat has chosen your boots. It won't tell me its name, and I've tried five.
event.story_cat.after: {if choice:cat.ledger}Ledger! Tilda will be insufferable. I'll tell her tonight.{else}{if choice:cat.quench}Quench! Juno will frame the vote. I'll tell her tonight.{else}{if choice:cat.sharp}Sharp! Piper will write a song. I'll tell her tonight.{else}A new name! The village will need a fresh slate. I'll tell everyone tonight.{/if}{/if}{/if}
dlg.piper.band.1.0: Juno started a band. With anvils. I'm not threatened. I'm composing a very long reply.
dlg.piper.band.2.0: A forge band! The rhythm section is a wash bucket. I respect it. I'll still win.
dlg.piper.band.after.0: Juno and I are playing together now. Fiddle on top, anvil underneath. Neither of us admits it was her idea.
dlg.juno.band.1.0: Okay, okay, okay: Piper has a fiddle. I have three anvils and a bucket. Technically that's a bigger band.
dlg.juno.band.2.0: Bram agreed to hit one anvil once. Once! I'm writing the whole song around it.
dlg.juno.band.after.0: The square liked the anvils. Nobody said so. They tapped their feet. I counted.
dlg.wren.band.1.0: Two bands and one square. I'm taking bets and selling earplugs. Both at fair prices.
dlg.wren.band.after.0: I called it a draw and everyone was happy. That's why I do the betting.
dlg.bram.band.1.0: Hm. Juno wants me to hit an anvil. In public. Once.
dlg.bram.band.after.0: Hm. I hit the anvil. The anvil forgave me. The square clapped. Hm.
dlg.tilda.pumpkin.1.0: My prize pumpkin is gone. From the window. In daylight. The goats are being blamed. The goats are innocent.
dlg.tilda.pumpkin.2.0: It weighed forty pounds. Somebody lifted it. I've put every muscle in Wetherell on the slate.
dlg.tilda.pumpkin.after.0: The pumpkin is back. The culprit owes me a pie. I've written it down twice.
dlg.felix.pumpkin.1.0: A missing pumpkin? I've seen nothing. I've been watching fish. Fish don't gossip. Mostly.
dlg.marcus.pumpkin.1.0: Tilda's pumpkin vanished. I was in my workshop all week. Carving. Planing. Innocent things.
dlg.dorian.pumpkin.1.0: A pumpkin. Missing. Interesting. I have no opinion. I have a small secret. Unrelated.
dlg.wren.pumpkin.1.0: The great pumpkin heist! My money's on the goats. Tilda's money's on a person. We've both bet the same pie.
dlg.wren.pumpkin.after.0: The pumpkin turned up! Nobody wins the pot. Tilda keeps it. Naturally.
dlg.tilda.cat.1.0: A gray cat sits in my window each morning. I've named it Ledger. It keeps the sill balanced.
dlg.juno.cat.1.0: Okay, okay, okay: the cat on the forge roof is Quench. It sits on the hottest tile. It's never wrong about heat.
dlg.piper.cat.1.0: The gray cat follows me to the saloon. I call it Sharp. It only likes the high notes.
dlg.hazel.cat.1.0: A gray cat sleeps on the returns box. (I've filed it under Index.) It doesn't mind the system.
dlg.bram.cat.1.0: Hm. A cat sits on the anvil. Warm. Hm. I call it nothing. It's called enough.
dlg.wren.cat.1.0: Everyone has a name for the gray cat. I call it Gossip. It never repeats anything I say. Rude.
dlg.wren.cat.ledger.0: The cat's name is Ledger now. Tilda hasn't stopped glowing. She's written it on the slate.
dlg.wren.cat.quench.0: The cat's name is Quench now. Juno made it a little bowl. The label says "Quench's Bowl".
dlg.wren.cat.sharp.0: The cat's name is Sharp now. Piper wrote it a theme song. It left during the second verse.
dlg.wren.cat.new.0: The cat has a brand-new name. It answers to it. It answers to nothing else. Progress.
dlg.story.band.talk.0: Exhibit A: a fiddle, a voice, a lifetime of practice. Watch.
dlg.story.band.talk.1: Exhibit B: three anvils, a wash bucket and Bram, who has agreed to hit one thing. Once.
dlg.story.band.talk.3: Well? Who owns the square tonight?
dlg.story.band.talk.r0: Ha! Justice and good taste. Bow, everybody.
dlg.story.band.talk.r1: Okay, okay, okay! Did you hear that, Bram? We won. Bram?
dlg.story.band.talk.r2: Together? ...That's either genius or a noise complaint. Let's find out.
dlg.story.pumpkin.dorian.0: You find Dorian behind the store, with a very large pumpkin and a very guilty face.
dlg.story.pumpkin.dorian.1: Is that my prize pumpkin? The one the whole village has been blaming the goats for?
dlg.story.pumpkin.dorian.r0: Kindly? Fine. Kindly. But he's on the slate for a pie.
dlg.story.pumpkin.dorian.r1: An apology. Yes. Very sorry. Truly. Pumpkin, I'm also sorry to you.
dlg.story.pumpkin.dorian.r2: You carry the heavy end. I'll supervise. We'll call it civic duty.
dlg.story.pumpkin.marcus.0: You find Marcus behind the store, with a very large pumpkin and a very guilty face.
dlg.story.pumpkin.marcus.1: Is that my prize pumpkin? The one the whole village has been blaming the goats for?
dlg.story.pumpkin.marcus.r0: Kindly? Fine. Kindly. But he's on the slate for a pie.
dlg.story.pumpkin.marcus.r1: An apology. Yes. Very sorry. Truly. Pumpkin, I'm also sorry to you.
dlg.story.pumpkin.marcus.r2: You carry the heavy end. I'll supervise. We'll call it civic duty.
dlg.story.pumpkin.felix.0: You find Felix behind the store, with a very large pumpkin and a very guilty face.
dlg.story.pumpkin.felix.1: Is that my prize pumpkin? The one the whole village has been blaming the goats for?
dlg.story.pumpkin.felix.r0: Kindly? Fine. Kindly. But he's on the slate for a pie.
dlg.story.pumpkin.felix.r1: An apology. Yes. Very sorry. Truly. Pumpkin, I'm also sorry to you.
dlg.story.pumpkin.felix.r2: You carry the heavy end. I'll supervise. We'll call it civic duty.
dlg.story.cat.talk.0: A small gray cat sits on your boots, perfectly satisfied, and looks up at you with the patience of a landlord.
dlg.story.cat.talk.1: Tilda calls it Ledger. Juno says Quench. Piper swears it's Sharp. Hazel files it under Index. I say Gossip. The cat answers to none of us.
dlg.story.cat.talk.2: So. What do you call it?
dlg.story.cat.talk.r0: Tilda's name. Careful. She keeps a very long slate.
dlg.story.cat.talk.r1: Juno's name. Brave. She'll label the cat's bowl.
dlg.story.cat.talk.r2: Piper's name. A fiddler's cat. It suits the whiskers.
dlg.story.cat.talk.r3: Something new! The cat tilts its head. ...It just purred. That's the one.
dlg.story.pumpkin.dorian.c2: Offer to help carry it back.
dlg.story.pumpkin.marcus.c2: Offer to help carry it back.
dlg.story.pumpkin.felix.c2: Offer to help carry it back.
dlg.juno.spring.1.0: Okay, okay, okay: spring means hinges. Every gate in Wetherell decided to fall off in the same week!
dlg.juno.spring.2.0: Plow blades, hoe heads, a bucket with a hole I labeled "Bucket (Hole)". It's been a very busy thaw.
dlg.juno.spring.3.0: The first warm day, Bram opened the forge door and said "Hm." That's the longest spring speech I've ever heard.
dlg.juno.spring.4.0: New iron smells like rain in a drawer. I know that's not a smell. It is, though!
dlg.juno.spring.5.0: My birthday's in spring. I'm not saying a word. I've labeled the date in the calendar. In red. Twice.
dlg.juno.spring.6.0: Every spring I forge one thing I don't sell. This year it's a tiny, perfect spoon. Don't ask.
dlg.juno.summer.1.0: The forge in summer is a sauna with opinions. I've stopped wearing sleeves. Bram's pretending not to see.
dlg.juno.summer.2.0: I keep a bucket of water by the door. Wren called it "the swimming pool". I put a sign on it. It says so.
dlg.juno.summer.3.0: Long evenings, short tempers, perfect weather for a clasp. I've made forty. I regret none!
dlg.juno.summer.4.0: Piper and I swam off the beach after closing. She sang. I hammered. The fish left.
dlg.juno.summer.5.0: Sunburn on one arm only, from the forge door. I look like a half-cooked loaf. A proud one.
dlg.juno.summer.6.0: The summer festival's coming, and I've entered a medal in the "made by hand" table. It's mostly polish. And nerves.
dlg.juno.fall.1.0: Fall: scythes, axes and a small flood of gift commissions. Everyone suddenly loves someone with a belt buckle.
dlg.juno.fall.2.0: The forge is the best seat in the village now. Bram says it isn't. Bram sits in it daily.
dlg.juno.fall.3.0: I labeled the leaves on the forge roof. "Leaf (Hissing)". They hiss when they land. I'm delighted.
dlg.juno.fall.4.0: Bram's birthday's in fall. He thinks nobody knows. I've made a card. It's mostly diagrams.
dlg.juno.fall.5.0: Cold mornings make iron feel honest. You can hear every dent. I love it. I also love tea.
dlg.juno.fall.6.0: Harvest week, I walk to the beach and talk to the tide about metal. It nods. Sort of.
dlg.juno.winter.1.0: Winter at the forge: the warmest room in Wetherell. Half the village comes in to "ask about nails".
dlg.juno.winter.2.0: Snow on the roof, sparks in the air, tea in a tin cup. I could weep. I might. It's soot.
dlg.juno.winter.3.0: Winter evenings, Bram tells me one thing about his old teacher. One thing. I've been counting. I've got eleven.
dlg.juno.winter.4.0: Frost on the anvil! It melts in a heartbeat. I labeled it "Anvil (Sulking)".
dlg.juno.winter.5.0: Long nights are good for filing. And for thinking about what to make that's never been made.
dlg.juno.winter.6.0: Last winter I made a snowflake in copper. It melted nothing and impressed everyone. Bram nodded. Nodded!
dlg.juno.mon.1.0: Monday. Bram and I are shut, and I still came in. I'm only here to label things. It's a hobby.
dlg.juno.mon.2.0: It's our day off. I spent it sharpening spoons for fun. Don't judge.
dlg.juno.tue.1.0: Tuesday. Wren's saloon is shut, so everyone's at the forge, warming up and asking questions.
dlg.juno.tue.2.0: Slow Tuesday, good for fine work. Tiny hinges, tiny hooks, tiny sighs.
dlg.juno.wed.1.0: Wednesday. Marcus is closed, so Bram's gone to sit on a bench. In silence. With him. It's adorable.
dlg.juno.wed.2.0: Midweek, which means orders. Orders mean noise. Noise means I'm happy.
dlg.juno.thu.1.0: Thursday. Felix is out of hooks, so I'm making some. Between us, they're lovelier than his.
dlg.juno.thu.2.0: Thursdays I sharpen everything, including the bucket. Bram's looking at me. I'm sharpening the bucket.
dlg.juno.fri.1.0: Friday! Everyone needs their tool done by Saturday. I've labeled the pile "Panic (Polite)".
dlg.juno.fri.2.0: Friday. Orders, noise and Wren's gossip floating in through the door like a very nosy breeze.
dlg.juno.sat.1.0: Saturday, market day. I'm selling clasps in the square, and Bram's in the forge saying "Hm" to a kettle.
dlg.juno.sat.2.0: Saturday afternoon, my favorite hour: the forge cools, the square's loud, and nobody needs me.
dlg.juno.sun.1.0: Sunday. I'm fixing things nobody asked me to fix. It's like Bram, but louder.
dlg.juno.sun.2.0: A quiet Sunday, and a very small anvil, and a very big idea I'm not telling you.
dlg.juno.sunny.1.0: Perfect weather. The forge is a furnace, the street is a postcard, and I'm a sweaty, grinning idiot.
dlg.juno.sunny.2.0: Sun on the anvil, sun on the roof, sun on my nose. I'm freckled in three places. New record.
dlg.juno.sunny.3.0: Bright day. I opened both doors. Bram closed one. We're negotiating.
dlg.juno.rain.2.0: Rain on the roof of the forge: the best sound in the world, and I'll fight anyone who says the sea.
dlg.juno.rain.3.0: Everybody brought in their tools to dry. Bram's running a laundry. I've labeled the line "Damp (Dignified)".
dlg.juno.rain.4.0: Rain makes the hot iron hiss like a cat that's been insulted. I love that cat. I'm that cat.
dlg.juno.storm.1.0: Thunder! The anvil rings back. They're old friends. I think they're arguing.
dlg.juno.storm.2.0: Storm night, and I'm filing a clasp by lantern light. It's romantic, if you squint and love clasps.
dlg.juno.storm.3.0: Lightning's loud. The forge is louder. I told the sky it can try harder.
dlg.juno.snow.1.0: Snow on the sill, glow in the forge. It looks like a postcard with a very hot secret.
dlg.juno.snow.2.0: Everything's muffled. Even my hammer. It feels like working inside a very large pillow.
dlg.juno.snow.3.0: Snow day. Bram opened the door a crack so we could watch it fall. He didn't say why. I knew.
dlg.juno.wind.1.0: Windy, so the door's arguing with the draft. The draft's winning. I've labeled it "Rude".
dlg.juno.wind.2.0: The ash is going everywhere. I'm gray to the elbows. I look like a very tired ghost.
dlg.juno.wind.3.0: Blustery day. The forge roars, the roof rattles, and I've lost my hat. Again. It's a pattern.
dlg.juno.morning.1.0: Early! The fire's still sleepy. I'm coaxing it. Don't talk too loud. It startles.
dlg.juno.morning.2.0: First heat of the day, first good idea. I wrote the idea on my glove. It's already smudged.
dlg.juno.morning.3.0: Before the shop opens it's just me, the iron and a very philosophical kettle.
dlg.juno.midday.1.0: Midday! Peak heat, peak noise, peak "Hm" from Bram. I've never been happier or sweatier.
dlg.juno.midday.2.0: Busy. Don't stand in the sparks. They have terrible manners.
dlg.juno.midday.3.0: Afternoon's when the best iron gets made. I have no proof. It's just a feeling in my elbows.
dlg.juno.evening.1.0: Closing soon. The fire's low, the floor's a disaster, and I'm still making one more clasp.
dlg.juno.evening.2.0: Evening. I sweep, Bram sits, and the forge hums like a sleepy cat. It's my favorite part.
dlg.juno.evening.3.0: Last job of the day is always the hard one. It's like the universe is checking my attendance.
dlg.juno.late.1.0: Late! The anvil's still warm, and so am I. I'm not working. I'm "letting the metal talk".
dlg.juno.late.2.0: Past closing. I should sleep. The iron says otherwise. The iron's a terrible roommate.
dlg.juno.late.3.0: Quiet hours at the forge. Best hours. That's when I try the thing I haven't made yet.
dlg.juno.here.1.0: Don't touch the one labeled "Hot". Or the one labeled "Hotter". Or the one labeled "Hm".
dlg.juno.here.2.0: Every tool has a label. Some of them are insults. Bram's chair says "Do Not". He sits anyway.
dlg.juno.here.3.0: Careful, the floor has opinions. I've labeled the opinionated tile "Mister Trip".
dlg.juno.fr.1.0: Oh! You came! Okay, okay, okay, look at this clasp. It closes. First try. Don't tell Bram I cried.
dlg.juno.fr.2.0: You ask good questions. Bram never asks. He nods, and the nod has footnotes.
dlg.juno.fr.3.0: I've labeled your spot at the forge "Guest (Welcome)". Bram crossed out the "Guest". I haven't asked why.
dlg.juno.fr.4.0: Piper says I talk to you more than I talk to the anvil. I told her that was not a comparison.
dlg.juno.fr.5.0: Look at this hinge! I made it with my own hands, a lot of tears and a little spite.
dlg.juno.fr.6.0: Tilda put a clasp on the slate in your name. That's how you know you've arrived.
dlg.juno.fr.7.0: You listen to me talk about metal. Nobody listens. You take notes with your face.
dlg.juno.fr.8.0: Come by tomorrow? I might have a surprise. Or a spoon. Possibly both.
dlg.juno.cl.1.0: I was thinking about leaving Wetherell once. Then you walked in with a muddy hat and asked about hinges. So.
dlg.juno.cl.2.0: Bram's proud of me. He's never said it. I can tell by how loudly he doesn't say it.
dlg.juno.cl.3.0: You're the first person I've shown my sketches to. They're mostly doodles of clasps. And you.
dlg.juno.cl.4.0: The forge feels warmer when you're in it. Bram says it's the fire. Bram is wrong, politely.
dlg.juno.cl.5.0: I told Wren you're my favorite customer. Now the whole village knows. Wren has been told. Wren has been told.
dlg.juno.cl.6.0: Okay, okay, okay, I made you something. It's not finished. It might never be. It's the best thing I've ever not finished.
dlg.juno.cl.7.0: You make me braver. I'm still terrified. But a bit more upright.
dlg.juno.cl.8.0: Your tools are the best looked-after in the valley. Bram says so too, and he never says anything.
dlg.juno.co.1.0: You're the reason I stayed in Wetherell. I should've said it years ago. Okay. I've said it. Stop looking at me.
dlg.juno.co.2.0: I've made a lot of clasps. The one I'm proudest of is the one I haven't made yet. It's for you.
dlg.juno.co.3.0: The forge is the warmest room in the world, and you've made it warmer. That's not a metaphor. I measured.
dlg.juno.co.4.0: If I wrote you a letter it would be forty pages and have footnotes on soot. I'd send it, though.
dlg.juno.co.5.0: I used to dream of leaving. Now I dream of the next order, and you walking in.
dlg.juno.co.6.0: Thank you, [player]. For everything. That's the whole speech. I practiced it for an hour. It was longer.
dlg.juno.co.7.0: I labeled you something. It's on the back of the anvil. You can look. It says "Home."
dlg.juno.co.8.0: Anything I make next, you'll have been there for it. That's the real signature on every piece.
dlg.juno.lonely.1.0: Quiet in the forge. I talk to the anvil. The anvil hasn't answered. It's rude, but consistent.
dlg.juno.lonely.2.0: You were gone a while. I made a clasp for each day. It's a very large pile.
dlg.juno.tired.1.0: Long day. My arms are noodles. Hot noodles. With opinions.
dlg.juno.tired.2.0: A bit tired. Don't tell Bram. He'll say "Hm," and it'll be worse.
dlg.juno.delighted.1.0: Best day ever! I made a clasp that closes with a click. A click! I've named it "Click".
dlg.juno.delighted.2.0: Everything worked. Everything. Even the bucket, which I'd given up on. Today is a good day!
dlg.juno.mischief.1.0: I put a rubber chicken on Bram's anvil. Wren swore it was an accident. It was not an accident.
dlg.juno.mischief.2.0: I labeled the kettle "Bram's Best Friend". It's been staring at him all morning.
dlg.juno.worried.1.0: I'm worried about the piece I'm working on. I labeled it "Don't Look." Now I can't stop.
dlg.juno.farm.1.0: Your field's coming along! Your hoe will need me soon. They always do. It's the law.
dlg.juno.farm.2.0: So many plants! So many tools to break. I'm thrilled. Bram's quietly counting the orders.
dlg.juno.farm.3.0: Animals! You'll need fence hooks and a very good bucket. I know where to find both.
dlg.juno.farm.4.0: A cow on your farm, and a bell on the cow? I'll make you a bell. A good one.
dlg.juno.fest.1.0: Festival soon! I've polished a medal and my nerves. Both shine. Neither is for sale.
dlg.juno.fest.2.0: Festival week. Bram's coming. Bram! In a clean shirt! I've told nobody. I'm vibrating.
dlg.juno.fest.3.0: Festival day! The forge is shut, the square's loud, and I'm eating three things at once. Come find me!
dlg.juno.bday.1.0: My birthday's close. I'm not hinting. I put a sign on the anvil. It says "Hint."
dlg.juno.bday.2.0: Three days to go. Don't tell Bram. He knows. He's pretended not to for years. I love it.
dlg.juno.bday.3.0: It's today! Somebody told. I know who. Everyone. Everyone told. I'm very warm.
dlg.juno.bday.4.0: Bram's birthday! I made him a tool. He'll say "Hm." I'll cry. It's tradition.
dlg.juno.bday.5.0: Piper's birthday! I'm making her a fiddle bow clip. She'll haggle with me about the shine. Of course she will.
dlg.juno.rare.1.0: Technically it's art. Technically it's also a doorstop. The two are not in conflict.
dlg.juno.rare.2.0: I once labeled a puddle "Puddle (Ambitious)". It got deeper out of pride.
dlg.juno.rare.3.0: The first thing Bram ever taught me was patience. The second was where the good tea is hidden.
dlg.juno.rare.4.0: Don't tell Bram. (She lifts a tiny gold spoon.) I made this, with no help. Look at the mark. It's yours now.
A gold bar! Oh, oh, oh. Too soft for work, too pretty to ignore. I'm framing it. Don't tell Bram.
dlg.npc.juno.gift.item.forage.truffle.0: A truffle! Bram loves these. I love these. We're both going to pretend I found it.
dlg.npc.juno.gift.item.crop.pepper.0: A pepper! Hot like the forge, and twice as sensible. I'll eat it at the anvil and cry happily.
dlg.npc.juno.gift.item.resource.copperba: Copper! Clean and warm. I'll make you something with it. Don't ask what. I don't know yet.
dlg.npc.juno.gift.item.crop.potato.0: A potato. Honest and round. It'll go on the anvil for luck, and then in my lunch.
dlg.npc.juno.gift.item.resource.coal.0: Coal! For the forge. A very practical present. I'm a little moved. It's the soot.
dlg.npc.juno.gift.item.crop.kale.0: Kale. Hm, as Bram says. I'll give it to the cat. The cat will give it to the floor.
A dandelion. I'm making a wish and I'm not telling. It's about spoons.
dlg.npc.juno.gift.item.crop.cucumber.0: A cucumber. Cold and green and far from the forge. I'll put it in the bucket. It's been very brave.
dlg.npc.juno.gift.cat.Fish.0: A fish! Felix's department. I'll walk it over, and take a long, tragic look at the sea on the way.
Iron! Bram's favorite, so mine too. I'll make a hinge so good the door will blush.
dlg.npc.juno.gift.item.resource.stone.0: A rock! A really good one. I've labeled it "Rock (Excellent)". It goes on the windowsill.
dlg.npc.juno.gift.item.resource.wood.0: Wood! For the fire. Marcus would weep. Bram would nod. I'll do a bit of both.
dlg.npc.juno.gift.item.resource.bone.0: A bone. I'll make it a handle. Or a very small, serious flute. I haven't decided.
dlg.npc.juno.gift.item.resource.slime.0: Slime. It's looking at me. ...I'll label it "Do Not Touch" and apologize to it later.
dlg.npc.juno.gift.item.product.egg.0: An egg! Fragile and optimistic. I'll look after it. Probably.
dlg.npc.juno.gift.item.artisan.wine.0: Wine! For the forge's anniversary. I'll share it with Bram. He'll say "Hm" and mean it.
dlg.npc.juno.gift.item.crop.pumpkin.0: A pumpkin! I'll carve a hammer on it. A very large, very orange hammer.
dlg.npc.juno.gift.item.food.salad.0: Salad! A respectable lunch. I'll eat it standing up, near the anvil, quickly, like a professional.
dlg.npc.juno.gift.item.artisan.jam.0: Jam! Sticky, sweet and perfect on bread. I'll hide it from Bram. He'll find it. He always does.
dlg.npc.juno.gift.repeat.0: Another one! You're spoiling me. I've labeled the first one "Precious" and the second "Also Precious."
dlg.piper.spring.1.0: New season, new songs. Most of them are about parsnips. The rest are about what rhymes with parsnip.
dlg.piper.spring.2.0: Spring in the saloon: the windows are open, the fiddle is in tune, and the mud sings along.
dlg.piper.spring.3.0: I wrote a spring anthem. It's four lines and a hiccup. The hiccup is the chorus.
dlg.piper.spring.4.0: The first warm night, everyone sings. Badly. Beautifully. In the same key, occasionally.
dlg.piper.spring.5.0: My birthday's in spring. I'm not hinting. I'm humming. It's the song of someone hinting.
dlg.piper.spring.6.0: Every spring I retune the fiddle by the beach. The waves keep time. They have no sense of tempo.
dlg.piper.summer.1.0: Summer sets on the beach. Sand in the strings, salt in the song. It's rustic. It's also itchy.
dlg.piper.summer.2.0: The saloon's hot, so I play outside the door and charge nobody. The crowd pays in applause and lemonade.
dlg.piper.summer.3.0: A gull joined my song at the beach. It was flat. I've never been so insulted by a bird.
dlg.piper.summer.4.0: Long evenings, long notes. The sun sets, and I'm still on the second verse.
dlg.piper.summer.5.0: Juno and I swam after dark. She hammered the surf. I fiddled. The tide applauded in a very damp way.
dlg.piper.summer.6.0: At the summer festival I'll play something new. It's half written. The other half is panic.
dlg.piper.fall.1.0: Harvest dances! Everyone's feet are louder than my fiddle. I've never been happier to lose.
dlg.piper.fall.2.0: Fall is the season of ballads. Somebody always cries. I plan it. It's professional.
dlg.piper.fall.3.0: Everyone's making pies, so every song is about pie. I rhymed "crust" with "trust". It almost works.
dlg.piper.fall.4.0: The nights are cooler. The fiddle's tighter. The crowd is warmer. All in tune.
dlg.piper.fall.5.0: Wren's birthday's in fall. I'm writing her a song. It rhymes "cider" with "wider". She'll hate it.
dlg.piper.fall.6.0: Harvest week, I play for the empty fields. They never request anything. It's very restful.
dlg.piper.winter.1.0: Winter sets by the stove: wool socks, long ballads, a very tired bow.
dlg.piper.winter.2.0: The snow's soft and so is the music. Everyone sits closer. It's the best acoustic in the world.
dlg.piper.winter.3.0: A winter crowd sings quietly. That's the crowd I'd keep, if I could keep one.
dlg.piper.winter.4.0: Cold fingers on strings: a very small, very dramatic suffering. I've written it a song.
dlg.piper.winter.5.0: The saloon's a lantern in the snow. Everyone drifts toward it, and I get to be the glow.
dlg.piper.winter.6.0: Last winter I played one song, three times, slower each time. The crowd stayed. Nobody left.
dlg.piper.mon.1.0: Monday. The week begins with a minor chord and a slight sigh. It's my favorite key.
dlg.piper.mon.2.0: Mondays are for rehearsing songs I'll play on Friday. Most never make it. They're just good practice.
dlg.piper.tue.1.0: Tuesday. The saloon's shut, so I'm on the beach with a fiddle and an audience of crabs.
dlg.piper.tue.2.0: Tuesday is my day off and Wren's. We spend it apart, and then compare notes. Actual notes.
dlg.piper.wed.1.0: Wednesday. Midweek, mid-song, mid-nap. The three are not mutually exclusive.
dlg.piper.wed.2.0: Nothing happens on Wednesdays. I wrote a song about it. Nothing happens in it either.
dlg.piper.thu.1.0: Thursday. Felix's day off, so the beach is crowded with fishing hats and bad advice.
dlg.piper.thu.2.0: Thursday afternoons I tune the fiddle in the square. A dog sings along. It's a baritone.
dlg.piper.fri.1.0: Friday! The saloon's full, the strings are warm, and everybody wants "the one about the cow".
dlg.piper.fri.2.0: Friday night is my favorite. Every request is a challenge, and every challenge ends in a sing-along.
dlg.piper.sat.1.0: Saturday. Market day. I'm busking by the stalls. Folks pay in apples and approval.
dlg.piper.sat.2.0: Saturday night is the big one. I tune for an hour. Then I play something else entirely.
dlg.piper.sun.1.0: Sunday. I don't play. My fingers beg. My ears do too. It's a beautiful stalemate.
dlg.piper.sun.2.0: Sunday's for listening. I hum under my breath so I don't forget how.
dlg.piper.sunny.1.0: Sunny day, sunny key. Even the minor chords are wearing hats.
dlg.piper.sunny.2.0: The whole village is humming. I didn't plan it. I'm a little jealous.
dlg.piper.sunny.3.0: Bright morning, loud birds. They're warming up for the evening set. Competition's fierce.
dlg.piper.rain.2.0: Rain on the roof: percussion with a very strong opinion. I play along. It leads.
dlg.piper.rain.3.0: A wet day brings everyone in, and everyone sings. A rainy-day crowd is a choir with umbrellas.
dlg.piper.rain.4.0: The drip off the eaves is a perfect triplet. I'm writing it down before it changes its mind.
dlg.piper.storm.1.0: Thunder! A drum solo from the sky. I'll play the bridge. It can have the chorus.
dlg.piper.storm.2.0: A storm in the saloon, a storm outside, and a fiddle between. Dramatic. A bit loud. Wonderful.
dlg.piper.storm.3.0: Lightning's got no sense of timing. I admire it, and I'd never hire it.
dlg.piper.snow.1.0: Snow! The whole world has been muted by a kind percussionist.
dlg.piper.snow.2.0: Snow on the strings makes the notes shy. I play them anyway. They come out polite.
dlg.piper.snow.3.0: Snowfall's the quietest song there is. I won't try to compete. I'll just hum along.
dlg.piper.wind.1.0: Windy night: the fiddle wants to fly, and so does my hat. We're negotiating.
dlg.piper.wind.2.0: The wind's playing the chimney like an organ. It's flat. It's got confidence, though.
dlg.piper.wind.3.0: Blustery day. Every door whistles, and none of them know the tune.
dlg.piper.morning.1.0: Early. My fingers are still asleep. They'll wake up around the third cup of tea.
dlg.piper.morning.2.0: Morning on the beach: the tide for a metronome, and the gulls for a heckling section.
dlg.piper.morning.3.0: I like mornings, but only for composing. Anything else is a rumor.
dlg.piper.midday.1.0: Afternoon rehearsal. The fiddle's warm, the stage is empty, and the audience is a stool.
dlg.piper.midday.2.0: Daytime Piper writes. Nighttime Piper plays. They never meet. They send each other notes.
dlg.piper.midday.3.0: A quiet afternoon. Good for strings, bad for nerves. Come sit and be my metronome.
dlg.piper.evening.1.0: Nearly showtime. I tune, I breathe, I tell the fiddle it's gorgeous. It needs reassurance.
dlg.piper.evening.2.0: Evening! The saloon's filling up, and so's my head. Requests are rolling in like thunder.
dlg.piper.evening.3.0: The crowd arrives in waves. The first wave is polite. The third wave knows the words.
dlg.piper.late.1.0: Late set. The room's warm, the strings are loose, and everyone sings the second verse wrong. Perfect.
dlg.piper.late.2.0: Past midnight. The fiddle's tired, so am I, and the encore is already in motion.
dlg.piper.late.3.0: The best songs come after closing. That's when it's just me and the echo, and the echo's better than the crowd.
dlg.piper.here.1.0: Request anything. I'll probably play something else. It'll be better. Probably.
dlg.piper.here.2.0: Tip jar's on the left. It says "For the fiddle." Wren added "And for Wren." Wren was not asked.
dlg.piper.here.3.0: Sit anywhere. The stool by the stove is Wren's. The one by the stage is mine. The rest are chaos.
dlg.piper.fr.1.0: Front row again! You're my favorite regular. I named a chord after you. It's mostly a hum.
dlg.piper.fr.2.0: You said "farm", I heard "charm". It rhymes if you squint. That's a chorus.
dlg.piper.fr.3.0: Juno says I talk too fast. I said that was a compliment. She said it was a tempo.
dlg.piper.fr.4.0: Sing along tonight. Don't be shy. I'll cover you with a loud note and pretend it was me.
dlg.piper.fr.5.0: I wrote you a verse. It's terrible. It's yours. I'll play it once and then burn it.
dlg.piper.fr.6.0: Wren says you stay for the second set. Wren's right. She's usually right about things that make me blush.
dlg.piper.fr.7.0: Someone in the room who actually listens: it changes the way I play. I'd hate to lose that.
dlg.piper.fr.8.0: Come by after the set. I'll show you the third verse. It's not ready. Neither am I.
dlg.piper.cl.1.0: You make the silence between songs easier. I used to fill it. Now I just let it breathe.
dlg.piper.cl.2.0: Playing for you is my favorite thing, and the second is playing when you're there and I forget to.
dlg.piper.cl.3.0: I have a notebook of songs nobody's heard. You're in half of them. Don't look. I'll blush.
dlg.piper.cl.4.0: Juno says you're good for me. She said it between a hammer and a hinge. That's a sincere location.
dlg.piper.cl.5.0: I told Tilda I'd pay my tab in verses. She wrote it down. I'm now four sonnets in debt.
dlg.piper.cl.6.0: A song I've written is half-finished. I'm waiting for you to hear the rest. Take your time. I'll hum.
dlg.piper.cl.7.0: You never request anything. You ask what I'd like to play. Nobody does that. I played it twice.
dlg.piper.cl.8.0: [farm] sounds like a major key. I don't know why. I just hear it. A bit of sun and a little banjo.
dlg.piper.co.1.0: Wetherell needed a song. You were the chorus. I'm only the one holding the fiddle.
dlg.piper.co.2.0: I used to play so the room wouldn't be quiet. Now I play so you'll hear it. It's a better reason.
dlg.piper.co.3.0: The best song I ever wrote is the one I haven't. It's about someone who showed up. You can guess.
dlg.piper.co.4.0: If I wrote you a letter, it'd rhyme badly and run long. I'd send it with a tune. The tune would be flat.
dlg.piper.co.5.0: I used to fear the quiet. Now it sounds like the moment before you walk in.
dlg.piper.co.6.0: Thank you, [player]. For everything. That's the whole verse. It doesn't rhyme. I left it that way.
dlg.piper.co.7.0: I labeled a drawer in my head "Songs for later." Yours is at the top, and it's already playing.
dlg.piper.co.8.0: Anything I write next, you'll be the first to hear. And the first to hum along, badly, on purpose.
dlg.piper.lonely.1.0: Quiet week. I've been playing for the walls. They don't request anything. They don't clap, either.
dlg.piper.lonely.2.0: You were gone a while. I wrote a song every night. Most are sad. One is about soup.
dlg.piper.tired.1.0: Long set last night. My fingers are noodles and my voice is a rumor.
dlg.piper.tired.2.0: A bit worn today. The fiddle's fine. I'm the one out of tune.
dlg.piper.delighted.1.0: Best night of my life! Everyone knew the chorus. Even the stool. It's a legend now.
dlg.piper.delighted.2.0: I wrote a verse that rhymes! Actually rhymes! No squinting required. I'm basking.
dlg.piper.mischief.1.0: I changed the lyrics to "Barley Bells". Now it's about Wren. She hasn't noticed. She will.
dlg.piper.mischief.2.0: I told the crowd the next song was a secret. It's "Happy Birthday". It's nobody's birthday. Watch their faces.
dlg.piper.worried.1.0: I'm working on a new song, and it's terrible. I'm certain. I'm also certain I'll play it.
dlg.piper.farm.1.0: Your crops are coming in, and I've got a harvest song half-written. Needs more beets.
dlg.piper.farm.2.0: So many vegetables! I rhymed "turnip" with "return it". It's a masterpiece and a refund policy.
dlg.piper.farm.3.0: Animals on the farm: that's an audience! I'll bring the fiddle. The cow will request something sad.
dlg.piper.farm.4.0: A chicken's the most honest critic. It never claps and it never lies.
dlg.piper.fest.1.0: Festival soon! I'm rehearsing a set. It's mostly nerves with a tune on top.
dlg.piper.fest.2.0: Festival week. The whole village sings. I've never heard a room so in love with being out of tune.
dlg.piper.fest.3.0: Festival day! I'm playing till they carry me off. Come hear the new song. It's about all of you.
dlg.piper.bday.1.0: My birthday's close. I'm not hinting. I'm humming "Happy Birthday" in the key of Hint.
dlg.piper.bday.2.0: Three days to go. I'll be a year older and, I swear, exactly as flat.
dlg.piper.bday.3.0: It's today! Somebody told. Wren told. Everyone's singing. Badly. I'd like this on a record.
dlg.piper.bday.4.0: Wren's birthday! I wrote her a song. It rhymes "cider" with "wider". She'll hate it so much she'll frame it.
dlg.piper.bday.5.0: Juno's birthday! I'm giving her a tune on the fiddle and a clip for her bow. She'll say it's the wrong shape.
dlg.piper.rare.1.0: Three kinds of people: those who dog-ear, those who don't, and me, tuning a fiddle that's already in tune.
dlg.piper.rare.2.0: I once played a request for forty minutes because I forgot how to stop. They called it an encore.
dlg.piper.rare.3.0: The first time the whole saloon sang a song I'd written, I stopped playing to hear them. It's the only time I've been quiet on purpose.
dlg.piper.rare.4.0: Listen. (She plays four slow notes.) That's yours. It doesn't have a name yet. I'm waiting for you to hum the ending.
dlg.npc.piper.gift.item.crop.sunflower.0: A sunflower! A stage light you can eat. It goes by the fiddle case. I'll play it a song.
dlg.npc.piper.gift.item.artisan.jam.0: Jam! Sticky, sweet and the best snack for tuning. I'll write you a verse. It won't rhyme. It'll be sincere.
dlg.npc.piper.gift.item.artisan.juice.0: Juice! For the throat, for the soul, and for the second set. I'll sing you a very fruity ballad.
Strawberries! Red, round and ready for a duet. I'll share one with the fiddle. It's a good listener.
dlg.npc.piper.gift.item.forage.raspberry: Raspberries! Tiny and tart. Like a good high note. I'll eat them on stage and look dramatic.
dlg.npc.piper.gift.item.crop.corn.0: Corn! A tune you can husk. I'll hum "Barley Bells" at it and see if it blushes.
dlg.npc.piper.gift.item.resource.coal.0: Coal. Hm. A very sooty note. I'll keep it near the fiddle, as a warning.
dlg.npc.piper.gift.item.resource.slime.0: Slime! It's staring at me. I'll dedicate the next song to it. It won't applaud.
dlg.npc.piper.gift.item.resource.bat_win: A bat wing. I'll make a very small, very dramatic fan out of it. For the opera nobody asked for.
dlg.npc.piper.gift.cat.Fish.0: A fish! I'll play it a lullaby, and then Felix gets it. It seems to be listening. A stoic.
dlg.npc.piper.gift.item.resource.goldbar: A gold bar! The most expensive tambourine in the history of Wetherell. I'll keep it on the stage. For luck.
dlg.npc.piper.gift.item.resource.copperb: Copper! Juno will make me a fiddle clip from it. She'll say it's rustic. I'll call it vintage.
dlg.npc.piper.gift.item.resource.stone.0: A rock! The only percussion that never misses a beat. I'll tap it during the bridge.
dlg.npc.piper.gift.item.resource.wood.0: Wood! A fiddle's cousin, and a stage's best friend. Marcus will say it's too good for me. Marcus is right.
dlg.npc.piper.gift.item.resource.bone.0: A bone. I'll make a whistle from it. A creepy one. For a song that needs a graveyard.
dlg.npc.piper.gift.item.product.egg.0: An egg! Breakfast, percussion and a tiny maraca, all in one. I'll shake it near the cat.
dlg.npc.piper.gift.item.artisan.wine.0: Wine! For after the set, with Wren, who'll tell me I played the third verse wrong. She's lying. Probably.
dlg.npc.piper.gift.item.crop.pumpkin.0: A pumpkin! A drum. A very round, very orange drum. I'm already tapping it.
dlg.npc.piper.gift.item.crop.kale.0: Kale. Hm. A leafy note. I'll play it a ballad and give it to the goat.
dlg.npc.piper.gift.item.crop.potato.0: A potato. A humble note, a sturdy rhythm. I'll hum something low and put it in my pocket.
dlg.npc.piper.gift.item.food.salad.0: Salad! A leafy chorus. I'll eat it between sets, like a very green interval.
dlg.npc.piper.gift.repeat.0: Another one? You're a generous audience. I'll play you a thank-you in the key of "Oh, you shouldn't."
dlg.tilda.spring.1.0: Seed season. Everyone wants everything on the same morning. I love it.
dlg.tilda.spring.2.0: First warm day, the whole village shows up with the same question. "Is it too early?" It never is.
dlg.tilda.spring.3.0: Spring sale: every parsnip seed comes with advice. The advice is free. The parsnips are extra.
dlg.tilda.spring.4.0: The window's full of seed packets. I arranged them by color. Then by hope. It looked better.
dlg.tilda.spring.5.0: Mud on the doormat already. Good sign. Mud means customers.
dlg.tilda.spring.6.0: Spring cleaning. I found a coin from eleven years ago. I put it on the slate, under "Luck".
dlg.tilda.summer.1.0: The awning's up. The bell sounds better in the shade. I've tested it.
dlg.tilda.summer.2.0: Hot week. I keep a pitcher of water by the door. Nobody pays. Everyone returns.
dlg.tilda.summer.3.0: Summer is when the sunflower seeds go. They don't last. They never do.
dlg.tilda.summer.4.0: A customer asked for "something cool." I sold them the cellar. They stayed an hour.
dlg.tilda.summer.5.0: The days are long. I leave the door open. The street comes in on its own.
dlg.tilda.summer.6.0: The beach on Sunday, the saloon after. A shopkeeper needs one afternoon a week to be nobody's problem.
dlg.tilda.fall.1.0: Pie week. The whole village smells like cinnamon and quiet rivalry.
dlg.tilda.fall.2.0: Pumpkins in the window. Prize ones. I give them names, and then I don't sell them.
dlg.tilda.fall.3.0: The nights are cooler. Folks buy wool and chat for an hour longer.
dlg.tilda.fall.4.0: Everyone says their pie is the best. I eat all of them. I'm the only honest judge in town, and I'm also biased.
dlg.tilda.fall.5.0: Fall is when I count the year. Not the money. The kindnesses.
dlg.tilda.fall.6.0: Harvest week, I take the slate down and read it from the top. It's a good book.
dlg.tilda.winter.1.0: Winter hours are the same, but the shop is warmer than the street. People notice.
dlg.tilda.winter.2.0: The stove's on. The kettle's on. I'm not selling tea. I'm just not stopping anyone.
dlg.tilda.winter.3.0: I keep the lamp on late in winter. Somebody always needs a reason to leave the house.
dlg.tilda.winter.4.0: Stock is low, spirits are high. That's my favorite arithmetic.
dlg.tilda.winter.5.0: Snow on the sign. I leave it. It reads better that way.
dlg.tilda.winter.6.0: Winter evenings, I read upstairs, and the shop hums below me. It sounds like company.
dlg.tilda.mon.1.0: Monday. Fresh deliveries, fresh slate, fresh opinions about the weather.
dlg.tilda.mon.2.0: Monday is for restocking. Don't lean on the shelf. The shelf is nervous.
dlg.tilda.tue.1.0: Tuesday. The saloon's shut, so everyone drops in here to complain about it.
dlg.tilda.tue.2.0: Tuesdays Wren is off. The village gossip comes straight to me. I'm very busy.
dlg.tilda.wed.1.0: Wednesday. Marcus is closed, so the nails are going quickly.
dlg.tilda.wed.2.0: Midweek. The cat naps in the window and the whole street slows down for her.
dlg.tilda.thu.1.0: Thursday. Felix is off, so the fish prices are all anyone argues about.
dlg.tilda.thu.2.0: Thursdays I do the books. They add up better when nobody's watching.
dlg.tilda.fri.1.0: Friday. The whole village needs one more thing before the weekend.
dlg.tilda.fri.2.0: Friday's busy. Wren says it's because I have good lighting. I say it's the biscuits.
dlg.tilda.sat.1.0: Saturday. Market day. Half the village comes in just to look at the other half.
dlg.tilda.sat.2.0: Last day before my Sunday off. I'm already smiling at the sign that says "Closed".
dlg.tilda.sun.1.0: Sunday. The shop is shut, and so am I. Come back tomorrow. I'll put you on the slate.
dlg.tilda.sun.2.0: No shopkeeping today. I'm a person. It's an odd feeling. I'm trying it out.
dlg.tilda.sunny.1.0: Fine day. Folks buy seeds with a spring in their step and leave without their change.
dlg.tilda.sunny.2.0: The window's a sunbeam. The pumpkins are glowing. It's very unfair to the other produce.
dlg.tilda.sunny.3.0: Good weather, quiet shop. Everyone's outside, appreciating things.
dlg.tilda.rain.2.0: Rain's tapping the glass. The customers will come in and not buy anything. I love it.
dlg.tilda.rain.3.0: A wet day, and the door bell keeps ringing. Nobody's buying. Everybody's visiting.
dlg.tilda.rain.4.0: Dry seeds in a damp week. I've moved them to the top shelf. They can see the street.
dlg.tilda.storm.1.0: Thunder. I've put the glass jars on the floor and the cat on the counter. Both happier.
dlg.tilda.storm.2.0: Storm. The shop lights flicker. The slate stays put. The slate is stubborn.
dlg.tilda.storm.3.0: A storm like this is a good excuse to close early and read. I never do.
dlg.tilda.snow.1.0: Snow on the step. I've salted it, and the postman thanked me twice.
dlg.tilda.snow.2.0: The whole street's muffled. I can hear the stove tick, which is the best sound in the shop.
dlg.tilda.snow.3.0: Snow. People walk slowly and say hello properly. I wish it lasted all year.
dlg.tilda.wind.1.0: The sign's swinging. That means a long day of people holding onto their hats and asking about rope.
dlg.tilda.wind.2.0: Blustery. I've weighed the seed packets down with a pumpkin. It looks intentional.
dlg.tilda.wind.3.0: Wind like this, every door in the village bangs. It sounds like applause for nothing.
dlg.tilda.morning.1.0: Early. The shop's still waking up, and so is the kettle.
dlg.tilda.morning.2.0: First customer of the day gets the freshest bread and the oldest gossip.
dlg.tilda.morning.3.0: Morning light on the shelves. It makes everything look like it's worth twice as much.
dlg.tilda.midday.1.0: Midday. The busiest hour and the shortest patience. I'm managing both.
dlg.tilda.midday.2.0: Lunch rush. Everyone wants something small and a long chat.
dlg.tilda.midday.3.0: Afternoon in the shop. The dust's dancing, and so are the prices.
dlg.tilda.evening.1.0: Nearly closing. I stack the shelves and pretend I'm not waiting for one more customer.
dlg.tilda.evening.2.0: Evening. The street turns gold, and I turn the sign. In that order.
dlg.tilda.evening.3.0: Last hour. I do the sums and the kind of listening you can't put a price on.
dlg.tilda.late.1.0: Late. The lamp's still on. I'm "doing the books". You may sit.
dlg.tilda.late.2.0: Past closing. The shop's quiet, and the stove's still warm. Both are yours.
dlg.tilda.late.3.0: Evenings I count the day. Not coins. Faces.
dlg.tilda.here.1.0: Mind the step. The cat has opinions about it.
dlg.tilda.here.2.0: Everything here is for sale except the stool by the stove. That one's for talking.
dlg.tilda.here.3.0: Take your time. Browsing is free. So is the gossip. The biscuits are one coin.
dlg.tilda.fr.1.0: There you are. I put you down on the slate for a pie. I'll explain the pie later.
dlg.tilda.fr.2.0: You're the only customer who asks how the shop is. I noticed.
dlg.tilda.fr.3.0: Marcus asked if you were "available". I said you were "credited". He wrote it down.
dlg.tilda.fr.4.0: I saved the good stool for you. It's the one without the squeak.
dlg.tilda.fr.5.0: Your slate balance is healthy. I won't tell you the number. It would embarrass you.
dlg.tilda.fr.6.0: Wren says you're good company. Wren's never wrong about company. About lemons, always.
dlg.tilda.fr.7.0: A customer who stays for tea is worth ten who don't. You're worth at least twelve.
dlg.tilda.fr.8.0: Come by tomorrow. I'll find something you need and sell it at cost.
dlg.tilda.cl.1.0: You have your own seat now. I moved the chair an inch so it faces the door.
dlg.tilda.cl.2.0: Shops are quiet places, mostly. You make this one sound busy.
dlg.tilda.cl.3.0: When the village shrinks I count the stock instead of the people. It helps. A little.
dlg.tilda.cl.4.0: [farm] is the best account I've ever kept. Don't tell the others.
dlg.tilda.cl.5.0: Felix tried to settle his tab in fish. I accepted. The cat accepted first.
dlg.tilda.cl.6.0: You're a good neighbor. I'd like that on the sign, but there's no room.
dlg.tilda.cl.7.0: Remind me to show you the back room someday. It's mostly boxes, and one very good view.
dlg.tilda.cl.8.0: Talking to you is the part of the day I don't put on the slate. It's mine.
dlg.tilda.co.1.0: Kindness is the only stock that goes up when you give it away. You taught me that again.
dlg.tilda.co.2.0: I used to count the days I was open. Now I count the days you came in.
dlg.tilda.co.3.0: There's a lamp in the back that I leave on for the whole village. Tonight it's on for you.
dlg.tilda.co.4.0: Your slate page is the longest in the shop. I've started a second chalkboard.
dlg.tilda.co.5.0: I've sold a lot of seeds. The best thing I ever sold you was a "Good morning."
dlg.tilda.co.6.0: Thank you, [player]. I'll put it on the slate, but it won't fit, so I'll write it on the wall.
dlg.tilda.co.7.0: The village isn't shrinking. I counted again. It was only me, being foolish with a pencil.
dlg.tilda.co.8.0: When I think of a full shop, I think of you in the doorway, pretending to browse.
dlg.tilda.lonely.1.0: Quiet week. Nobody's in the shop but me and the dust. I've started talking to the dust.
dlg.tilda.lonely.2.0: I rang the bell twice just to hear it. You'll forgive an old shopkeeper her habits.
dlg.tilda.tired.1.0: Long day of lifting. My back's a ledger of every sack I've shifted.
dlg.tilda.tired.2.0: A bit worn today. The tea helps. So do you.
dlg.tilda.delighted.1.0: Best day I've had in months! Three customers cried with joy over a hinge. It's a small town.
dlg.tilda.delighted.2.0: Everything sold, everybody smiled, and the cat knocked nothing over. A perfect ledger.
dlg.tilda.mischief.1.0: I put the "sale" sign on the stool by the stove. Let's see who tries to buy it.
dlg.tilda.mischief.2.0: I told Marcus the nails were out of stock. They weren't. I wanted to see his face.
dlg.tilda.worried.1.0: The shelves are fuller than the street. I don't like that arithmetic.
dlg.tilda.farm.1.0: Your field's coming along, I hear. Whatever you grow, I'll put it in the window.
dlg.tilda.farm.2.0: Everyone in the village is talking about your crops. I'm taking credit for the seeds.
dlg.tilda.farm.3.0: Animals! You'll need feed, rope and a very patient hat. I stock all three.
dlg.tilda.farm.4.0: A cow is a long conversation. A chicken is a short, loud one. Choose wisely.
dlg.tilda.fest.1.0: Festival soon. I'm stocking ribbons and flour. The whole village over-buys both.
dlg.tilda.fest.2.0: A festival week fills the shop with people who don't need a thing. They just want company.
dlg.tilda.fest.3.0: Festival day! The shop's shut and the slate's off. I'm only here to eat.
dlg.tilda.bday.1.0: My birthday's close. I don't make a fuss. I make a large pie.
dlg.tilda.bday.2.0: Another year on the shelf. Still good. No expiry date. Don't check.
dlg.tilda.bday.3.0: Oh, you remembered. I'm putting it on the slate, in capital letters. Thank you.
dlg.tilda.bday.4.0: Juno's birthday is close. I've baked her something. She'll say she didn't need it. She'll eat it all.
dlg.tilda.bday.5.0: Piper's birthday. I'm sending a ribbon for the fiddle. She'll haggle about the color.
dlg.tilda.rare.1.0: In thirty years of shopkeeping I've sold exactly one thing I regret: a parrot. It stayed.
dlg.tilda.rare.2.0: Somebody once paid me in a song. It's on the slate. It's the only entry I reread.
dlg.tilda.rare.3.0: There's a very small door behind the flour sacks. It's for the cat. The cat has a key.
dlg.tilda.rare.4.0: Come closer. (She turns the slate around.) That's your name at the top, [player]. It's been there since the first day.
Strawberries! Oh, [player]. These go in the window, and then they go in me.
dlg.npc.tilda.gift.item.forage.elderflow: Elderflower. My mother used to dry it in the back room. The whole shop would smell like June.
dlg.npc.tilda.gift.item.food.pumpkin_pie: A pumpkin pie. For me? That's three slate entries and a tear. I'll go and find my glasses.
dlg.npc.tilda.gift.item.crop.cauliflower: Cauliflower. A sensible vegetable. A very white one. I'll find it a place on the shelf.
dlg.npc.tilda.gift.item.crop.potato.0: A potato. Honest, round and ready for anything. Thank you. I'll put it with the others.
dlg.npc.tilda.gift.item.forage.raspberry: Raspberries! Tiny, red and wonderful. I'll eat three, and hide the rest from the cat.
dlg.npc.tilda.gift.item.resource.stone.0: A stone. Hm. I'm sure it's a very good one. I'll keep it near the door, to hold it open.
dlg.npc.tilda.gift.item.forage.clam.0: A clam. I don't sell fish, dear. But it's a thoughtful gift, in a briny sort of way.
dlg.npc.tilda.gift.item.resource.slime.0: Slime. In my shop. On my counter. ...I'll put it on the slate under "Regrets".
dlg.npc.tilda.gift.cat.Fish.0: A fish. I don't sell fish, and I don't take fish. The cat will take the fish. Thank you.
dlg.npc.tilda.gift.item.resource.goldbar: A gold bar! That's more than the shop's worth, dear. I'll keep it in the safe, under "Someday".
