dlg.npc.tilda.gift.item.resource.copperb: Copper. Bram will want to see this. I'll keep it on the shelf until he wanders in.
dlg.npc.tilda.gift.item.resource.coal.0: Coal. For the stove. A very practical gift, and a warm one. Thank you.
dlg.npc.tilda.gift.item.resource.wood.0: Wood. For the shelves. Marcus will be jealous, and the shelves will be thrilled.
dlg.npc.tilda.gift.item.resource.bone.0: A bone. I'll put it in the window. People will assume it's a rare cheese.
dlg.npc.tilda.gift.item.product.egg.0: An egg. Fresh, I hope. I'll sell it back to you at a loss.
dlg.npc.tilda.gift.item.artisan.jam.0: Jam! My mother's favorite, and mine. I'll put it on the shelf, behind a sign that says "Not for sale."
dlg.npc.tilda.gift.item.artisan.wine.0: Wine. For the shop's anniversary. I'll open it in March. Or tomorrow. One of those.
dlg.npc.tilda.gift.item.crop.pumpkin.0: A pumpkin! A prize one, by the look. I'll put it in the window and give it a name.
dlg.npc.tilda.gift.item.food.salad.0: Salad. A respectable meal and a very green one. I'll eat it at the counter and call it lunch.
dlg.npc.tilda.gift.item.forage.truffle.0: A truffle. A real one. I don't know whether to eat it or insure it.
dlg.npc.tilda.gift.item.resource.ironbar: Iron. Bram's department. I'll hold it until he comes, with a note that says "Safe, and a little jealous."
dlg.npc.tilda.gift.repeat.0: Another one! I'll put it on the slate twice, in different handwriting. Thank you.
event.tilda_heart4.intro: Come around the counter. I want you to see something. Mind the cat.
event.tilda_heart4.after: {if choice:slate.thanks}A thank-you. In chalk. It looks very well on a slate.{else}{if choice:slate.joke}A joke on the slate! Nobody's ever dared. I'll leave it up.{else}A promise. I'll hold you to it. I hold everyone to everything, kindly.{/if}{/if}
event.tilda_heart6.intro: Lock the door behind you, would you? It's after hours. I do the books after hours. Sit.
event.tilda_heart6.after: Thank you for letting me say it out loud. It weighs less than it did. Mind the step on the way out.
event.tilda_heart8.intro: Stocktake day. Help me move the flour? There's something behind the shelf I've never had the nerve to look at.
event.tilda_heart8.after: {if choice:card.bake}Baking from it, then. Flour, butter and my mother's handwriting. I'll need a bigger oven and a smaller heart.{else}{if choice:card.keep}Keep it safe. A card doesn't need to be a pie to matter.{else}Sharing it. I'll write it out for the whole village. Mother would have scolded me, then smiled.{/if}{/if}
event.tilda_heart10.intro: Close your eyes. No, really. I've done something on the front of the shop and I'm too nervous to watch.
event.tilda_heart10.give: I baked it from her card. Take it. It's the first one. The sign outside says you're a supplier, and so you are.
event.tilda_heart10.thanks: {if choice:card.share}I copied the recipe for the whole village, and put your name at the bottom, in chalk.{else}{if choice:card.bake}The pie came out right. It tasted like June, and my mother, and you.{else}The card's still safe. The pie's yours. Both are the best things in the shop.{/if}{/if}
event.tilda_friend.ask: Saturday stocktake, and I'm three sunflowers short of finishing the window. Do you have any?
event.tilda_friend.success: Three sunflowers! The window's finished. It looks like noon. Thank you, dear. I'll put it on the slate.
event.tilda_friend.fallback: Three sunflowers, if you find them? The window's half dressed and very embarrassed.
event.juno_heart4.setup: Okay, okay, okay, don't move! I have a surprise and a very sticky label.
event.juno_heart4.prank: Done! You've been labeled. It says 'Guest (Excellent)'. I'm very proud.
event.juno_heart4.reaction: {if choice:label.accept}A label that stays! I'll put one on your hat tomorrow.{else}{if choice:label.relabel}Relabeled! 'Apprentice (Chaotic)'. That's fair, and now it's on my forehead.{else}You ate the label! Nobody's ever eaten a label! I'm thrilled and slightly worried.{/if}{/if}
event.juno_heart6.intro: Don't come in. Okay, come in. Close the door. I made something. It's crooked. I'm about to put it in the quench barrel.
event.juno_heart6.after: Thank you for stopping me. It's still crooked. It's also still mine. That's a new feeling.
event.juno_heart8.intro: Okay, okay, okay. Tonight I show it to Bram. The crooked horseshoe. Will you stand next to me? I'll sweat less.
event.juno_heart8.after: {if choice:shoe.wait}You waited. That meant more than any speech. He's holding it now. He hasn't said a word. It's the best word.{else}{if choice:shoe.praise}You said it was wonderful. He's frowning at it like he agrees. That's how Bram says yes.{else}You gave me the hammer. So I tapped the bend one last time. It's better, and it's still mine.{/if}{/if}
event.juno_heart10.intro: Okay, okay, okay. Hold out your hand. I made a mark. My own. Nobody else has it. I stamped this with it before I told anyone.
event.juno_heart10.give: It's the first thing with my name on it. A tiny copper bar. It isn't much. It's the most I've ever made.
event.juno_heart10.thanks: {if choice:shoe.wait}Bram saw the mark, and waited, and nodded once. Once! You were there for the whole thing.{else}Bram saw the mark and said, 'Hm.' I'm having it framed.{/if}
event.juno_friend.intro: Okay, okay, okay, quick one. Come see the swimming pool. It's a bucket. Wren named it. I made the sign.
event.juno_friend.doing: See? 'Swimming Pool (Official)'. I'm very proud, and the bucket is very wet.
event.juno_friend.wrap: Best pool in Wetherell. Also the only pool. Also a bucket. I'll cherish it.
event.piper_heart4.intro: Last set of the night, and I'm out of ideas. You pick one. Anything. I'll pretend it's mine.
event.piper_heart4.after: {if choice:request.ballad}A ballad! I'll play it slowly and cry with my elbows.{else}{if choice:request.jig}A jig! Feet, take cover. I'm warming up the bow.{else}The parsnip song! My masterpiece! I'll sing it with feeling and a straight face.{/if}{/if}
event.piper_heart6.intro: Down here. The cellar. It's quiet. I'm not hiding. I'm resting my nerves among the barrels.
event.piper_heart6.after: Thank you. The nerves are still here. But they're smaller. They fit in the fiddle case.
event.piper_heart8.intro: Come sit by the stage. I'm writing a song, and I need your help with every line. It's the only way it'll be good.
event.piper_heart8.after: {if choice:chorus.home}'Home' in the chorus. Of course. That's the word that was missing.{else}{if choice:chorus.road}'The road' in the chorus. Yes. Wanderers love a road.{else}'The saloon' in the chorus. A song about the room itself. Brilliant, and a bit cheeky.{/if}{/if}
event.piper_heart10.intro: Tonight I play the song we wrote. I'll start it. After the first verse, I'm stepping off the stage.
event.piper_heart10.outro: {if choice:chorus.home}They sang 'home' back to me. All of them. I didn't play a note.{else}{if choice:chorus.road}They sang the road back to me. Every verse. I only stood and listened.{else}They sang the room back to the room. Even the stool joined in.{/if}{/if}
event.piper_friend.intro: Friday! Come hear the parsnip ballad. It's four verses, and one of them is about the cat.
event.piper_friend.doing: 'Oh, parsnip, parsnip, in the soil...' I'm not done. I'm very close. I'm very dramatic.
event.piper_friend.wrap: That's a chorus! A bad one. Mine. Tell nobody, and come back for the encore.
quest.tilda_display.title: A Window Worth Looking At
quest.tilda_display.desc: Tilda needs five parsnips for the shop window.
quest.tilda_cauliflower.title: Quiet Things
quest.tilda_cauliflower.desc: Tilda wants three cauliflowers for the harvest basket.
quest.tilda_pie_week.title: Pie Week
quest.tilda_pie_week.desc: Tilda would like a pumpkin pie baked by a friend for the window.
quest.tilda_pie_week.o0: Bring a pumpkin pie to Tilda
quest.juno_ore.title: Ore to Ruin
quest.juno_ore.desc: Juno wants practice iron to ruin on purpose.
quest.juno_charcoal.title: Coal for Polish
quest.juno_charcoal.desc: Juno needs coal for a clasp she cannot talk about.
quest.juno_gold.title: Her First Mark
quest.juno_gold.desc: Juno needs a gold bar to stamp her first mark.
quest.juno_gold.o0: Bring a gold bar to Juno
quest.piper_strings.title: New Strings
quest.piper_strings.desc: Piper needs fiber to twist new fiddle strings.
quest.piper_flowers.title: Stage Lights
quest.piper_flowers.desc: Piper wants three sunflowers for the stage.
quest.piper_juice.title: For the Throat
quest.piper_juice.desc: Piper would like two bottles of juice before the big night.
letter.tilda_bday.subject: A note from the slate
letter.tilda_bday.body: My birthday is soon. I don't make a fuss. If you were to bring a pie, I'd pretend I'd forgotten. -- Tilda
letter.juno_bday.subject: Okay, okay, okay
letter.juno_bday.body: My birthday is soon! I'm not hinting! I've labeled the date in red, twice. Any gift is fine, except kale. -- Juno
letter.juno_thanks.subject: The label
letter.juno_thanks.body: I kept your label. It's on the anvil. Bram hasn't noticed. Bram has noticed. -- Juno
letter.piper_bday.subject: A short verse
letter.piper_bday.body: My birthday's soon. I'm not hinting. I'm humming. A gift of jam would rhyme with 'ham'. -- Piper
letter.piper_thanks.subject: About the request
letter.piper_thanks.body: The song you chose is now the one everybody asks for. It's your fault. Thank you. -- Piper
dlg.tilda.bark.1.0: Mind the step. The cat has opinions.
dlg.tilda.bark.2.0: I'll put it on the slate.
dlg.tilda.bark.3.0: Seeds, string and gossip. All fairly priced.
dlg.tilda.bark.4.0: Marcus owes Odalys an apology and a pie. It's on the slate.
dlg.tilda.bark.5.0: Wren borrowed lemons I never had. I'm not asking.
dlg.tilda.bark.6.0: The bell sounds best at nine. I've tested it.
dlg.tilda.bark.7.0: Browsing is free. So is the tea. Mostly.
dlg.tilda.bark.8.0: Somebody's whistling outside. I like it. I'm suspicious.
dlg.tilda.bark.rain.1.0: Rain on the glass. Best customer I've had all week.
dlg.tilda.bark.storm.1.0: The jars are on the floor. The cat's on the counter.
dlg.tilda.bark.snow.1.0: Snow on the sign. I'm leaving it.
dlg.tilda.bark.wind.1.0: The sign's swinging. Hold your hats, everyone.
dlg.tilda.bark.spring.1.0: Seed season! Everyone wants parsnips on the same morning.
dlg.tilda.bark.summer.1.0: Awning's up. The bell sounds better in shade.
dlg.tilda.bark.fall.1.0: Pie week. The whole street smells like cinnamon and rivalry.
dlg.tilda.bark.winter.1.0: Stove's on. Kettle's on. Come in.
dlg.tilda.bark.morning.1.0: First customer gets the freshest bread and the oldest gossip.
dlg.tilda.bark.evening.1.0: Nearly closing. One more customer, please. I'm not desperate.
dlg.tilda.bark.here.1.0: Everything's for sale except the stool by the stove.
dlg.tilda.bark.here.2.0: Take your time. The dust is in no hurry.
dlg.tilda.bark.sun.1.0: Closed today. I'm a person. It's strange.
dlg.tilda.bark.sat.1.0: Market day. Half the village visits to look at the other half.
dlg.tilda.bark.rare.1.0: I once sold a parrot. It stayed. It's still here.
dlg.tilda.bark.rare.2.0: Kindness is the only stock that rises when given away.
dlg.juno.bark.1.0: Okay, okay, okay, nobody touch the hot thing.
dlg.juno.bark.2.0: Technically it's art. Technically it's also a doorstop.
dlg.juno.bark.3.0: Hammer, tongs, patience. In that order, mostly.
dlg.juno.bark.4.0: I labeled the kettle "Bram's Best Friend".
dlg.juno.bark.5.0: Piper says I talk too fast. I said that was a tempo.
dlg.juno.bark.6.0: That clasp closes! Don't tell Bram I cried.
dlg.juno.bark.7.0: Wren's gossip is floating in again. It smells like cider.
dlg.juno.bark.8.0: Bram said "Hm" to the bucket. It was a good "Hm".
dlg.juno.bark.rain.1.0: Rain on a hot forge! Best sound in the world.
dlg.juno.bark.storm.1.0: Thunder! The anvil rang back. They're old friends.
dlg.juno.bark.snow.1.0: Snow on the sill, glow in the forge. Postcard.
dlg.juno.bark.wind.1.0: Wind blew the ash everywhere. I'm gray to the elbows.
dlg.juno.bark.spring.1.0: Spring means hinges. Every gate in town fell off.
dlg.juno.bark.summer.1.0: Summer forge: a sauna with opinions.
dlg.juno.bark.fall.1.0: Leaves on the roof hiss when they land. Delightful.
dlg.juno.bark.winter.1.0: Winter forge. Warmest room in Wetherell. Ask Bram. He'll nod.
dlg.juno.bark.morning.1.0: Coaxing the fire. Don't talk loud. It startles.
dlg.juno.bark.evening.1.0: Last clasp of the day. Always the hard one.
dlg.juno.bark.here.1.0: Everything's labeled. Some labels are insults. Bram's chair says "Do Not".
dlg.juno.bark.here.2.0: Mind the floor. The tile by the door is "Mister Trip".
dlg.juno.bark.mon.1.0: Closed Mondays. I'm here anyway. Labeling.
dlg.juno.bark.thu.1.0: Thursday: sharpening everything. Even the bucket.
dlg.juno.bark.rare.1.0: I labeled a puddle "Puddle (Ambitious)". It got deeper.
dlg.juno.bark.rare.2.0: Bram taught me patience first. Then where the good tea is hidden.
dlg.piper.bark.1.0: Request anything. I'll probably play something else.
dlg.piper.bark.3.0: You said "turnip", I heard "return it". It rhymes.
dlg.piper.bark.4.0: Juno says I talk too fast. I call it tempo.
dlg.piper.bark.5.0: Wren borrowed my rosin. I'm composing a strongly worded verse.
dlg.piper.bark.6.0: The fiddle's in tune. I'm the one slightly flat.
dlg.piper.bark.7.0: I wrote a song about parsnips. It's a masterpiece. Ask anyone.
dlg.piper.bark.8.0: Somebody hum the second verse. I've forgotten it. Dramatically.
dlg.piper.bark.rain.1.0: Rain's a drummer with strong opinions. I'll play along.
dlg.piper.bark.storm.1.0: Thunder's the bass. I'll take the bridge.
dlg.piper.bark.snow.1.0: Snowfall's the quietest song there is. I'll hum.
dlg.piper.bark.wind.1.0: The wind plays the chimney flat. Confident, though.
dlg.piper.bark.spring.1.0: New season, new songs. Mostly about parsnips.
dlg.piper.bark.summer.1.0: Beach sets! Sand in the strings, salt in the song.
dlg.piper.bark.fall.1.0: Harvest dances! Everyone's feet are louder than the fiddle.
dlg.piper.bark.winter.1.0: Winter ballads. Wool socks and slow bows.
dlg.piper.bark.morning.1.0: Early. My fingers wake around the third cup of tea.
dlg.piper.bark.evening.1.0: Showtime soon. I'm telling the fiddle it's gorgeous.
dlg.piper.bark.here.1.0: Tip jar's on the left. Wren added "And for Wren."
dlg.piper.bark.here.2.0: The stool by the stage is mine. The rest is chaos.
dlg.piper.bark.tue.1.0: Day off. I'm on the beach with a fiddle and crabs.
dlg.piper.bark.fri.1.0: Friday! Everybody wants "the one about the cow".
dlg.piper.bark.rare.1.0: I once played one request for forty minutes. Called an encore.
dlg.piper.bark.rare.2.0: The first time they sang my song, I stopped playing to listen.
dlg.tilda.slate.0: This is the slate. Every small kindness in Wetherell, in chalk. Look. Marcus is two planks ahead of Odalys.
dlg.tilda.slate.1: There's room under your name. What would you like me to write?
dlg.tilda.slate.r0: A thank-you. Plain, honest and very hard to cash. My favorite currency.
dlg.tilda.slate.r1: A joke! On my slate! ...Oh, that's good. I'm laughing in a shop. Don't tell anyone.
dlg.tilda.slate.r2: A promise. I'll write it small and keep it large.
dlg.tilda.hours.0: I count the stock every night. And every night the street is quieter than it was. It's an odd thing for a shopkeeper to notice.
dlg.tilda.hours.1: I tell myself the village isn't shrinking. Then I count again. What do you think?
dlg.tilda.hours.r0: It isn't. ...Say it again, slower. I'd like to put it on the slate in your handwriting.
dlg.tilda.hours.r1: Together. Now that's a plan I'd stock. Bring ideas. And tea.
dlg.tilda.hours.r2: Gently. Yes. Recounting with kindness. I'll try that, and the cat can supervise.
dlg.tilda.card.0: Behind the flour sacks, in a very old tin, lies a recipe card in faded ink.
dlg.tilda.card.1: My mother's pumpkin pie. I've never baked from it. I was afraid I'd get it wrong. What should I do?
dlg.tilda.card.r0: Bake it. Yes. With you in the kitchen, so I can't back out.
dlg.tilda.card.r1: Safe. It's been safe for forty years. That's not a bad record.
dlg.tilda.card.r2: The whole village. ...The pie feud would hate that. I love it.
dlg.juno.label.0: So? What do you say about it? I'll accept any answer except "Hm."
dlg.juno.label.r0: Accepted! You're officially a fixture. I'll sweep around you.
dlg.juno.label.r1: Relabel me! Oh, that's brilliant. "Apprentice (Chaotic)". Stick it on. Right here.
dlg.juno.label.r2: You... you ate it. ...I'm labeling this moment "Do Not Repeat". And then I'll want it repeated.
dlg.juno.strike.0: It's my first piece that's not a copy. A little horseshoe. Look at it. It's lopsided, and I made it, and I hate that I love it.
dlg.juno.strike.1: Do I keep it, or does it go in the barrel?
dlg.juno.strike.r0: Keep it. Yes. Even crooked. Especially crooked.
dlg.juno.strike.r1: Together! You hold the tongs, I'll tap the bend. Okay, okay, okay, let's go.
dlg.juno.strike.r2: Okay, it's very funny. A horseshoe for a three-legged horse. A very proud three-legged horse.
dlg.juno.shoe.0: Bram stands at the far end of the forge. Juno holds out the horseshoe with both hands and does not look up.
dlg.juno.shoe.1: I can't look. Tell me what's happening.
dlg.juno.shoe.r0: ...Thank you. Quiet's good. The anvil's listening too.
dlg.juno.shoe.r1: Wonderful? It's crooked! ...But thank you. I'm going to look up now. Slowly.
dlg.juno.shoe.r2: A hammer. Okay. One more tap. For luck. For me. For crooked things everywhere.
dlg.piper.request.0: The room's waiting. A ballad, a jig, or my masterpiece about parsnips?
dlg.piper.request.r0: A ballad. A sad one. A sad one with a happy ending, at least. Gather round.
dlg.piper.request.r1: A jig! Get your boots! The stool in the corner is going to dance, I can feel it.
dlg.piper.request.r2: The parsnip song! That's a chorus. A bad one. Mine.
dlg.piper.fright.0: I can play for a hundred people and never blink. But tonight, I think they'll know. That I'm not as good as I say I am.
dlg.piper.fright.1: What do I do with that?
dlg.piper.fright.r0: Talk. Okay. I'm scared of silence, and of being quiet. And of being forgotten. There. Now it's on the barrel.
dlg.piper.fright.r1: ...Thank you. Silence is easier when someone shares it.
dlg.piper.fright.r2: A bucket! You're going to drum on a bucket? ...Okay. Okay! Count me in, in four. One, two, three...
dlg.piper.chorus.0: The verse is about someone arriving. The chorus is about where they end up. What is it?
dlg.piper.chorus.r0: Home. ...Oh. Oh, that's it. I've been missing that word for three months.
dlg.piper.chorus.r1: The road. Restless, wide and honest. It rhymes with "code". If you squint.
dlg.piper.chorus.r2: This room! A song about the saloon. The stools will cry.
dlg.tilda.display.ask.0: The window needs something that says "we're open". Five parsnips, nicely lined up. A tidy row sells anything.
dlg.tilda.display.ask.1: You grow the best parsnips in Wetherell. Would you lend me five? I'll put you on the slate for a pie.
dlg.tilda.display.ask.r0: A dear. Five parsnips. I'll clear the sill.
dlg.tilda.display.ask.r1: That's all right. The window will manage. It's patient.
dlg.tilda.display.remind.0: Five parsnips for the window. Nothing fancy. Just a row of honest roots.
dlg.tilda.display.turnin.0: Look at those! The window looks like noon. I'll put it on the slate in big letters. Here's something for your trouble.
dlg.tilda.cauli.ask.0: Cauliflower, dear. Three heads, firm and white. They're for the harvest basket in the window.
dlg.tilda.cauli.ask.1: Everyone says it's a plain vegetable. I say it's a quiet one. Would you grow me three?
dlg.tilda.cauli.ask.r0: Three. Perfect. I'll start a slate entry titled "Quiet Things".
dlg.tilda.cauli.ask.r1: Later is fine. The basket's in no hurry. It has all the time in the world.
dlg.tilda.cauli.remind.0: Three cauliflowers for the harvest basket. Firm ones, if you can.
dlg.tilda.cauli.turnin.0: Oh, those are beauties. White as fresh chalk. Thank you, [player]. I'll put it all on the slate.
dlg.tilda.pie.ask.0: Pie week is coming. I'd like a pumpkin pie in the window, baked by someone who loves baking. Not me. You.
dlg.tilda.pie.ask.1: One pie. Warm, if you can. I'll put a sign beside it that says "Made by a friend".
dlg.tilda.pie.ask.r0: A pie from you, in my window. That's three entries on the slate and a happy tear.
dlg.tilda.pie.ask.r1: Think. A pie is a promise, and a promise deserves a minute.
dlg.tilda.pie.remind.0: One pumpkin pie, for the window. Pie week is coming on, and the shelf is empty.
dlg.tilda.pie.turnin.0: A pie! A real one! Warm, even. It goes in the window, and the whole street will stop. Thank you, dear.
dlg.juno.ore.ask.0: Okay, okay, okay: I'm out of practice iron. Five chunks of ore? I want to smelt something I can ruin freely.
dlg.juno.ore.ask.1: Bram says ruin is a method. I'm testing that.
dlg.juno.ore.ask.r0: Five ore! You're the best. I'll label the pile with your name. It'll say "Hero (Dusty)".
dlg.juno.ore.ask.r1: No worries! The anvil can wait. It never complains. Much.
dlg.juno.ore.remind.0: Five iron ore, to ruin on purpose. It's a tradition. I just started it.
dlg.juno.ore.turnin.0: Ore! Look at it! Gray, lumpy, full of possibility. Thank you! This is for you, and the pile's labeled.
dlg.juno.coal.ask.0: Okay, okay, okay: I need coal. Six pieces. For polishing. The finest finish comes from the worst fire.
dlg.juno.coal.ask.1: I'm making a clasp I'm not allowed to talk about. Can you help?
dlg.juno.coal.ask.r0: Six coals! You're a saint with soot on your boots. I'll make you something small and secret.
dlg.juno.coal.ask.r1: Not now's fine! The clasp's patient. It's practicing its click.
dlg.juno.coal.remind.0: Six pieces of coal, for the secret clasp. It keeps asking when. I tell it soon.
dlg.juno.coal.turnin.0: Coal! Six lovely black lumps. This is the best day. Thank you, [player]. The clasp is blushing.
dlg.juno.gold.ask.0: Okay, okay, okay. This is a big one. I need a gold bar. Just one. It's for my first mark, my own mark.
dlg.juno.gold.ask.1: If you can find one, I'll stamp the first piece with it. I think you should have it.
dlg.juno.gold.ask.r0: A gold bar! For my mark! You're the reason I'm even doing this. Don't tell Bram I cried.
dlg.juno.gold.ask.r1: Look. Slowly. I'll practice being patient. That's the other thing I'm bad at.
dlg.juno.gold.remind.0: One gold bar, for my first mark. I've cleared the corner of the anvil for it.
dlg.juno.gold.turnin.0: Gold. A real bar. I'm holding it, and my hands are shaking. Thank you, [player]. It's the beginning of something.
dlg.piper.strings.ask.0: The fiddle's strings are done for. I need fiber to twist new ones. Five bundles. It's a very low-tech art.
dlg.piper.strings.ask.1: Bring me the fiber, and the next song's on the house. It's not good. It's free.
dlg.piper.strings.ask.r0: Five bundles! You're a roadie in disguise. The fiddle thanks you in advance, in a squeal.
dlg.piper.strings.ask.r1: Not now's fine. The fiddle can wait. It's got a flat sense of time.
dlg.piper.strings.remind.0: Five bundles of fiber for new strings. The fiddle's been whispering about it.
dlg.piper.strings.turnin.0: Fiber! Soft and strong. I'll twist the strings tonight, and the first note will be yours. Thank you!
dlg.piper.flowers.ask.0: Three sunflowers for the stage. A fiddle needs a few stage lights, and a sunflower's the cheapest sun.
dlg.piper.flowers.ask.1: I'd put them by the stool, and play them a very sentimental song.
dlg.piper.flowers.ask.r0: Three sunflowers! A garden for the stage! The stool will be so jealous.
dlg.piper.flowers.ask.r1: Later's fine. The stool can stay boring. It's used to it.
dlg.piper.flowers.remind.0: Three sunflowers for the stage. The stool's waiting, in a very dignified sulk.
dlg.piper.flowers.turnin.0: Sunflowers! They're glorious. The stage looks like a sunrise. I'll write you a verse. It won't rhyme. Thank you, [player].
dlg.piper.juice.ask.0: Two bottles of juice, for the throat. Big gigs ahead. I'd like a gentle, fruity warm-up and a quiet moment of thanks.
dlg.piper.juice.ask.1: Nobody else asks what I'd like to drink. You do. That's why I'm asking you.
dlg.piper.juice.ask.r0: Two bottles! I'll toast the stool, the stage and you. In that order. It's a tradition. Starting now.
dlg.piper.juice.ask.r1: Not yet. The throat can wait. It's a patient instrument.
dlg.piper.juice.remind.0: Two bottles of juice, for the big night. The throat's practicing its thank-you.
dlg.piper.juice.turnin.0: Juice! Two bottles, sweet and cold. That's a chorus. A drinkable one. Thank you, [player]. I'll sing you the first verse.
topic.tilda.gossip: Ask what the village is saying
topic.piper.silence: Ask about the quiet between songs
dlg.react.tilda.spring.d.0: Seed season! The whole village will want parsnips on the same morning. I've cleared the counter and my nerves.
dlg.react.tilda.fall.d.0: Pie week. Everyone's arguing about crust, and everyone's wrong. I'm taking notes in chalk.
dlg.react.tilda.harvest.d.0: First harvest! You grew something. In my window it goes. I'll put you on the slate for a pie.
dlg.react.tilda.wren.d.0: I hear Wren sang something terrible last night. Four people told me. I charged none of them for the gossip.
dlg.react.juno.spring.d.0: Okay, okay, okay, spring! Every gate in town fell off. I've labeled the pile "Opportunity".
dlg.react.juno.summer.d.0: The forge is a sauna with opinions. I stopped wearing sleeves. Bram's pretending not to see.
dlg.react.juno.harvest.d.0: Your first harvest! Okay, okay, okay, tell me every detail. Especially the tools.
dlg.react.juno.bram.d.0: Bram said "Good enough. Better than good." about a repair. I'm having it carved on the anvil.
dlg.react.piper.spring.d.0: New season, new songs! Most are about parsnips. All are better than the last. It's a rule.
dlg.react.piper.winter.d.0: Winter ballads! Wool socks, slow bows, and everyone sits closer. It's my favorite acoustic.
dlg.react.piper.harvest.d.0: You harvested something! I'm writing a verse. It rhymes "crop" with "stop". It almost works.
dlg.react.piper.wren.d.0: Wren's Opening Night! I heard it through three walls. I'm furious it was good.
dlg.social.tilda.joke.good.0: Ha! A joke with good margins. I'll put it on the slate.
dlg.social.tilda.joke.great.0: Oh, that's a good one. I'm laughing in a shop. Don't tell anyone.
dlg.social.tilda.joke.flop.0: Hm? Was that a joke? ...Oh. Ha. I was counting change. Say it again, slower.
dlg.social.tilda.compliment.good.0: That's kind of you. I'll put it in the till, where it can grow.
dlg.social.tilda.compliment.great.0: Oh, my. A compliment that size will need its own shelf. Thank you.
dlg.social.tilda.compliment.flop.0: Oh. You're very kind. I'm not sure what to do with it. Where do I put it?
dlg.social.tilda.advice.great.0: Advice? Ask me anything. First: buy early. Second: pay in kindness. Third: wear a hat in March.
dlg.social.tilda.advice.good.0: My advice? Plant parsnips first. They pay for everything else.
dlg.social.tilda.advice.flop.0: Advice from me? Dear, I sell seeds. I give directions, mostly. I'll try. Where to?
dlg.social.tilda.tease.great.0: Oh, you cheeky thing! I'll put that on the slate. Under "Brave."
dlg.social.tilda.tease.good.0: Ha! Cheeky. A fair price for being fond of me.
dlg.social.tilda.tease.flop.0: Teasing? In my shop? ...I'm choosing to take that as affection. Careful.
dlg.social.juno.joke.good.0: Ha! Good one! Okay, okay, okay, I'm using that on Bram.
dlg.social.juno.joke.great.0: Oh, that's brilliant! I'm going to label it. "Joke (Excellent)."
dlg.social.juno.joke.flop.0: Okay, okay, okay... Was that a joke? ...Oh! Ha. Sorry. The forge is loud.
dlg.social.juno.compliment.good.0: Aw! Thanks! I'm blushing. It's the forge, probably. It's also you.
dlg.social.juno.compliment.great.0: Okay, okay, okay, I'm going to cry! It's soot! It's definitely soot. Thank you!
dlg.social.juno.compliment.flop.0: Oh! Er. Thank you. I wasn't ready. I'm holding a hammer. It's awkward.
dlg.social.juno.advice.good.0: Advice? Okay! Sure. Here's mine: label everything. Twice.
dlg.social.juno.advice.great.0: Advice! I love advice! Okay, okay, okay: don't trust the red one. Always trust the hot one.
dlg.social.juno.advice.flop.0: Advice? Hm. I'd rather find out by burning myself. It's how I learned everything.
dlg.social.juno.tease.great.0: Oh, you wicked thing! Do it again! I'll label it "Excellent Insult."
dlg.social.juno.tease.good.0: Ha! Cheeky! I'll get you back with a very small, very sharp spoon.
dlg.social.juno.tease.flop.0: Okay, okay, okay... I'm not sure if that was funny. I'll decide later. Hm.
dlg.social.piper.joke.good.0: Ha! Nice timing. You'd make a good drummer.
dlg.social.piper.joke.great.0: That's a chorus! Oh, I'm stealing it. I'll say I wrote it.
dlg.social.piper.joke.flop.0: Wait, was that a joke? ...Oh! Ha. Sorry. I was tuning. Say it again, in B flat.
dlg.social.piper.compliment.good.0: Aw, thanks! I'll hum it later. It's a lovely melody, as compliments go.
dlg.social.piper.compliment.great.0: Stop it, you'll make me modest! I won't manage it. It's off-brand.
dlg.social.piper.compliment.flop.0: Oh! Uh. Thank you. I'm not used to speeches without a drum roll.
dlg.social.piper.advice.good.0: Advice? Sure. Never play a request in the key you were asked in. Keep them guessing.
dlg.social.piper.advice.great.0: Advice! Here: always tune before you panic. Panic's worse out of tune.
dlg.social.piper.advice.flop.0: Advice? Hm. I'd rather learn from a wrong note. It stays with you.
dlg.social.piper.tease.great.0: Oh, that's a fine tease! I'll write it into the bridge.
dlg.social.piper.tease.good.0: Ha! Cheeky. I'll answer in a very flat verse.
dlg.social.piper.tease.flop.0: Hm. Funny. I'll remember that during the encore.
dlg.tilda.topic.gossip.0: Pull up the stool. I never gossip. I just keep accurate books of what's said.
dlg.tilda.topic.gossip.1: {Wren's asking for lemons again.|Juno ordered three hundred rivets and a very small spoon.|Piper owes me four sonnets.|Marcus and Odalys are still not speaking over a pie.}
dlg.tilda.topic.gossip.2: I'd say more, but the slate has ears.
dlg.tilda.topic.slate.0: The slate? Every small kindness in Wetherell, in chalk. It's an honor system. Mostly honor.
dlg.tilda.topic.slate.1: Yours is the best page. I won't tell you why. I'll just write more.
dlg.juno.topic.labels.0: Okay, okay, okay, the labels! Come look.
dlg.juno.topic.labels.1: {Tongs: "Not a Back Scratcher".|Bram's chair: "Do Not".|The bucket: "Swimming Pool (Official)".|The anvil: "Sulking, Possibly".}
dlg.juno.topic.labels.2: There's a new one every week. Bram pretends not to read them. He reads them.
dlg.juno.topic.mark.0: My own mark. A small stamp that's only mine. I haven't made it yet.
dlg.juno.topic.mark.1: Okay. Okay. When I do, you'll see it first. That's a promise, and I label my promises.
dlg.piper.topic.request.0: A request! Finally. Let me guess: "something cheerful"?
dlg.piper.topic.request.1: {Here's a jig.|Here's a ballad. It's four minutes of sighing.|Here's the parsnip song.|Here's something I wrote this morning. It has a hiccup.}
dlg.piper.topic.request.2: That's a chorus! Come back after the set. I'll take requests for the encore.
dlg.piper.topic.silence.0: The quiet between songs? I used to fill it. With chatter, with puns, with panic.
dlg.piper.topic.silence.1: With you here, I let it sit. It's the best part of the set. Don't tell the fiddle.
letter.tilda_slate_thanks.subject: About the slate
letter.tilda_slate_thanks.body: Your name's still at the top. Come by when the chalk needs company. -- Tilda
dlg.npc.wren.missed.0: There you are! A whole week without a word. I nearly told the stool your secrets just to have someone to tell.
dlg.npc.hazel.missed.0: Oh. You're back. (I kept your chair. It stayed empty. It was very polite about it.) I'm glad.
dlg.npc.bram.missed.0: ...Hm. A week. Forge was quiet. Hm. Good to see you.
dlg.npc.tilda.missed.0: There you are! I kept your page on the slate warm. The shop's been quiet without you. Mind the cat.
dlg.npc.juno.missed.0: Okay, okay, okay, you're back! I made a clasp for every day you were gone. The pile's a bit embarrassing.
dlg.npc.piper.missed.0: A week! I wrote you a verse for every night. Most are bad. One is about soup. That's a chorus.
dlg.npc.marcus.missed.0: Ah. You're back. The workshop's been quiet. I planed a plank twice, just to hear the sound.
dlg.npc.odalys.missed.0: Welcome back. I trust you've been well. The clinic noticed your absence, in a clinical sort of way.
dlg.npc.felix.missed.0: There you are. The fish were asking after you. Or I was. Hard to tell, at that hour.
dlg.npc.ione.missed.0: Oh, hello again. I kept your place in the book. Nobody read ahead. I checked the margins.
dlg.npc.dorian.missed.0: ...You returned. I had a small mushroom for you, and then I ate it. I'll find another.
dlg.npc.elara.missed.0: Back at last. I've kept a list of questions for you. It's become a short book.
dlg.tilda.namefarm.sunnyside.0: Sunnyside. A good name and a good promise. I'll put the sign in the window.
dlg.tilda.namefarm.green_acres.0: Green Acres. A lovely name and a lovely hope. Let's both aim for the second.
dlg.tilda.namefarm.home.0: Just 'Home'. Oh. That's the nicest farm name in the valley, and I sell seeds for a living.
dlg.tilda.namefarm.maple.0: Maple. Warm, sticky and sweet in fall. A farm name with a good pantry.
dlg.tilda.namefarm.wetherell.0: Wetherell! Naming it after the village. I'll put it on the slate as 'Loyal'.
dlg.tilda.namefarm.farm.0: Just 'Farm'. Bold. Minimal. I'll put it on the slate as 'Farm (Honest)'.
dlg.tilda.namefarm.farmville.0: Farmville. A bit on the nose, dear, but the nose is a good one.
dlg.tilda.namefarm.parsnip_palace.0: Parsnip Palace. Parsnips are the sensible king of the garden. I'll stock a crown.
dlg.tilda.namefarm.pumpkin.0: Pumpkin! Round, orange and very prize-worthy. I'll put your name in the window.
dlg.tilda.namefarm.pie.0: Pie. There's a feud brewing in this village over that very word. You've picked a side. I admire it.
dlg.tilda.namefarm.cozy_corner.0: Cozy Corner. I'm borrowing that for the back of the shop. I'll put you on the slate for it.
dlg.tilda.namefarm.default.0: Default. Practical, dear. I'll update the slate to 'Default (Sensible)'.
dlg.tilda.nameplayer.farmer.0: Farmer. Ha. The honest name for a very honest job. I'll put it on the slate in big letters.
dlg.tilda.nameplayer.nobody.0: Nobody. Dear, you're somebody to this shop. I'll put it on the slate as 'Somebody'.
dlg.hazel.namefarm.meadowbrook.0: Meadowbrook. (It sounds like a book that smells of grass.) A gentle name.
dlg.hazel.namefarm.willow.0: Willow. (A name that bends and doesn't break.) I'd read that book.
dlg.hazel.namefarm.my_farm.0: My Farm. (Plain and honest. The best titles never try.)
dlg.hazel.namefarm.new_farm.0: New Farm. (It's the first line of a long book.) I'd like to see the second.
dlg.hazel.namefarm.baa.0: Baa. (A farm named after a sheep's whole opinion.) I like it.
dlg.hazel.namefarm.the_burrow.0: The Burrow. (Small, warm, and good for hiding with a book.) That's a farm I understand.
dlg.hazel.namefarm.untitled.0: Untitled. (The best books start that way. The worst ones stay that way.) I'm hopeful.
dlg.hazel.namefarm.lorem_ipsum.0: Lorem Ipsum. (A very old, very empty book.) I'd like to fill it for you.
dlg.hazel.namefarm.dragon.0: Dragon. (There aren't any in the library.) That's ambitious for a parsnip patch.
dlg.hazel.nameplayer.you.0: You. (A very direct name.) It makes every sentence a little shy.
dlg.bram.namefarm.hillside.0: Hillside. Hm. Good drainage. Good name.
dlg.bram.namefarm.oakwood.0: Oakwood. Strong. Slow to burn. Good.
dlg.bram.namefarm.beans.0: Beans. Hm. Short. Good. Easy to say. Hard to improve.
dlg.bram.namefarm.hay.0: Hay. Hm. Plain. Warm. Good for horses and people.
dlg.bram.namefarm.hoe.0: Hoe. Hm. A name and a tool. I approve of both.
dlg.bram.namefarm.dirt.0: Dirt. Hm. Where it all begins. Good name.
dlg.bram.namefarm.nothing.0: Nothing. Hm. Bold. Then fill it.
dlg.juno.namefarm.home_sweet_home.0: Home Sweet Home! Okay, okay, okay, I want that carved on a gatepost. I'll do the lettering.
dlg.juno.namefarm.honeybee.0: Honeybee! Okay, okay, okay, buzzing is a great work ethic. I'll make you a bee clasp.
dlg.juno.namefarm.potato.0: Potato! Okay, okay, okay, honest, round and ready for anything. That's me. That's the farm.
dlg.juno.namefarm.bacon.0: Bacon! Okay, okay, okay, the smell alone would pay the rent. I'm in.
dlg.juno.namefarm.cluck.0: Cluck! Okay, okay, okay, short, loud and a little smug. I'll make you a chicken weathervane.
dlg.juno.namefarm.scarecrow.0: Scarecrow! Okay, okay, okay, named for the one worker who never complains. Brilliant.
dlg.juno.namefarm.noodle.0: Noodle! Okay, okay, okay, wobbly, long and impossible to stop eating. Exactly what a farm should be.
dlg.juno.namefarm.asdf.0: Asdf! Okay, okay, okay, keyboard-mashing is a legitimate naming strategy. I once labeled a bucket 'Qwerty'.
dlg.juno.namefarm.bob.0: Bob! Okay, okay, okay, a farm called Bob. I'm not sure it needs anything else. Bob is enough.
dlg.juno.namefarm.pizza.0: Pizza! Okay, okay, okay, nothing's more delightful. I'll show up at dinner.
dlg.juno.nameplayer.test.0: Okay, okay, okay, your name's Test. I'm going to treat that as the name of a very proud person.
dlg.juno.nameplayer.boss.0: Boss! Okay, okay, okay, I'll take orders. Mostly the ones that involve labeling.
dlg.piper.namefarm.fairview.0: Fairview! It rhymes with 'I knew', if you squint. I'll write you a gate song.
dlg.piper.namefarm.riverside.0: Riverside. There's no river. That's the kind of honesty I like in a song.
dlg.piper.namefarm.sunflower.0: Sunflower! The best stage light there is, and you can eat it. That's a chorus.
dlg.piper.namefarm.old_macdonald.0: Old MacDonald! Had a farm, and so do you! Ee-i-ee-i-o. It's already a chorus.
dlg.piper.namefarm.parsnip.0: Parsnip! I wrote a masterpiece about it. I'll dedicate the second verse to your gate.
dlg.piper.namefarm.moo.0: Moo! The only farm name that works as a song. 'Moo, moo, moo.' That's a chorus.
dlg.piper.namefarm.hoedown.0: Hoedown! Oh, I'm bringing the fiddle. Wear your heavy boots.
dlg.piper.namefarm.spud_life.0: Spud Life! It's the title of a ballad I haven't written. I'll start tonight.
dlg.piper.namefarm.placeholder.0: Placeholder! The only farm name that promises a better one later. That's a chorus, and a plan.
dlg.piper.namefarm.steve.0: Steve. That's it, just Steve. I'll write a love song to the fence.
dlg.piper.namefarm.unicorn.0: Unicorn! The most sparkly farm in Wetherell. Do you also have a rainbow, or just manure?
dlg.piper.nameplayer.bob.0: Bob! It rhymes with 'job', and with 'sob', and with 'knob'. A fine name for a verse.
dlg.piper.nameplayer.chef.0: Chef! I'll write you a theme song with a lot of pots in it.
dlg.wren.namefarm.clover.0: Clover! Luck, with a stem. I'll pour you something green on the house. For luck.
dlg.wren.namefarm.daisy.0: Daisy! Cheerful, sturdy and slightly bossy. Is that the farm or you?
dlg.wren.namefarm.the_farm.0: 'The Farm'. Not even a name, just a fact. I admire a farmer who doesn't decorate.
dlg.wren.namefarm.farmy_mcfarmface.0: Farmy McFarmface! Oh, I love it. The whole village will say it with a straight face, and I'll see to that.
dlg.wren.namefarm.turnip.0: Turnip! The most dignified root and the funniest word. Wetherell approves.
dlg.wren.namefarm.cabbage_patch.0: The Cabbage Patch! Where good gossip grows. I'll visit with a very large basket.
dlg.wren.namefarm.cheese.0: Cheese! The only farm name that makes every person in the room hungry. Well played.
dlg.wren.namefarm.haystack.0: Haystack! Finding anything there is a hard job. I'll be careful with my needles.
dlg.wren.namefarm.mud.0: Mud! Honest, brown and everywhere. I hope you're prepared for the mat.
dlg.wren.namefarm.banana.0: Banana! There isn't a single banana in Wetherell. The village is baffled. I'm thrilled.
dlg.wren.namefarm.test.0: 'Test'! You're testing it. So am I. How's it holding up? Better than the saloon roof.
dlg.wren.namefarm.farm_name.0: 'Farm Name'! You named your farm 'Farm Name'. I'm laughing so much I've forgotten what I was saying.
dlg.wren.namefarm.everything.0: Everything! A big name for a farm. I hope the soil keeps up.
dlg.wren.namefarm.the_ranch.0: 'The Ranch'. We don't have a ranch. We have a farm. I'm going to pretend I didn't see that.
dlg.wren.nameplayer.player.0: Player! Of what? Cards? Pipes? Hearts? I'll assume the first, and then be disappointed gently.
dlg.wren.nameplayer.steve.0: Steve! The most dependable name there is. I'll save you the good stool.
event.marcus_heart8.intro: Come here. I want you to look at the roof plan. Not many have. Measure twice, I tell myself. Then I ask you to look once.
event.marcus_heart8.after: {if choice:roof.measure}You measured with me. Twice, then a third time under your breath. It's the first time I haven't been alone with it.{else}{if choice:roof.design}A new pitch. I'd never have tried it. I'll draw it tonight. Not nine times. Perhaps four.{else}You held the ladder. That's half of any building. The roof's still nearly fixed. But less alone.{/if}{/if}
event.odalys_heart8.intro: Sit. The clinic is closed. I'm taking my own prescription tonight: soup and company. I haven't had either in some time.
event.odalys_heart8.after: {if choice:office.insist}You insisted I rest. I filed it under 'Unreasonable'. Then I did as I was told. It was remarkably effective.{else}{if choice:office.soup}We shared the soup. I'll write it up as 'Treatment, successful'.{else}Your prescription says 'Come back anyway.' I've pinned it above my desk. Doctor's orders.{/if}{/if}
event.felix_heart8.intro: Dawn, the pond, and a line that's tugging. I've a feeling about this one. Hold the net. Don't breathe.
event.felix_heart8.after: {if choice:big.net}You netted it! It was this big. I'll say it's bigger by Friday.{else}{if choice:big.release}You let it go. It waved, I'm sure. I'll catch it again. We've an understanding.{else}You measured it honestly. Eleven inches. I'm devastated. And moved. Mostly devastated.{/if}{/if}
event.dorian_heart8.intro: ...Sit. Here. On the log. I'm going to show you something. Don't speak yet.
event.dorian_heart8.after: {if choice:notebook.praise}You praised them. Nobody has. I'll draw a tiny one for you, tomorrow.{else}{if choice:notebook.ask}You asked for one. I tore it out myself. It's the best one. Don't lose it.{else}You drew one back. It's crooked. It's wonderful. I'll keep it in the notebook.{/if}{/if}
event.elara_heart8.intro: Come see! I've never shown this to anyone. It's a list. A long one. With drawings. Don't laugh. Laugh a little.
event.elara_heart8.after: {if choice:list.pick}We picked one together. The sea, from a boat. I've circled it twice, and then once more in pen.{else}{if choice:list.add}You added a place. I've written it in the margin: 'Somewhere [player] suggests.' It's already my favorite.{else}You promised to visit. I'm holding you to it. Gently. With a very long scarf.{/if}{/if}
event.ione_heart8.intro: Come with me. There's a shelf at the back that I haven't shown anyone. It's quiet. It's a little sad. It's mine.
event.ione_heart8.after: {if choice:shelf.take}You took one for someone. That's the first set-aside book that's ever left the shelf. I'll note it.{else}{if choice:shelf.read}You read one aloud. The shelf has never been so quiet. Or so pleased.{else}You left a note. I'll never move it. It's the best bookmark I've ever had.{/if}{/if}
quest.marcus_planks.title: Planks for the Roof
quest.marcus_planks.desc: Marcus needs wood for the hall roof.
quest.odalys_elderflower.title: Elderflower for the Clinic
quest.odalys_elderflower.desc: The clinic needs elderflower for a tonic.
quest.felix_bait.title: Bait for the Dawn
quest.felix_bait.desc: Felix is short of bait for the morning tide.
quest.dorian_basket.title: A Basket for the Forest
quest.dorian_basket.desc: Dorian needs mushrooms for his basket.
quest.elara_wool.title: Wool for the Waiting Room
quest.elara_wool.desc: Elara is out of wool for the scarf.
quest.ione_pearl.title: Pearls for the Reading Room
quest.ione_pearl.desc: Ione would like a pearl for her favorite book.
letter.marcus_bday.subject: A short note
letter.marcus_bday.body: My birthday is soon. I plane a plank for it. A straight board would be a fine present. Measure twice. -- Marcus
letter.odalys_bday.subject: A medical note
letter.odalys_bday.body: My birthday is soon. I observe it with soup. Visitors are permitted. Doctor's orders. -- Dr. Penn
letter.felix_bday.subject: Tide table
letter.felix_bday.body: Birthday's soon. I'll be at the pond. A fish would be a fine present. A big one. This big. -- Felix
letter.dorian_bday.subject: A leaf
letter.dorian_bday.body: Birthday soon. It's fine. A mushroom would be fine. A quiet walk, finer. -- D.
letter.elara_bday.subject: Guess what!
letter.elara_bday.body: My birthday's soon! Any gift is fine, except bad news. I'll knit you a sock either way. -- Elara
letter.ione_bday.subject: A note, set aside
letter.ione_bday.body: My birthday is soon. A book would be welcome. Not one I own. I own most of them. -- Ione
dlg.dorian.spring.1.0: Spring. Wild garlic first. Then ferns. Then everything at once.
dlg.dorian.spring.2.0: Moss turns bright after rain. I notice. Nobody asks.
dlg.dorian.spring.3.0: Found a mushroom shaped like a hat. It's not mine. It's very smug.
dlg.dorian.summer.1.0: Summer. Berries, shade, quiet paths. The forest keeps cool. I follow.
dlg.dorian.summer.2.0: Long days. Short sentences. It suits the heat.
dlg.dorian.summer.3.0: Bees in the clover. They don't mind me. I don't mind them.
dlg.dorian.fall.1.0: Fall. The best mushrooms. Truffles hide under oak. They hide well.
dlg.dorian.fall.2.0: Leaves everywhere. A soft sound underfoot. I walk slowly to hear it.
dlg.dorian.fall.3.0: Leaves fall without a word. It's how I'd like to leave a room.
dlg.dorian.winter.1.0: Winter. Winter roots. Frost on the moss. Small gifts, if you look.
dlg.dorian.winter.2.0: Snow keeps the forest quiet. I keep it company. My birthday's in winter. I don't mention it.
dlg.dorian.winter.3.0: Tracks in snow tell a story. Mostly about rabbits. They're busy.
dlg.dorian.mon.1.0: Monday. Marcus sharpens things. I listen from the porch. It sounds like thinking.
dlg.dorian.tue.1.0: Tuesday. Quiet forest. Quieter village. A good day for walking.
dlg.dorian.wed.1.0: Wednesday. Marcus is on a bench with Bram. I stay home. I like the silence.
dlg.dorian.thu.1.0: Thursday. Felix is off. The pond's busy. I avoid it.
dlg.dorian.fri.1.0: Friday. The village gets loud. I take the back path. It's longer. It's better.
dlg.dorian.sat.1.0: Saturday. Market. Noise. I leave a mushroom on a step and go.
dlg.dorian.sun.1.0: Sunday. I stay in the forest. The trees don't ask what day it is.
dlg.dorian.sunny.1.0: Sun through leaves. Green light. It makes everything look kind.
dlg.dorian.sunny.2.0: Dry day. Mushrooms hide. I look anyway.
dlg.dorian.rain.2.0: Wet moss, open caps. A good day to be small and patient.
dlg.dorian.rain.3.0: Wet moss, soft sound. I stand under a tree and listen.
dlg.dorian.storm.1.0: Storm. The forest bows. I wait under the thickest oak.
dlg.dorian.storm.2.0: Thunder echoes through the trunks. Like a very large footstep.
dlg.dorian.snow.1.0: Snow. Every branch is a line drawn in white.
dlg.dorian.snow.2.0: Hush. Even my boots are quiet. I like it.
dlg.dorian.wind.1.0: Wind in the canopy. A long, low sound. Like breathing.
dlg.dorian.wind.2.0: Gusty. Leaves fly. I keep my hat on and my words in.
dlg.dorian.morning.1.0: Early. Dew on every web. I try not to break them.
dlg.dorian.morning.2.0: First light. The forest wakes in order. Birds, then bees, then me.
dlg.dorian.midday.1.0: Midday. Shade. A flask. A log. That's lunch.
dlg.dorian.midday.2.0: Busy forest. Everyone's pretending not to be.
dlg.dorian.evening.1.0: Evening. Gold light. I walk home slowly. The basket's heavy. Good.
dlg.dorian.evening.2.0: Dusk. Owls begin. They don't mind company.
dlg.dorian.late.1.0: Late. I sketch what I found. Nobody sees the drawings. Please don't ask.
dlg.dorian.late.2.0: Night. Moss glows a little, if you squint. I squint.
dlg.dorian.here.1.0: Step softly. Under the roots. Everyone looks up.
dlg.dorian.here.2.0: The chair by the stove is mine. The cushion knows. Marcus pretends.
dlg.dorian.fr.1.0: You say little. That's the best kind of company, [player].
dlg.dorian.fr.2.0: Come with me tomorrow. Bring a basket. Don't bring questions.
dlg.dorian.fr.3.0: A mushroom was on your step. Not me. The forest.
dlg.dorian.fr.4.0: You stand the right distance. Not many do.
dlg.dorian.fr.5.0: Walking is better with someone who doesn't need an answer.
dlg.dorian.cl.1.0: I'm not a talker. But I'm glad you're nearby.
dlg.dorian.cl.2.0: The forest likes you. That's rare. It likes very few.
dlg.dorian.cl.3.0: There's a spot I go. Quiet. I'll show you. Someday. Soon.
dlg.dorian.cl.4.0: I draw mushrooms. I haven't shown anyone. I might. Don't hurry me.
dlg.dorian.cl.5.0: Marcus asked who the gifts were from. I said "the forest". He nodded. Twice.
dlg.dorian.co.1.0: Words are slow for me. You wait. It's the whole gift.
dlg.dorian.co.2.0: I left something on your step. It was me. Not the forest.
dlg.dorian.co.3.0: A letter from me would be a drawing. Of a mushroom. With a speech bubble.
dlg.dorian.lonely.1.0: A long walk. Nobody. The trees were kind. It wasn't enough.
dlg.dorian.tired.1.0: Tired. The basket's heavy. So's the day.
dlg.dorian.delighted.1.0: Found a perfect mushroom. Cap round, stem straight. I stood there smiling. A bit.
dlg.dorian.mischief.1.0: I left a pinecone on Marcus's chair. He's been looking for the culprit all day.
dlg.dorian.worried.1.0: The forest feels strange today. Probably me. Probably.
dlg.dorian.farm.1.0: Your field's coming along. Plants speak slowly. They say yes.
dlg.dorian.farm.2.0: Animals. Noisy. Warm. I'd visit. From a distance.
dlg.dorian.fest.1.0: Festival soon. Crowds. I'll bring a mushroom. Then leave.
dlg.dorian.fest.2.0: Festival. I'm here. Near the edge. Near the exit. It's fine.
dlg.dorian.bday.1.0: My birthday's near. It's fine. I'll walk. Alone, mostly. Fine.
dlg.dorian.bday.2.0: You came. I didn't say. ...Who said? Marcus. Of course.
dlg.dorian.bday.3.0: Marcus's birthday. I'll leave a pinecone. It's tradition.
dlg.dorian.rare.1.0: I once argued with a stump. I lost. It was a very good stump.
dlg.dorian.rare.2.0: I kept the first mushroom I ever found. Dried. In my pocket. It's tiny. It's mine.
dlg.dorian.rare.3.0: Look. (He opens a small notebook.) My drawings. You're the first. Please be kind.
dlg.npc.dorian.gift.item.forage.mushroom: A mushroom. Perfect gills. Where did you find it? ...Never mind. Thank you.
A truffle. You found one. I'm quiet because I'm moved.
dlg.npc.dorian.gift.item.forage.wildgarl: Wild garlic. Sharp. Green. Good. I'll cook it with the stew.
dlg.npc.dorian.gift.item.forage.hazelnut: Hazelnuts. Small. Patient. I'll keep them for a squirrel. And me.
dlg.npc.dorian.gift.item.forage.blackber: Blackberries. Sweet and thorny. Like the forest. Thank you.
dlg.npc.dorian.gift.item.forage.raspberr: Raspberries. Red and shy. I'll eat them slowly.
dlg.npc.dorian.gift.item.crop.tomato.0: A tomato. Hm. Too round. Too loud. I'll find it a home. Far away.
dlg.npc.dorian.gift.item.fish.pufferfish: A pufferfish. It's looking at me. I'm looking at it. We've reached an understanding.
Slime. Hm. I'll keep it outside. It looks homesick.
dlg.npc.dorian.gift.repeat.0: Another one. Thank you. I'll leave you something. Not me. The forest.
dlg.elara.spring.1.0: Spring! Sneezes, sprains and a lot of "I'm fine, really". I love the optimism.
dlg.elara.spring.2.0: My birthday's in spring. I knit myself a hat to celebrate. It has a very small hat on it.
dlg.elara.spring.3.0: Everyone's allergic to something this month. Mostly work. I prescribe a nap and tea.
dlg.elara.summer.1.0: Summer means sunburn and sand in the plasters. I keep a bucket of cold water for dramatic exits.
dlg.elara.summer.2.0: The clinic's a cool corner. Half the village drops in to "check their pulse". It's the fan.
dlg.elara.summer.3.0: Saturdays I'm at the beach. Sea air, sandwiches, a very long knitting row. Bliss.
dlg.elara.fall.1.0: Fall: scrapes, sniffles and a lot of pumpkin related injuries. Don't ask. Do ask. I love stories.
dlg.elara.fall.2.0: The clinic smells of cinnamon and cough drops. I'd bottle it, if I could.
dlg.elara.fall.3.0: Harvest week, everybody's tired and proud. Best patients ever. They bring cake.
dlg.elara.winter.1.0: Winter: chills, chapped lips and one very long scarf in progress. It's now the length of a cat.
dlg.elara.winter.2.0: The waiting room's the warmest place in town. People "come for the cough". They stay for the tea.
dlg.elara.winter.3.0: Snow on the sill, tea in hand, a baby sock on the needles. I'm happy. Don't tell Dr. Penn.
dlg.elara.mon.1.0: Monday! New bandages, new gossip, new reasons to say "keep your socks on".
dlg.elara.tue.1.0: Tuesday. Wren's shut. Everyone has nowhere to be sad. I've got extra tea.
dlg.elara.wed.1.0: Wednesday. Marcus is on a bench with Bram. I'm told they're communicating. In silence. Brilliant.
dlg.elara.thu.1.0: Thursday. Felix is off. His hands are always cold. I knit him mittens. He pretends he hates them.
dlg.elara.fri.1.0: Friday! The week's aches arrive all at once. I love a rush. It's like a very polite flood.
dlg.elara.sat.1.0: Saturday. The clinic's shut. I'm on the beach with a sandwich and a very long scarf.
dlg.elara.sun.1.0: Sunday. A quiet day. I tidy the shelves and give each bottle a pep talk.
dlg.elara.sunny.1.0: Sunny! Everybody outside means fewer sniffles. I miss the company, though.
dlg.elara.sunny.2.0: Perfect weather for a walk. I'm prescribing one for you. Doctor's orders. Don't tell Dr. Penn I said so.
dlg.elara.rain.2.0: Rain means sniffles. I'll be busy. I've put the kettle on for all of them.
dlg.elara.rain.3.0: A rainy day: needles, tea and drip on the glass. It's like being tucked in.
dlg.elara.storm.1.0: Thunder! I tell nervous patients it's the sky clearing its throat. Works about half the time.
dlg.elara.storm.2.0: A storm is the best time to knit. The clicks keep time with the thunder.
dlg.elara.snow.1.0: Snow! Everyone's cheeks are pink. It's a free health check.
dlg.elara.snow.2.0: I drew a face on the frosty window. Dr. Penn pretended not to see. She waved at it later.
dlg.elara.wind.1.0: Windy. Hats off, hair everywhere. The clinic door keeps opening on its own. I say hello to it.
dlg.elara.wind.2.0: Gusty day. The scarf's flying. It's longer than the clinic. It's starting to look intentional.
dlg.elara.morning.1.0: Good morning! The first patient's always the kettle. It's been waiting since dawn.
dlg.elara.morning.2.0: Early. I'm winding yarn and humming. The clinic hums back. It's a quiet duet.
dlg.elara.midday.1.0: Midday. A cough, a splinter, a very dramatic sneeze. I've seen all three before lunch.
dlg.elara.midday.2.0: Busy hour. Please hold your wound with dignity. I'll be right with you.
dlg.elara.evening.1.0: Nearly closing. I roll the bandages and the day. Both neat. Both a little crooked.
dlg.elara.evening.2.0: Evening. The last patient leaves smiling. That's the only medicine I'm sure about.
dlg.elara.late.1.0: Late. I knit by the lamp. Click, click, clack. A very small, very sleepy symphony.
dlg.elara.late.2.0: Past closing. The clinic's quiet, the tea's cold and I'm three rows from the end.
dlg.elara.here.1.0: Sit anywhere. Not on the skeleton's chair. He's shy.
dlg.elara.here.2.0: I put a tiny hat on the plant. Dr. Penn took it off. I put it back. We're at an impasse.
dlg.elara.here.3.0: The sea's the only doctor I never argue with. It always says "rest".
dlg.elara.fr.1.0: Hey, [player]! You look better every week. That's my favorite kind of good news.
dlg.elara.fr.2.0: I made extra tea. Stay a minute? It's a very small prescription.
dlg.elara.fr.3.0: Dr. Penn says I smile too much at patients. I say it's the best remedy. She's undecided.
dlg.elara.fr.4.0: I knit you something. It's a sock. Don't ask what it's for. It's just a sock.
dlg.elara.fr.5.0: You're one of my favorite people to see. And I see a lot of people.
dlg.elara.cl.1.0: If you ever feel low, come find me. I'll have tea and nothing to fix.
dlg.elara.cl.2.0: I keep a list of places I've never been. The beach is at the top. You're at the bottom, in pencil.
dlg.elara.cl.3.0: I tell the village to rest. I'm terrible at it. You're allowed to tell me.
dlg.elara.cl.4.0: Dr. Penn says I'm "a bit much". I told her that's the diagnosis. She smiled.
dlg.elara.cl.5.0: I knit something for everyone in Wetherell. Yours is the longest. It's also a surprise.
dlg.elara.co.1.0: I wanted to see the sea from a boat. Then I met you. Now I want a boat for two.
dlg.elara.co.2.0: I used to be afraid of staying forever. Now I'd stay, if you're nearby.
dlg.elara.co.3.0: If I wrote you a letter it'd be a very long scarf. With a postscript at the far end.
dlg.elara.co.4.0: Thank you, [player]. Keep your socks on. And keep coming by.
dlg.elara.lonely.1.0: Quiet clinic. I knitted a sock for the kettle. It didn't say thanks. Rude.
dlg.elara.tired.1.0: A long day. My needles are dragging. I'll cast off early and nap with the cat.
dlg.elara.delighted.1.0: Best day ever! Three patients got better, and one didn't even want to leave! I'm glowing!
dlg.elara.mischief.1.0: I put a tiny hat on Dr. Penn's skeleton. She noticed. She said nothing. She's on to me.
dlg.elara.worried.1.0: A patient didn't come for their check-up. I'll visit with soup. It's my favorite kind of nosy.
dlg.elara.farm.1.0: Your crops look so healthy! I'd write you a clean bill of fields.
dlg.elara.farm.2.0: Animals! Lovely. Keep a basin and a very large bandage handy. For the chicken's pride.
dlg.elara.fest.1.0: Festival soon! I'll bring the first-aid kit and a very festive scarf.
dlg.elara.fest.2.0: Festival day! I'm off duty. My patients have been warned to be fine.
dlg.elara.bday.1.0: My birthday's close! I'm not hinting. I'm knitting a very pointed hat.
dlg.elara.bday.2.0: You remembered! I'm blushing in knit-and-purl. Thank you!
dlg.elara.bday.3.0: Dr. Penn's birthday. I knitted her a scarf in the color of "very sensible". She'll love it.
dlg.elara.rare.1.0: I once knitted a sock for a chair. The chair wore it with pride. Dr. Penn took a photo.
dlg.elara.rare.2.0: The first person I ever bandaged hugged me. I've been chasing that feeling ever since.
dlg.elara.rare.3.0: Close your eyes. (Two needles click.) Now open them. It's a tiny scarf for your favorite chicken.
A snowdrop! The brave little flower. I'll press it in my notebook, next to the first one.
dlg.npc.elara.gift.item.crop.cranberry.0: Cranberries! Tart and shiny. I'll make jam, and then I'll tell everyone it was my idea.
dlg.npc.elara.gift.item.artisan.jam.0: Jam! Sticky, sweet and perfect on toast. I'm sharing it. Possibly with myself.
A seashell! I'll hold it to my ear. It's saying "Take a vacation". I believe it.
dlg.npc.elara.gift.item.crop.spinach.0: Spinach. Strong and sensible. Dr. Penn will approve. I'll eat it quickly.
dlg.npc.elara.gift.item.artisan.juice.0: Juice! For a very long afternoon. I'll drink a tiny bit and hide the rest from the cat.
dlg.npc.elara.gift.item.resource.bone.0: A bone! Eek. I'll put it in the anatomy drawer, next to the other, worse ones.
dlg.npc.elara.gift.item.resource.bat_win: A bat wing! I'll knit it a hat. A very small, very dignified one.
dlg.npc.elara.gift.item.resource.slime.0: Slime! It's wobbling at me. I'll put it in a jar and call it "Brenda". Brenda stays.
dlg.npc.elara.gift.repeat.0: Another one! You're spoiling me. I'll knit you something back. It'll be a sock. It's always a sock.
dlg.marcus.roof.0: Here's the plan. Pitch, rafters, shingles. I've drawn it nine times. I'm afraid it still won't hold.
dlg.marcus.roof.1: What do you think I should do?
dlg.marcus.roof.r0: Measure with me. Yes. Hold the end of the tape. Twice. Then once more.
dlg.marcus.roof.r1: A new design. I'd stopped asking. ...Show me the angle. Slowly.
dlg.marcus.roof.r2: The ladder. Plain, steady, necessary. That's the best offer I've had.
dlg.odalys.office.0: I advise everyone to rest. I take none of it. Tonight I'm trying. It's unfamiliar. Be gentle.
dlg.odalys.office.r0: Insist? ...Fine. I'll rest. Under protest, with soup, and with a witness.
dlg.odalys.office.r1: Soup, shared. That's the whole treatment. You've diagnosed me. Accurately.
dlg.odalys.office.r2: A prescription? For me? Hm. "Come back anyway." I'll follow it to the letter.
dlg.felix.big.0: Something very large tugs on Felix's line. It might be a fish. It might be the bottom of the pond.
dlg.felix.big.1: It's this big. Maybe bigger. What do we do?
dlg.felix.big.r0: The net! Hold steady. ...There she is. A beauty. I'll never doubt your wrist again.
dlg.felix.big.r1: Let it go? ...Aye. A good fish deserves a long life. And a good story. Both stay.
dlg.felix.big.r2: Honestly. Hm. Eleven inches. ...It was this big a moment ago. I'm not saying it was your fault.
dlg.dorian.notebook.0: Dorian takes a small, worn notebook from his coat. He holds it closed for a long moment.
dlg.dorian.notebook.1: My drawings. Mushrooms. Hundreds. You're the first. Please be kind.
dlg.dorian.notebook.r0: ...Thank you. Nobody's said. Not once. It's a good word. I'll keep it.
dlg.dorian.notebook.r1: One. For you. Take the best. It's the small brown one. It's me, really.
dlg.dorian.notebook.r2: You drew a mushroom. It has a face. ...I love it. Don't tell anyone.
dlg.elara.list.0: Elara unrolls a very long paper, covered in tiny writing and doodled boats.
dlg.elara.list.1: Places I've never been. Forty-one. I've crossed none off. What do you think?
dlg.elara.list.r0: Together! The sea, from a boat. I'm circling it. I'm packing a sandwich. I'm already packing!
dlg.elara.list.r1: A new one! Forty-two! Oh, you've made my whole week. Don't tell Dr. Penn.
dlg.elara.list.r2: You promise? ...I'll write it down. In ink. And knit you a sock for the journey.
dlg.ione.shelf.0: At the back of the library stands a shelf of books, each with a small slip of paper tucked in. None has a name.
dlg.ione.shelf.1: Books I set aside for people who never came. I couldn't bear to shelve them. What would you do?
dlg.ione.shelf.r0: Take one. ...For someone who'll come. Yes. That's what they were waiting for.
dlg.ione.shelf.r1: Aloud? I haven't heard these in a human voice for years. Go slowly. Please.
dlg.ione.shelf.r2: A note. In a book nobody's opened. ...It's the kindest thing anyone's done for this shelf.
dlg.marcus.planks.ask.0: Ten planks for the hall roof. Oak if you have it. I'd ask someone else, but you hold a ladder well.
dlg.marcus.planks.ask.1: Ten planks, then. I'll measure twice. You'll fetch once.
dlg.marcus.planks.remind.0: Ten planks of wood for the hall roof. I'll measure twice.
dlg.marcus.planks.turnin.0: Ten planks. Good grain. Straight. Thank you, [player]. The roof's a bit less nearly fixed.
dlg.odalys.elder.ask.0: Three bunches of elderflower for the clinic. Fresh. For a tonic. I'd gather it myself, but I've a waiting room.
dlg.odalys.elder.ask.1: Three. Fresh. I'll prescribe you a cup of tea in return.
dlg.odalys.elder.remind.0: Three elderflowers for the tonic. Fresh. I'll note them in the ledger.
dlg.odalys.elder.turnin.0: Elderflower. Fresh, and in good order. Thank you, [player]. The clinic is in your debt, and I dislike debts.
dlg.felix.bait.ask.0: Short on bait. Five, if you've them. The tide's turning, and so's my luck.
dlg.felix.bait.ask.1: Five bait. I'll catch something this big. Bigger, by tomorrow.
dlg.felix.bait.remind.0: Five bait for the dawn. The tide's waiting.
dlg.felix.bait.turnin.0: Bait. Five. Perfect. Thank you, [player]. I'll fish for you. The first one's yours.
dlg.dorian.basket.ask.0: A basket. Three mushrooms. It's for the forest. Don't ask. Please.
dlg.dorian.basket.ask.1: Three. Bring them. I'll say thank you later. Quietly.
dlg.dorian.basket.turnin.0: Mushrooms. Three. Good. Thank you, [player]. The forest says so too.
dlg.elara.wool.ask.0: I'm out of wool! Two skeins, if you can. The scarf is at the length of a dog. It wants to be a horse.
dlg.elara.wool.ask.1: Two wool! I'll knit you something. A sock, probably.
dlg.elara.wool.remind.0: Two wool for the scarf. It's already the length of a dog.
dlg.elara.wool.turnin.0: Wool! Soft and warm. Thank you, [player]! The scarf will now reach the next village.
dlg.ione.pearl.ask.0: A pearl. One. For the reading room. I keep one in my favorite book, and it's tarnished. I'd like a new one.
dlg.ione.pearl.ask.1: A pearl. Small, quiet, and round. I'll set a book aside for you.
dlg.ione.pearl.remind.0: One pearl for the reading room. I'll set a book aside.
dlg.ione.pearl.turnin.0: A pearl. Perfect. Quiet and round. Thank you, [player]. It's going in the front of a very old book.
dlg.react.marcus.fall.d.0: Fall. The oak's in and the coops need roofs. I've cleared the bench and a calendar.
dlg.react.marcus.harvest.d.0: First harvest. A good crop wants a good shed. Come by when you're ready.
dlg.react.marcus.bram.d.0: Bram fixed a repair and said 'Good enough'. It's the longest sentence he's said in a week.
dlg.react.odalys.winter.d.0: Winter. Chilblains, coughs and gloves. Wear all three of the last. Doctor's orders.
dlg.react.odalys.harvest.d.0: A first harvest. Wash your hands before you eat it. Then eat it. Enthusiastically.
dlg.react.odalys.skill.d.0: Your farming has improved. The village's health improves with it. I'll note it in the ledger.
dlg.react.felix.summer.d.0: Summer's come. The beach is full of people who think fish come when called.
dlg.react.felix.harvest.d.0: A first harvest! Fine. Now try fishing. It's the same, with more waiting.
dlg.react.felix.skill.d.0: Your fishing's getting better. The pond noticed. So did I. You should've seen the other one.
dlg.react.dorian.fall.d.0: Fall. The best mushrooms. I'll show you. Not today. Soon.
dlg.react.dorian.harvest.d.0: First harvest. Hm. Good. The soil likes you.
dlg.react.dorian.skill.d.0: You forage well now. I saw. A mushroom was on your step. Not me. The forest.
dlg.react.elara.spring.d.0: Spring! Sneezes, sprains and optimism. I've put the kettle on for all of them!
dlg.react.elara.harvest.d.0: Your first harvest! I'm knitting a very small basket cozy. For luck.
dlg.react.elara.skill.d.0: Your farming's improving! I can tell by the callouses. Keep your socks on, hands and feet!
dlg.react.ione.winter.d.0: Winter. I've set aside a very long book. It's yours, if the snow stays.
dlg.react.ione.harvest.d.0: A first harvest. I've a book on preserving. It's mostly poetry. You'll love it.
dlg.react.ione.skill.d.0: You forage well. I set aside a field guide. It has lovely drawings of mushrooms. Dorian helped.
dlg.social.marcus.joke.great.0: Hm. A good one. I'll tell it at the bench. Bram will say nothing. It'll be perfect.
dlg.social.marcus.joke.good.0: Ha. That's funny. Dry, like good timber.
dlg.social.marcus.joke.flop.0: A joke? ...Ah. I was measuring. Say it again, slower.
dlg.social.marcus.compliment.great.0: That's kind. I'll carry it around for a week. Like a good pencil.
dlg.social.marcus.compliment.good.0: Thank you. I'll note it. Quietly.
dlg.social.marcus.compliment.flop.0: Oh. Hm. That's a lot of weather for one sentence.
dlg.social.marcus.advice.great.0: Advice? Gladly. Never rush a cut. Never cut in anger. Never throw away the offcut.
dlg.social.marcus.advice.good.0: My advice: measure twice. Then ask someone else to measure once.
dlg.social.marcus.advice.flop.0: Advice? From me? I mostly say 'Measure twice'. I'll see what else is there.
dlg.social.marcus.tease.great.0: Ha. Cheeky. A crooked joke on a straight board. I'll allow it.
dlg.social.marcus.tease.good.0: Hm. Funny. A very small chisel to the ribs.
dlg.social.marcus.tease.flop.0: Teasing? In my shop? ...I'll take it as affection. Cautiously.
dlg.social.odalys.joke.great.0: A joke. Clinical timing, good delivery. I may prescribe it to a patient.
dlg.social.odalys.joke.good.0: Ha. Dry. I approve. The laugh is medicinal.
dlg.social.odalys.joke.flop.0: Was that a joke? ...Oh. Yes. I was reading a chart. Do continue.
dlg.social.odalys.compliment.great.0: A compliment. How unusual. I'll have to take my pulse.
dlg.social.odalys.compliment.good.0: Thank you. I'll file it under 'Unexpected'.
dlg.social.odalys.compliment.flop.0: Oh. Hm. That's... kind. I'm not sure where to put my hands.
dlg.social.odalys.advice.great.0: Advice? Ask. Sleep eight hours, eat a vegetable, and call me if your ears itch.
dlg.social.odalys.advice.good.0: My advice: soup, sleep and silence. In that order.
dlg.social.odalys.advice.flop.0: Advice from me? I'll prescribe a nap. It's the only thing I know for certain.
dlg.social.odalys.tease.great.0: Ha! Cheeky. I'll note the tone. And the posture. It's excellent.
dlg.social.odalys.tease.good.0: Hm. Clever. A diagnosis I'll consider.
dlg.social.odalys.tease.flop.0: Teasing a doctor? Bold. ...I'll prescribe you a very long lecture.
dlg.social.felix.joke.great.0: Ha! That's a good one. I'll steal it for the next story. It'll grow.
dlg.social.felix.joke.good.0: Ha. That's the right size of funny. Nets, not trawlers.
dlg.social.felix.joke.flop.0: A joke? ...Ah. I was watching a float. Say it again.
dlg.social.felix.compliment.great.0: That's kind. I'll tell the fish. They'll be unmoved.
dlg.social.felix.compliment.good.0: Thank you. It's a good line. I'll cast it later.
dlg.social.felix.compliment.flop.0: Oh. Hm. A bit much for a man in rubber boots.
dlg.social.felix.advice.great.0: Advice? Gladly. Patience, bait and a good hat. In reverse order, if it's raining.
dlg.social.felix.advice.good.0: My advice: sit. Then sit some more. Then catch something, maybe.
dlg.social.felix.advice.flop.0: Advice? From me? I say 'wait'. It seems to work.
dlg.social.felix.tease.great.0: Ha! Cheeky. A fine one. This big. Bigger now.
dlg.social.felix.tease.good.0: Hm. A bit of bait on the hook. I like it.
dlg.social.felix.tease.flop.0: Teasing? ...I'll let that go. Like a small fish.
dlg.social.dorian.joke.great.0: ...Ha. That was good. I'll tell the moss. It'll say nothing.
dlg.social.dorian.joke.flop.0: A joke? ...Oh. I was listening to a bird. Again?
dlg.social.dorian.compliment.great.0: ...Thank you. I'll keep that. In my pocket. With the mushroom.
dlg.social.dorian.compliment.good.0: Oh. Thank you. It's quiet. I like it.
dlg.social.dorian.compliment.flop.0: Hm. That's a lot of words at once.
dlg.social.dorian.advice.great.0: Advice? Look under old roots. Walk slowly. Don't talk to mushrooms. They're shy.
dlg.social.dorian.advice.good.0: My advice: stay quiet. It's all there is.
dlg.social.dorian.advice.flop.0: Advice from me? ...I mostly stand very still. It works.
dlg.social.dorian.tease.great.0: ...Ha. I'd say something back. I'm thinking. I'll tell you in the spring.
dlg.social.dorian.tease.flop.0: Teasing? ...I'll go and look at a tree.
dlg.social.elara.joke.great.0: Ha! Oh, that's a good one! I'm using it on Dr. Penn. She'll frown, then smile!
dlg.social.elara.joke.good.0: Ha! Funny! I'll put it on the waiting room wall!
dlg.social.elara.joke.flop.0: Wait, was that a joke? ...Oh! Ha! Sorry! I was counting stitches.
dlg.social.elara.compliment.great.0: Oh, you're too kind! I'm blushing in two colors of wool!
dlg.social.elara.compliment.good.0: Aw, thank you! That's very sweet!
dlg.social.elara.compliment.flop.0: Oh! Er. Thanks! I wasn't ready. I'm holding a needle. It's awkward.
dlg.social.elara.advice.great.0: Advice! I love advice! Keep your socks on. Sleep. Don't tell Dr. Penn I said it.
dlg.social.elara.advice.good.0: My advice: laugh, rest, knit. In any order.
dlg.social.elara.advice.flop.0: Advice? Hm. I'd rather find out by getting it wrong. It's how I learned everything.
dlg.social.elara.tease.great.0: Oh, you wicked thing! I love it! I'll knit you a very small, very pointed hat!
dlg.social.elara.tease.good.0: Ha! Cheeky! I'll get you back with a very long scarf!
dlg.social.elara.tease.flop.0: Teasing? ...Hm. I'll decide if it was funny later. With tea.
dlg.social.ione.joke.great.0: Oh. That's lovely. I'll file it under 'Humor, Gentle'. Right next to poetry.
dlg.social.ione.joke.good.0: Ha. Quiet and clever. Like a good footnote.
dlg.social.ione.joke.flop.0: Was that a joke? ...Oh. I was reading the last line. Again, please.
dlg.social.ione.compliment.great.0: Thank you. That's the kindest line I've heard all day. I'll set it aside.
dlg.social.ione.compliment.good.0: Oh. That's kind. I'll remember it.
dlg.social.ione.compliment.flop.0: Oh. Hm. That's a lot of warmth for a quiet room.
dlg.social.ione.advice.great.0: Advice? I'd suggest reading the first page and the last. Then deciding if you care.
dlg.social.ione.advice.good.0: My advice: a good book, a warm lamp, and no hurry.
dlg.social.ione.advice.flop.0: Advice? I mostly recommend books. It's usually the same thing.
dlg.social.ione.tease.great.0: Oh, you wicked reader! I'll set aside a very dull book for you.
dlg.social.ione.tease.good.0: Hm. Gentle. A footnote with teeth.
dlg.social.ione.tease.flop.0: Teasing the librarian? ...I'll keep that in mind, quietly, in the margins.
dlg.marcus.joinery.d.0: A good joint? Two pieces that agree. No nails, no glue, just patience.
dlg.marcus.joinery.d.1: It takes a year to learn. I learned it in two. Don't tell my father.
dlg.odalys.remedies.d.0: A remedy? One bowl of soup, one hour of sunshine, and an unreasonable amount of cheese.
dlg.felix.tide.d.0: The tide? In at six, out at noon. A fish this big comes at four.
dlg.felix.tide.d.1: Don't write that down. I'll deny it.
dlg.dorian.mushrooms.d.0: Mushrooms. Gills, caps, rings. Don't eat the shy ones.
dlg.dorian.mushrooms.d.1: Check under the oak leaves. Few do.
dlg.elara.knitting.d.0: A scarf! Or a blanket. Or a very ambitious sock. It changes by the hour!
dlg.elara.knitting.d.1: I'll finish it by spring. Or summer. It's a scarf with ambitions.
dlg.ione.book.d.0: A book? I set something aside for you. It's small and a little odd.
dlg.ione.book.d.1: You'll like it. It's about someone who read a lot and learned to listen.
dlg.felix.spring.1.0: Spring tide. The shallows are full of nonsense and minnows. I love every second.
dlg.felix.spring.2.0: Cold water, warm sun. The perch don't know what to think. Neither do I.
dlg.felix.spring.3.0: Caught a trout this big last week. Bigger, now that I've thought about it.
dlg.felix.summer.1.0: Summer. The beach is full of folk who think fish come when called. I let them try.
dlg.felix.summer.2.0: Long evenings, slow lines. A man could fish till he forgets what he wanted.
dlg.felix.summer.3.0: My birthday's in summer. I fish. Nothing grand. If the tuna comes, I'll thank it.
dlg.felix.fall.1.0: Fall runs. The river's thick with them. You can almost hear them thinking.
dlg.felix.fall.2.0: Cooler water, hungrier fish. A good month for patience and a warm hat.
dlg.felix.fall.3.0: I like fall dawn best. Mist on the pond, nobody about. Just me and the line.
dlg.felix.winter.1.0: Winter. The pond's quiet. The beach is quieter. I cast anyway. It's company.
dlg.felix.winter.2.0: Cold hands, slow tide. A flask of something warm and a long story. That's winter.
dlg.felix.winter.3.0: The sturgeon sleeps in winter. I tip my hat to it each morning. It never answers.
dlg.felix.mon.1.0: Monday. Fresh catch, fresh gossip. The first goes faster than the second.
dlg.felix.tue.1.0: Tuesday. Wren's shut, so I sit with my own cooking. A sad fish, but mine.
dlg.felix.wed.1.0: Wednesday. Marcus is sawing something quiet. I can hear it from the dock. It's soothing.
dlg.felix.thu.1.0: Thursday. Stall's shut. I'm on the pond. If you find me, bring bait and an opinion.
dlg.felix.fri.1.0: Friday. Everyone wants fish for the weekend. I've named the good ones. They're not for sale.
dlg.felix.sat.1.0: Saturday. Market day. The fish and I attract a crowd. It's mostly curious cats.
dlg.felix.sun.1.0: Sunday. The tide table's my church. I read it slowly and take the day off.
dlg.felix.sunny.1.0: Fine day. Fish dive deep when it's bright. I'm not offended. I'm patient.
dlg.felix.sunny.2.0: Sun on the water. Looks like a thousand silver coins. All of them lies.
dlg.felix.rain.2.0: Rain's the best time. The fish forget to be careful. So do I, a little.
dlg.felix.rain.3.0: Wet hat, warm flask, steady line. If a day could be a person, it'd be this one.
dlg.felix.storm.1.0: Storm on the water. I tie the boat twice and talk it down. It listens.
dlg.felix.storm.2.0: Lightning makes the whole pond flinch. The fish go quiet. I respect that.
dlg.felix.snow.1.0: Snow on the pier. The gulls look offended. I tell them I'm sorry.
dlg.felix.snow.2.0: Everything's quiet under snow. Even the tide sounds like it's whispering.
dlg.felix.wind.1.0: Wind on the beach. The line sings. A good sound, a bad cast.
dlg.felix.wind.2.0: Gusts blow the bait off the hook. I'm told it's a metaphor. I'm told a lot.
dlg.felix.morning.1.0: Dawn's the best hour. The water's still deciding whether to be awake.
dlg.felix.morning.2.0: Early light. First cast. First hope. Nothing's wasted yet.
dlg.felix.midday.1.0: Midday. The stall's closing, the fish are thinking, and I'm eating a sandwich the size of a catfish.
dlg.felix.midday.2.0: Slow hour. A good one for mending and lies.
dlg.felix.evening.1.0: Evening tide. The light goes copper. A man could cry if he'd not promised not to.
dlg.felix.evening.2.0: Sun's down on the pond. The frogs take over. They know the whole tune.
dlg.felix.late.1.0: Late. The moon does strange things to the pond fish. I just watch.
dlg.felix.late.2.0: Night line. Quiet, cold and clever. The best fish are the ones that don't show.
dlg.felix.here.1.0: Mind the nets. They look like they're sleeping. They're plotting.
dlg.felix.here.2.0: Wren calls this "Felix's stool". I call it "the stool". Wren's right. It remembers me.
dlg.felix.fr.1.0: You're getting the hang of this, [player]. The fish are starting to like you.
dlg.felix.fr.2.0: You should've seen the other one. Last week's. It was this big. Bigger now.
dlg.felix.fr.3.0: Take my spot tomorrow. I've a feeling about the tide. It's usually wrong. Yours won't be.
dlg.felix.fr.4.0: Fishing's mostly sitting. Good company makes the sitting count.
dlg.felix.fr.5.0: I've fished alone a long time. It's nicer with two lines in the water.
dlg.felix.cl.1.0: You've the patience of a heron. That's the best compliment I've got.
dlg.felix.cl.2.0: Dawn's the best hour. It's better with someone to say so. I'm saying so.
dlg.felix.cl.3.0: Tilda says I smile more since you arrived. I told her it's the tide. She didn't buy it.
dlg.felix.cl.4.0: I told the sturgeon about you. It stayed on the bottom. A good sign.
dlg.felix.cl.5.0: The pond has a secret or two. I'll share one. Not today. Soon.
dlg.felix.co.1.0: I fished alone my whole life. This is better. Don't tell the fish. They're very sensitive.
dlg.felix.co.2.0: You're the best thing I've pulled up. And I've pulled up a boot with a clock in it.
dlg.felix.co.3.0: If I wrote you a letter, it'd be about the one that got away. It'd run to eleven pages.
dlg.felix.co.4.0: Thank you, [player]. That's the whole tide table. I put your name next to dawn.
dlg.felix.lonely.1.0: Quiet pond. Quiet stall. I talked to a minnow. It had no opinions.
dlg.felix.tired.1.0: Up before the gulls and still behind the tide. A long one.
dlg.felix.delighted.1.0: I caught one this big! Then I let it go, and it waved. I'm fairly sure.
dlg.felix.mischief.1.0: I told Tilda the fish were free today. Watch her face when she checks the sign.
