dlg.piper.festival.summer.day.0: The Tidewatch! I'm singing the shanty from a very small boat! It rocks! So does the song!
dlg.piper.festival.summer.after.0: The boat's still rocking, and so's my voice! Felix cried at the third verse! The fish stayed silent! Critics!
dlg.piper.festival.fall.before.0: Harvest Fair tomorrow! I wrote a song about pumpkins! It has a bridge! The pumpkins have not responded!
dlg.piper.festival.fall.day.0: The Fair! I'm playing the pumpkin song! The pumpkins are listening! At least they're not leaving!
dlg.piper.festival.fall.after.0: Pumpkin song, a hit! A ribbon on the stool, and one on my hat! I'm calling it a chart-topper!
dlg.piper.festival.winter.before.0: Lantern Feast tomorrow! I wrote a quiet song! It's actually quiet! I'm as shocked as you are!
dlg.piper.festival.winter.day.0: The Feast! I'm playing the quiet one tonight! It's the only song I've written where nobody has to clap!
dlg.piper.festival.winter.after.0: The quiet song worked! Nobody clapped, and everyone stayed! It's my best review!
dlg.marcus.festival.spring.before.0: Blossom Day tomorrow. I built the dance floor. Planed it flat. Dorian helped. Don't ask what he said.
dlg.marcus.festival.spring.day.0: Blossom Day. The floor's level. Dance on it. Please. I measured it twice for you.
dlg.marcus.festival.spring.after.0: The floor held. Nobody fell. A few danced hard. That's a good result for a floor.
dlg.marcus.festival.summer.before.0: Tidewatch tomorrow. I built the judges' bench. It's oak. It's too heavy. Nobody will sit.
dlg.marcus.festival.summer.day.0: Tidewatch. The bench is oak, and the judges are small. It still holds. A good bench.
dlg.marcus.festival.summer.after.0: The bench held all afternoon. Nobody noticed. That's the best praise for a bench.
dlg.marcus.festival.fall.before.0: Harvest Fair tomorrow. I built forty stalls. They're straight. Tilda wants them crooked. We negotiated.
dlg.marcus.festival.fall.day.0: The Fair. Forty stalls, all level. Tilda stands on one. Fine. That's what it's for.
dlg.marcus.festival.fall.after.0: Forty stalls, forty clean planks. Tomorrow I'll take them down. Today they're still a village.
dlg.marcus.festival.winter.before.0: Lantern Feast tomorrow. I built the long table. It seats the whole village. It took eleven planks.
dlg.marcus.festival.winter.day.0: The Feast. The table's set. Eleven planks, everyone seated. That's a good day's work.
dlg.marcus.festival.winter.after.0: The table's still warm. Everyone's gone home. It held the village. That's all it's for.
dlg.odalys.festival.spring.before.0: Blossom Day tomorrow. I advise sleep and moderate dancing. Elara advises the opposite. We'll compromise.
dlg.odalys.festival.spring.day.0: Blossom Day. I'm on duty, near the cider, for sprained ankles. Dance. I'll be nearby. Quietly pleased.
dlg.odalys.festival.spring.after.0: Three sprained ankles, one broken hat. A good Blossom Day, medically speaking.
dlg.odalys.festival.summer.before.0: Tidewatch tomorrow. I advise sunscreen. Felix advises optimism. We'll bring both.
dlg.odalys.festival.summer.day.0: The Tidewatch. I'm on the sand with a bandage kit. So far, one fish bite. Mine. It was an accident.
dlg.odalys.festival.summer.after.0: One sunburn, three splinters, no major incidents. The contest was a medical success.
dlg.odalys.festival.fall.before.0: Harvest Fair tomorrow. I advise small portions. Tilda advises large ones. I'll supervise, reluctantly.
dlg.odalys.festival.fall.day.0: The Fair. I'm checking the cider. It's safe. It's also strong. Drink water between cups.
dlg.odalys.festival.fall.after.0: The Fair left two stomachaches and one very happy cat. Medical staff are satisfied.
dlg.odalys.festival.winter.before.0: Lantern Feast tomorrow. I advise warm layers and shared soup. Elara knitted forty mittens. Take a pair.
dlg.odalys.festival.winter.day.0: The Feast. I'm serving soup for the hall. Take the warm bowl. That's a prescription.
dlg.odalys.festival.winter.after.0: The Feast left everyone warm and sleepy. I closed the clinic early. It's allowed. Occasionally.
dlg.felix.festival.spring.before.0: Blossom Day tomorrow. I'm bringing a fish to the dance. It's for the table. It's not for dancing.
dlg.felix.festival.spring.day.0: Blossom Day. I danced once. The fish didn't. It watched from the bucket. Disapproving.
dlg.felix.festival.spring.after.0: My feet ache. The fish is fine. We both learned something about dancing. It isn't for us.
dlg.felix.festival.summer.before.0: The Tidewatch is tomorrow. I'm in charge. I've never been in charge. I've written it on a board.
dlg.felix.festival.summer.day.0: The Tidewatch. I'm in charge, with chalk. Everyone's a winner. It's my rule. I made it up this morning.
dlg.felix.festival.summer.after.0: The board's smudged, the fish are free, and everyone's a winner. That was the plan. It worked.
dlg.felix.festival.fall.before.0: Harvest Fair tomorrow. I'm bringing a fish pie. It's Tilda's recipe and my fish. We argued about salt.
dlg.felix.festival.fall.day.0: The Fair. The fish pie's on the table. Take a slice. It's mostly fish. It's mostly good.
dlg.felix.festival.fall.after.0: The pie's gone. The salt argument continues. Tilda says she won. She did.
dlg.felix.festival.winter.before.0: Lantern Feast tomorrow. I'm bringing a lantern shaped like a fish. It looks like a boot. It's loved.
dlg.felix.festival.winter.day.0: The Feast. The fish-lantern glows. It looks like a boot. A very warm boot. I'm proud.
dlg.felix.festival.winter.after.0: The lantern burned until dawn. The boot-fish is on my shelf. It'll be back next year.
dlg.dorian.festival.spring.before.0: ...Blossom Day tomorrow. Marcus asked me to help build the floor. I said yes. Quietly.
dlg.dorian.festival.spring.day.0: ...Blossom Day. I'm at the edge of the crowd. It's loud. It's good. I'll stay a while.
dlg.dorian.festival.spring.after.0: ...The blossoms fell in the forest too. I kept one. It's on my shelf. With the pinecone.
dlg.dorian.festival.summer.before.0: ...The Tidewatch tomorrow. Felix asked me to hold the board. I said yes. Silent hands.
dlg.dorian.festival.summer.day.0: ...The Tidewatch. I hold the board. The crowd's loud. Felix's voice is louder. It's fine.
dlg.dorian.festival.summer.after.0: ...The board's back with Felix. My arms are tired. The beach was warm. A good day. Quiet at the end.
dlg.dorian.festival.fall.before.0: ...The Fair tomorrow. I'm bringing mushrooms. Small ones. For the stew. Don't tell Dr. Penn.
dlg.dorian.festival.fall.day.0: ...The Fair. The mushrooms are in the stew. It's safe. Dr. Penn checked. Twice.
dlg.dorian.festival.fall.after.0: ...The stew's gone. The mushrooms were praised. I'm not used to that. It's strange. Pleasant.
dlg.dorian.festival.winter.before.0: ...The Feast tomorrow. I made a lantern. It's a plain one. A stick, some paper, a candle.
dlg.dorian.festival.winter.day.0: ...The Feast. My lantern's the plain one. Third from the end. It's warm. That's enough.
dlg.dorian.festival.winter.after.0: ...The lanterns went out. The forest was quiet. I walked home in the dark. It was kind.
dlg.elara.festival.spring.before.0: Blossom Day tomorrow! I knitted a hundred tiny blossoms! They're for the garlands! I ran out of pink!
dlg.elara.festival.spring.day.0: BLOSSOM DAY! The garlands have my blossoms! Every one! Some are slightly crooked! That's the charm!
dlg.elara.festival.spring.after.0: Petals everywhere, and wool in my hair! The best Blossom Day! I'll knit it into a scarf!
dlg.elara.festival.summer.before.0: The Tidewatch tomorrow! I'm knitting little flags for the boats! They're very small! They're very proud!
dlg.elara.festival.summer.day.0: The Tidewatch! Every boat has a flag! Mine's the red one! It's very windy! Hold your hat!
dlg.elara.festival.summer.after.0: The flags are sandy and loved! One flew off with a seagull! It's the happiest flag in the world!
dlg.elara.festival.fall.before.0: Harvest Fair tomorrow! I knitted a pumpkin cozy! It's for a real pumpkin! It's a big pumpkin!
dlg.elara.festival.fall.day.0: The Fair! The pumpkin has a cozy! It won first place! Technically it's the cozy that won! I'm so proud!
dlg.elara.festival.fall.after.0: The cozy's still on the pumpkin! It refuses to leave! I'll knit it a second one! It's a pumpkin's right!
dlg.elara.festival.winter.before.0: Lantern Feast tomorrow! I knitted forty mittens for the line! There are forty-one people! I'm so sorry about the last one!
dlg.elara.festival.winter.day.0: The Feast! Mittens for everyone! Dr. Penn's pair is the blue one! She pretended she didn't need them!
dlg.elara.festival.winter.after.0: Forty mittens, all gone! Dr. Penn kept hers on all night! She'd deny it! I saw it!
dlg.ione.festival.spring.before.0: Blossom Day tomorrow. The library will be open until noon. Then we'll all go and be silly together.
dlg.ione.festival.spring.day.0: Blossom Day. I closed early. Hazel and I are in the square. It's loud. It's good. Come say hello.
dlg.ione.festival.spring.after.0: A blossom landed on the desk this morning. I've left it there. It's a very good bookmark.
dlg.ione.festival.summer.before.0: The Tidewatch tomorrow. I packed a book and a thermos. The book's for the shade. The thermos is for Felix.
dlg.ione.festival.summer.day.0: The Tidewatch. I'm on the beach with a book. I'm not reading it. I'm watching Felix be happy.
dlg.ione.festival.summer.after.0: Sand in the thermos, sand in the book. A fine summer day. I'll shelve it under 'Good'.
dlg.ione.festival.fall.before.0: The Harvest Fair tomorrow. The library's contributing a ribbon. It's labeled 'Best Quiet Entry'. Hazel's nominated.
dlg.ione.festival.fall.day.0: The Fair. Hazel won 'Best Quiet Entry'. She's pretending she didn't. I'm very proud, quietly.
dlg.ione.festival.fall.after.0: Hazel put the ribbon on her desk. She said it's a coincidence. It's labeled and framed.
dlg.ione.festival.winter.before.0: The Lantern Feast tomorrow. I'm reading the first line of a very old story aloud. It's short. It's kind.
dlg.ione.festival.winter.day.0: The Feast. I read the old story aloud. The hall listened. That was lovely. Please sit. Have soup.
dlg.ione.festival.winter.after.0: The story's back on its shelf. It's warm to the touch. The books enjoyed the Feast, too.
event.festival_winter_lanterns.0: Everyone has a lantern, dear. Hold it up. Don't light it yet. Wait for the bell.
event.festival_winter_lanterns.1: (One lantern each.) (A small light, and a small wish.) Please keep yours private.
event.festival_winter_lanterns.2: It's this big. The wish, I mean. I'll say no more. The lantern will do the telling.
event.festival_winter_lanterns.3: Now. Together, and slowly. Let them go. The dark will do the rest.
dlg.juno.upgrade.ready.1.0: Your tool's done! I polished it twice! Twice! Come and take it before I polish it a third time!
dlg.juno.upgrade.ready.2.0: It's ready, it's ready! I labeled the handle 'Yours (Better)'! Go on, grab it!
dlg.juno.upgrade.wait.1.0: I'm working on your tool! It's in the vise! It's very comfortable! Come back soon!
dlg.juno.upgrade.wait.2.0: Don't peek! Okay, peek a little. It's going to be shiny. Like, embarrassingly shiny!
dlg.bram.upgrade.ready.1.0: Hm. Your tool's done. Better than before. Collect it.
dlg.bram.upgrade.ready.2.0: Hm. Finished. The edge is true. Take it.
dlg.bram.upgrade.wait.1.0: Hm. Still on the anvil. Not ready. Patience.
dlg.tilda.merchant.1.0: The traveling merchant's in town, dear. I'm watching his prices very politely.
dlg.tilda.merchant.2.0: A stranger with a cart, dear. He sells things I don't. I'm not jealous. Much.
dlg.tilda.shipped.1.0: I hear you've been shipping things, dear. The valley notices a busy farm.
dlg.tilda.shipped.2.0: A hundred shipments, dear! The slate has a new column, and it only has your name.
dlg.wren.gold.rich.0: Heard you're doing well, my darling. Drinks are on you. Kidding. Mostly. Sit, anyway.
dlg.wren.gold.poor.0: You look skint, my darling. Have a pickle. It's free. It's also a meal.
dlg.marcus.rare.4.0: Every plank I've ever cut has a name. This one's Gerald. Don't ask. Gerald is straight.
dlg.odalys.rare.4.0: I don't sleep much. I'm told that's irony. I call it a long shift with good company.
dlg.felix.rare.4.0: I named my favorite fish Tuesday. She's been gone for years. Every Tuesday, I look for her.
dlg.dorian.rare.4.0: ...There's an owl by my hut. We don't speak. We have an understanding. It's perfect.
dlg.elara.rare.4.0: I once knitted a scarf so long it went around the clinic twice! Dr. Penn used it as a hallway!
dlg.ione.rare.4.0: A book once fell off the shelf exactly when I needed it. I've never moved it. It's still there.
dlg.gazette.head.quiet.0: A QUIET WEEK, A WARM VILLAGE
dlg.gazette.head.library.0: LIBRARY REPORTS A GOOD WEEK FOR SILENCE
dlg.gazette.head.summer.0: HEAT WAVE: VILLAGE BLAMES THE ANVIL
dlg.gazette.head.festival.0: FESTIVAL NEAR: THE VILLAGE IS ALREADY PRACTICING
dlg.gazette.news.stool.0: A Saloon spokesperson denies the stool is haunted. It is merely opinionated.
dlg.gazette.news.kettle.0: The library's kettle was seen boiling, unattended. Authorities suspect Ione.
dlg.gazette.news.hook.0: A very large fish was reported near the pond. Its size has grown since Tuesday.
dlg.gazette.news.wreath.0: A small cat was seen entering the general store. It left with a ribbon and no explanation.
dlg.gazette.news.owl.0: An owl by the forest hut has reportedly befriended its neighbor. Neither has commented.
dlg.gazette.news.sock.0: A single sock was found on the clinic roof. Elara says it is a flag.
dlg.gazette.news.plank.0: A plank named Gerald won a local straightness award. Nobody asked to see the certificate.
dlg.gazette.news.pickle.0: The saloon's pickle supply is stable. Officials urge calm, and napkins.
dlg.gazette.news.song.0: A new song is circulating. Its chorus has been confirmed to rhyme, mostly.
dlg.gazette.news.forge.0: The forge has installed a label on everything. Residents report feeling very organized.
dlg.gazette.news.clinic.0: The clinic handed out forty mittens this week. Dr. Penn says that is within reason.
dlg.gazette.news.bench.0: A bench on the village green has been declared the best seat in town by several people who sat on it.
dlg.gazette.news.blossom.0: Garlands are being hung early. The village is feeling optimistic and slightly sticky.
dlg.gazette.news.tide.0: The tide remains reliable. The fishing contest has not yet been told.
dlg.gazette.news.pie.0: Pumpkin pies appear on every windowsill. Neighbors are keeping score.
dlg.gazette.news.lantern.0: Paper lanterns are on order. The general store reports it ran out of candles twice.
dlg.gazette.news.puddle.0: A puddle on the main road has been named by local children. The name is not printable.
dlg.gazette.news.laundry.0: Washing lines are full. The village smells like warm cloth and good decisions.
dlg.gazette.news.wren.0: Wren was heard laughing at her own joke. Witnesses say it was a good one.
dlg.gazette.news.hazel.0: Hazel was spotted reading in the open air. She was not alone, and the book was not either.
dlg.gazette.news.bram.0: Bram forged something small and kind this week. He declined to say what.
dlg.gazette.news.tilda.0: Tilda's slate now lists [player] under 'Reliable'. It is in capital letters.
dlg.gazette.news.juno.0: Juno labeled her lunch this week. The label said 'Lunch (Eaten)'.
dlg.gazette.news.piper.0: Piper debuted a new song at the saloon. The room clapped, then asked her to play it again.
dlg.gazette.news.feud.0: The pie dispute continues. Both bakers deny it is a dispute.
dlg.gazette.news.notes.0: Anonymous notes keep appearing in mailboxes. They are all very kind.
dlg.gazette.farm.generic.0: [farm] has a good reputation in the valley. The scarecrow is rumored to be proud.
dlg.gazette.farm.crops.0: Rows are looking neat at [farm]. A passing neighbor called them 'well-behaved'.
dlg.gazette.farm.animals.0: The animals at [farm] are reportedly well fed and rather smug about it.
dlg.gazette.farm.shipped.0: [player] has been shipping steadily. The valley's crates have never been fuller.
dlg.gazette.farm.shipped100.0: Over a hundred shipments from [farm]. The valley calls it 'dependable', which is high praise here.
dlg.gazette.farm.rich.0: Rumor says [player] is doing well. The saloon has politely moved the good stool closer.
dlg.gazette.farm.upgrade.0: A tool from [farm] is at the forge. Bram says it is coming along. Juno says it is shiny.
dlg.gazette.farm.upgradeready.0: A finished tool awaits [player] at the forge. It has been polished more than once.
dlg.gazette.weather.sunny.0: Sun, mostly. Light breeze. Hats optional, sunscreen advised by Dr. Penn.
dlg.gazette.weather.rain.0: Rain, steady. Good for crops, bad for hair. Umbrellas will be debated.
dlg.gazette.weather.storm.0: Storm possible. The blacksmith advises staying in. The saloon advises staying in, too, with a drink.
dlg.gazette.weather.snow.0: Snow likely. Lanterns lit early. Mittens, by order of Elara, mandatory.
dlg.gazette.weather.wind.0: Windy. Hold your hats and your opinions.
dlg.gazette.weather.spring.0: Spring: mild, damp, hopeful. Mud level: moderate.
dlg.gazette.weather.summer.0: Summer: warm, bright, a little loud. Shade is in high demand.
dlg.gazette.weather.fall.0: Fall: crisp, golden, smells of cinnamon and other people's secrets.
dlg.gazette.weather.winter.0: Winter: cold, clear, quiet. A bowl of soup is recommended.
dlg.gazette.class.stool.0: WANTED: A level stool. Contact the saloon. Do not tell the stool.
dlg.gazette.class.book.0: FOUND: One library book, seven years overdue. Return at your leisure. The library has waited this long.
dlg.gazette.class.mittens.0: FREE: Forty mittens, various colors. Ask at the clinic. One is for you.
dlg.gazette.class.plank.0: FOR SALE: A very straight plank. Name: Gerald. Not for sale. Gerald is just visiting.
dlg.gazette.class.song.0: SEEKING: A rhyme for 'Wetherell'. Apply at the saloon. No refunds.
dlg.gazette.class.slate.0: NOTICE: The general store slate is not a forum. It has opinions anyway.
dlg.gazette.class.fish.0: LOST: One fish, about this big. Last seen on a Tuesday. If found, please tell Felix gently.
dlg.gazette.class.pickle.0: WANTED: A friend with a good pickle recipe. Reply to the saloon.
photo.hint: Photo mode: Enter or F8 takes a photo, 1-6 emote, Tab next villager, 0 clear, Esc leave
dlg.wren.bark.festival.1.0: Festival day! Everyone's my friend until the cider runs out.
dlg.hazel.bark.festival.1.0: (A festival. Loud, bright, and surprisingly pleasant.)
dlg.bram.bark.festival.1.0: Hm. Festival. Good day for small iron.
dlg.tilda.bark.festival.1.0: Festival, dear! The slate's closed and the ribbons are open.
dlg.juno.bark.festival.1.0: It's festival day! I labeled my good shirt! It says 'Shirt (Festive)'!
dlg.piper.bark.festival.1.0: Festival! I have a song! Please clap at the bridge!
dlg.marcus.bark.festival.1.0: Festival. The stalls are level. Enjoy them.
dlg.odalys.bark.festival.1.0: Festival. Drink water between cups. That is a gentle order.
dlg.felix.bark.festival.1.0: Festival day. Even the fish are quiet. They're listening.
dlg.elara.bark.festival.1.0: Festival! I knitted the square a blanket! It's a very small square!
dlg.ione.bark.festival.1.0: A festival. The library's open, but I'm out. Come say hello.
dlg.gazette.news.ladder.0: A ladder was found leaning on nothing near the carpenter's. Investigators suspect optimism.
dlg.gazette.news.bell.0: The village bell rang once by accident and twice on purpose. Both were well received.
dlg.gazette.news.crow.0: A crow has taken up residence on the general store sign. It has been charged no rent.
dlg.gazette.news.kite.0: A kite was flown over the beach for most of an afternoon. It returned in better spirits than it left.
dlg.gazette.news.recipe.0: A soup recipe is going around. Everyone swears it is a family secret and everyone has a copy.
dlg.gazette.news.path.0: The path to the forest was swept by persons unknown. Residents are grateful and slightly suspicious.
dlg.gazette.news.hat.0: A hat blew across the square three times this week. It was returned to its owner three times.
dlg.gazette.news.well.0: The village well was cleaned and the water tastes, in the words of one resident, 'of Tuesday'.
dlg.gazette.news.owlpost.0: The mailbox was found full of acorns. The postal service denies involvement. The squirrels decline comment.
dlg.gazette.news.garden.0: Someone planted marigolds along the lane overnight. No one has confessed. Everyone has thanked everyone.
dlg.gazette.news.seedling.0: Seedlings are up all over the valley. The general store reports a run on small watering cans.
dlg.gazette.news.shade.0: Shade is now a currency. The big oak by the beach has been oversubscribed.
dlg.gazette.news.leaves.0: The leaves have turned. The library window has been declared the best view in the village.
dlg.gazette.news.frost.0: Frost on every windowsill this morning. The bakery smelled better than usual out of spite.
dlg.gazette.news.thunder.0: A storm rolled through. The blacksmith's forge, for once, was the quietest place in the village.
dlg.gazette.news.snowman.0: A snowman appeared on the green. By evening it had a scarf, a hat and a mild reputation.
dlg.gazette.news.felix.0: Felix reports a fish of unusual size. The pond has not confirmed. The pond rarely does.
dlg.gazette.news.dorian.0: Dorian was seen at the edge of the village square, listening. He stayed a full ten minutes.
dlg.gazette.news.elara.0: Elara has knitted a scarf for the clinic's roof. Dr. Penn has asked it to come down. It has not.
dlg.gazette.news.ione.0: Ione has reorganized the third shelf. Nobody has noticed. She says that is how you know it worked.
dlg.gazette.news.marcus.0: Marcus built a bench without a single crooked board. He seems unsure what to do with the feeling.
dlg.gazette.news.odalys.0: Dr. Penn closed the clinic ten minutes early. Authorities suspect a nap.
dlg.gazette.farm.rows.0: The rows at [farm] have been described as 'almost suspiciously straight'. Marcus is said to approve.
dlg.gazette.farm.busy.0: A busy farm, say the neighbors. [farm] is on everyone's route, and the animals have noticed.
dlg.gazette.farm.crate.0: The shipping crate at [farm] is rumored to be getting tired. It has asked for a longer lid.
dlg.gazette.farm.savings.0: Word is [player] has a tidy sum put by. The saloon has been very warm in its greetings.
dlg.gazette.farm.scarecrow.0: The scarecrow at [farm] has been seen in a new hat. Nobody has admitted to the hat.
dlg.gazette.weather.hotsun.0: Hot and bright. Drink water. Dr. Penn is watching, from the shade, with a clipboard.
dlg.gazette.weather.fallrain.0: Fall rain, steady and golden. Fine weather for soup and a long look out the window.
dlg.gazette.weather.deepsnow.0: Snow, soft and quiet. The village has lowered its voice. Mittens are in force.
dlg.gazette.weather.springwind.0: A spring wind. Petals will travel without a ticket. Washing lines are advised to hold on.
dlg.gazette.class.lantern.0: WANTED: A lantern that stays lit. Apply at the general store. Candles provided.
dlg.gazette.class.owl.0: LOST: A quiet afternoon. If found, please keep it and tell no one.
dlg.gazette.class.sock.0: FOUND: One sock, red, on the clinic roof. Owner may collect. Owner may also keep it up there.
dlg.gazette.class.stoolrepair.0: SERVICES: Stool leveling. Inquire at the carpenter's. The saloon stool is excluded on principle.
dlg.gazette.class.pie.0: FOR TRADE: One pumpkin pie for any kind word. Ask at the general store. The pie is patient.
dlg.gazette.class.duet.0: SEEKING: A voice for the second verse. Apply at the saloon. Bring your own key.
dlg.gazette.class.map.0: FOR SALE: A very old map of the valley. Several roads are in the wrong place. The view is correct.
dlg.gazette.class.thanks.0: NOTICE: A heartfelt thank-you is owed to whoever swept the lane. The lane is also grateful.
item.prop.cat.name: Gray Cat
item.prop.cat.desc: A small gray cat that belongs to the whole village.
item.prop.umbrella.name: Red Umbrella
item.prop.umbrella.desc: A large red umbrella with a story.
item.prop.note.name: Kind Note
item.prop.note.desc: A folded note tied with a red ribbon.
item.prop.lantern.name: Paper Lantern
item.prop.lantern.desc: A paper lantern, glowing and warm.
item.prop.trophy.name: Anvil Trophy
item.prop.trophy.desc: A tiny iron anvil with a fish on top. It does not do anything.
item.prop.pumpkin.name: Prize Pumpkin
item.prop.pumpkin.desc: A very large pumpkin wearing a ribbon.
item.prop.scarecrow.name: Contest Scarecrow
item.prop.scarecrow.desc: A scarecrow in a floppy patched hat.
item.prop.shell.name: Pink Shell
item.prop.shell.desc: A pink spiral shell. It says hello.
event.overheard_juno_bram_4.l1: Bram. Someday I'll open my own forge. A tiny one!
event.overheard_juno_bram_4.l3: You would? You'd sit on my bench?
event.overheard_juno_bram_4.l4: Hm. Move over. I'll bring the good tongs.
event.overheard_marcus_dorian_4.l1: Dorian. I built a window for the hut. Square. Oak.
event.overheard_marcus_dorian_4.l3: Facing the owl. You can say hello.
event.overheard_marcus_dorian_4.l4: ...Thank you. The owl will want a name.
event.overheard_wren_piper_4.l1: Piper, my darling. Next month, you headline. I mean it.
event.overheard_wren_piper_4.l2: Wren! Headline! Me! On your stage! I'll cry! Then write a song about crying!
event.overheard_wren_piper_4.l3: Do both. Cry first. Song after. The stool will survive.
event.overheard_wren_piper_4.l4: It's a deal! Actually, it's a duet!
event.overheard_tilda_felix_4.l1: Tilda, I brought a pie. For once. A fish pie. Don't judge.
event.overheard_tilda_felix_4.l2: Dear Felix, I'll judge it kindly. And salt it.
event.overheard_tilda_felix_4.l3: It's a fair sentence. Pass the fork.
event.overheard_tilda_felix_4.l4: To an old friend, dear. And to this very strange pie.
event.overheard_bram_marcus_1.l2: Your weld's clean. Don't tell Juno.
event.overheard_bram_marcus_2.l1: Hm. Handle for the big hammer?
event.overheard_bram_marcus_2.l2: Made you one. Oak. Measured twice. Your grip's in the shop.
event.overheard_bram_marcus_2.l4: Good. Don't thank me. I'll blush into the sawdust.
event.overheard_bram_marcus_3.l2: A hundred and four. All straight.
event.overheard_tilda_wren_1.l1: Wren, dear. Your chalkboard looks like my slate.
event.overheard_tilda_wren_1.l2: Imitation is flattery, my darling, with better lighting.
event.overheard_tilda_wren_1.l4: A ribbon! Pin it to the stool.
event.overheard_tilda_wren_2.l1: I heard something, dear. About a certain cat.
event.overheard_tilda_wren_2.l2: I heard it first, my darling. Three days ago.
event.overheard_tilda_wren_2.l3: Then we'll trade. You tell me yours.
event.overheard_tilda_wren_2.l4: Mine's better. It has a pickle in it.
event.overheard_tilda_wren_3.l1: Dear Wren, I've counted eleven hours. May I sit?
event.overheard_tilda_wren_3.l2: My darling Tilda, you've earned the good chair. Sit. Cider's on me.
event.overheard_tilda_wren_3.l3: Just one cup, dear. Then the slate.
event.overheard_tilda_wren_3.l4: The slate will wait. It's good at that.
event.overheard_piper_juno_1.l1: Juno! Could you hammer quieter? My ballad is drowning!
event.overheard_piper_juno_1.l2: Quieter? Piper, it's a forge! It's meant to be felt!
event.overheard_piper_juno_1.l3: I felt it in my teeth! Through the stage!
event.overheard_piper_juno_1.l4: Then the anvil's a fan! I'll take it!
event.overheard_piper_juno_2.l1: Juno! I wrote a song to the rhythm of your hammer!
event.overheard_piper_juno_2.l2: You did? Play it! No, wait, I'll hammer along!
event.overheard_piper_juno_2.l3: One, two, clang! That's the chorus!
event.overheard_piper_juno_2.l4: It's a banger! I'll label it 'Song (Forge)'!
event.overheard_piper_juno_3.l1: Juno, you made me a tiny stage out of a crate?
event.overheard_piper_juno_3.l2: It says 'Stage (Piper)'! I labeled it! Play on it!
event.overheard_piper_juno_3.l3: I'll play my best set! You watch!
event.overheard_piper_juno_3.l4: Okay! No, I'll hammer! No, watch! Both! Always both!
event.overheard_dorian_hazel_1.l2: (Dorian.) Good morning. Sit, if you like.
event.overheard_dorian_hazel_1.l4: (The best kind.) Stay as long as you need.
event.overheard_dorian_hazel_2.l1: ...I found a mushroom guide. Pressed leaves inside.
event.overheard_dorian_hazel_2.l2: (Pressed leaves.) May I borrow it? (I'll treat them as bookmarks.)
event.overheard_dorian_hazel_2.l3: ...They'd like that. They like being kept.
event.overheard_dorian_hazel_2.l4: (Then we agree.) I'll return it, with a leaf of my own.
event.overheard_dorian_hazel_3.l2: (We could.) The window faces the forest.
event.overheard_dorian_hazel_3.l4: (They always do.) I'll keep the chair warm.
event.overheard_felix_elara_1.l1: Elara. A fish doesn't want comfort. It wants to be free.
event.overheard_felix_elara_1.l2: Then it's a free, comfortable net! Everybody wins!
event.overheard_felix_elara_1.l3: ...It does look warm. Hand it over. For science.
event.overheard_felix_elara_1.l4: I knew you'd love it! I'll knit a bigger one!
event.overheard_felix_elara_2.l1: It was this big. Bigger. A true giant.
event.overheard_felix_elara_2.l2: I made a scarf this big! Same size! They'd be friends!
event.overheard_felix_elara_2.l3: A scarf-fish friendship. I like it. Tell no one.
event.overheard_felix_elara_2.l4: Everyone knows! I told the clinic!
event.overheard_felix_elara_3.l1: Quiet, yes. Until you count stitches aloud.
event.overheard_felix_elara_3.l3: ...It's soothing. Don't stop. The fish like it.
event.overheard_felix_elara_3.l4: I won't! Nineteen! Twenty! Fish are lovely listeners!
event.overheard_odalys_ione_1.l1: Ione. The library lamp was lit at midnight.
event.overheard_odalys_ione_1.l2: Dr. Penn. The clinic's was lit at one.
event.overheard_odalys_ione_1.l3: Professional courtesy. I'd call it a draw.
event.overheard_odalys_ione_1.l4: Then let's both go home. Tomorrow.
event.overheard_odalys_ione_2.l1: I prescribe you a nap, Ione. Ten minutes. Non-negotiable.
event.overheard_odalys_ione_2.l2: I prescribe you a novel, Dr. Penn. One chapter. Equally firm.
event.overheard_odalys_ione_2.l4: Agreed. Chapter one is short. The nap can be long.
event.overheard_odalys_ione_3.l1: Thank you for the tea, Ione. I will drink it slowly.
event.overheard_odalys_ione_3.l2: It's the calm kind. The library cat likes it too.
event.overheard_odalys_ione_3.l3: Then it is a verified remedy. Pass the cup.
dlg.gazette.head.hall.0: COMMUNITY HALL REOPENS: THE VILLAGE CELEBRATES
dlg.gazette.head.hallhalf.0: HALF THE HALL IS BACK, SAYS A HOPEFUL VILLAGE
dlg.gazette.head.barn.0: A NEW BARN RISES, STRAIGHT AS A RULER
dlg.gazette.news.hallroom.0: A room of the Community Hall has been restored. The village has begun to hope in earnest.
dlg.gazette.news.hallmore.0: Three rooms of the hall are open. The saloon has begun planning the party and the library the speeches.
dlg.gazette.news.halldone.0: The Community Hall stands whole again. The first thing anyone did inside was sit down and say nothing, happily.
dlg.gazette.news.coop.0: A new coop has gone up at [farm]. The chickens moved in at once and have already filed three complaints.
dlg.gazette.farm.coop.0: The coop at [farm] is the talk of the lane. The chickens decline interviews.
dlg.gazette.farm.barn.0: A barn now stands at [farm]. Marcus is said to have measured it three times and approved it twice.
dlg.gazette.farm.greenhouse.0: The greenhouse at [farm] glows warm on cold evenings. Neighbors report feeling hopeful about tomatoes.
dlg.gazette.farm.pack.0: [player] was seen carrying a larger pack. Tilda was asked what is in it. She declined to say.
dlg.gazette.farm.energy.0: [player] has been noticed working past noon without a yawn. Dr. Penn has taken the credit, quietly.
dlg.marcus.built.coop.0: Coop's standing. Level, plumb, dry. The chickens are lucky.
dlg.marcus.built.barn.0: The barn. Oak all the way through. Worth every plank.
dlg.marcus.built.greenhouse.0: The greenhouse glass is clean. Don't tell Dorian. He'll want one.
dlg.marcus.hall.half.0: The hall's roof is holding. Half the rooms are back. Good work.
dlg.tilda.pack.big.0: A bigger pack, dear! I hope you fill it with something sensible. Seeds, preferably.
dlg.tilda.hall.half.0: The hall's coming back, dear. I've dusted the slate for the opening.
dlg.odalys.energy.up.0: Your stamina's up. I did that. I'd like it noted. Quietly.
dlg.wren.hall.half.0: Half the hall's restored, my darling! The saloon's already planning the party.
dlg.wren.hall.done.0: The whole hall's open again. I cried. Into a pickle. Tell no one.
dlg.hazel.hall.room.0: (The hall has a room again.) The books are very interested.
dlg.bram.hall.iron.0: Hm. The hall's roof is iron-braced. Good iron. Don't tell Marcus I helped.
dlg.juno.gossip.bram.d.0: Bram pretends he doesn't read my labels! He moved one yesterday! It said 'Chair (Do Not)'! He sat on it! Defiantly!
dlg.bram.gossip.juno.d.0: Hm. Juno labeled my lunch. It said 'Lunch (Eaten)'. Accurate.
dlg.hazel.gossip.ione.d.0: (Ione rearranged the third shelf.) Nobody noticed. (I noticed.) I said nothing. It is our understanding.
dlg.ione.gossip.hazel.d.0: Hazel reads at the window every afternoon. She thinks I don't see.
dlg.ione.gossip.hazel.d.1: I don't mention it. The light is kind to her.
dlg.elara.gossip.odalys.d.0: Dr. Penn says she doesn't need mittens! She wore them all night! I saw! I'm not telling!
dlg.odalys.gossip.elara.d.0: Elara knits during consultations. It is unprofessional. The patients recover faster.
dlg.marcus.gossip.dorian.d.0: Dorian says three words a day. I count. Yesterday he said five.
dlg.marcus.gossip.dorian.d.1: We built a bench. Good day.
dlg.wren.gossip.piper.d.0: Piper's third verse is a masterpiece, my darling, and the rest is a hazard. I clap loudest at the bridge.
dlg.piper.gossip.wren.d.0: Wren pretends she doesn't sing along! She does! Every night! I hear her over the register!
dlg.tilda.gossip.felix.d.0: Felix has sold me the same carp four times, dear. It improves with each sale.
dlg.felix.gossip.tilda.d.0: Tilda keeps a tab for me on the slate. It's long. It's also very polite.
dlg.bram.gossip.marcus.d.1: I'd never say it to his face.
dlg.marcus.gossip.bram.d.0: Bram's welds are clean. Don't tell him I said so.
dlg.tilda.gossip.wren.d.0: Wren thinks I haven't noticed she copies my slate handwriting, dear. Imitation, flattery, and all that.
dlg.wren.gossip.tilda.d.0: Tilda's slate has more gossip than my bar, my darling. She calls it bookkeeping.
dlg.piper.gossip.juno.d.0: Juno hammers in time with my songs! She says it's a coincidence! It's a rhythm section!
dlg.juno.gossip.piper.d.0: Piper's too loud! Wonderful, but too loud! I labeled my ears! 'Ears (Delighted)'!
dlg.dorian.gossip.hazel.d.0: ...Hazel borrows my pressed leaves. Returns them with a note.
dlg.dorian.gossip.hazel.d.1: The notes are small. I keep them.
dlg.hazel.gossip.dorian.d.0: (Dorian leaves pressed leaves in the books.) A kind habit. (I never mention it.) I return them, annotated.
dlg.felix.gossip.elara.d.0: Elara knits nets for fish. Fish don't use them. She brings another.
dlg.felix.gossip.elara.d.1: It's very touching and slightly damp.
dlg.elara.gossip.felix.d.0: Felix tells the best fish stories! They get bigger every time! I knit a scarf to match!
dlg.odalys.gossip.ione.d.0: Ione prescribes me novels. I follow the prescription. Chapter one only.
dlg.ione.gossip.odalys.d.0: Dr. Penn naps in the reading room when she thinks no one is looking.
dlg.cameo.juno.bram8.d.0: Bram talked to you! Properly! With words! He hummed at me once and I labeled it 'Event (Rare)'!
dlg.cameo.bram.juno8.d.0: Hm. She told you about the forge. Hm. She's ready. Don't tell her I said.
dlg.cameo.ione.hazel8.d.0: Hazel was smiling at the returns desk this morning. I think you had something to do with it. Thank you.
dlg.cameo.hazel.ione8.d.0: (Ione was quiet this morning. A good quiet.) You talked with her. (Thank you. I noticed.)
dlg.cameo.piper.wren8.d.0: Wren told you the bag thing! She never tells anyone! I knew about the bag! I wrote a song about the bag! She hates it!
dlg.cameo.wren.piper8.d.0: My darling Piper played you the new one, didn't she? I heard the bridge from the cellar. I wept into a pickle.
dlg.cameo.felix.tilda8.d.0: Tilda told you something, didn't she. She's never told me. Thirty years, and not a word. Hm. I respect it.
dlg.cameo.tilda.felix8.d.0: I hear Felix told you about the big one, dear. It's been this big for thirty years. It's a good fish.
dlg.cameo.marcus.dorian8.d.0: Dorian said a whole sentence yesterday. About you. I built him a shelf. It seemed right.
dlg.cameo.dorian.marcus8.d.0: ...Marcus finished the roof. He looked up at it a long time. ...I stood with him.
dlg.cameo.odalys.elara8.d.0: Elara has been unusually calm. I suspect you. It is a clinical improvement. Thank you.
dlg.cameo.elara.odalys8.d.0: Dr. Penn took a nap! A real one! With the lamp off! I heard you helped! I'm knitting you something!
dlg.cameo.juno.piper4.d.0: Piper played you a song! I heard it through the wall! It was too loud! It was perfect! I labeled the wall 'Wall (Thin)'!
dlg.cameo.piper.juno4.d.0: Juno showed you the label maker! She showed me first! I have eleven labels! One says 'Piper (Loud)'! It's accurate!
dlg.gazette.news.gifts.0: A steady stream of small gifts has been seen around the village this week. Nobody will say who is behind it. Everybody knows.
dlg.gazette.news.errands.0: A good week for favors. A job was finished, a promise kept, and a neighbor said thank you out loud.
dlg.gazette.news.practice.0: Practice paid off for somebody this week. Calloused hands were seen. The village approves.
dlg.gazette.news.moment.0: Something happened in the village this week that people are still talking about. Details are being improved with each telling.
dlg.gazette.farm.bigsale.0: The shipping bin at [farm] did very well this week. The crate is said to be insufferable about it.
dlg.gazette.farm.giver.0: [player] has been generous this week. The Gazette notes it, and the Gazette does not note things lightly.
dlg.gazette.farm.helper.0: [player] finished a job for a neighbor this week. It was done properly. That is the review.
dlg.gazette.head.bigsale.0: RECORD WEEK AT THE SHIPPING BIN
dlg.gazette.head.moment.0: A WEEK THE VILLAGE WILL REMEMBER
dlg.sale.tilda.d.0: A very full bin yesterday, dear! The seed shelf is jealous. I've put a little extra in your next order.
dlg.sale.wren.d.0: I hear the bin did very well, my darling. The whole valley's talking. Sit. First cup's on the house, second's on the shipping.
dlg.sale.felix.d.0: Heard you had a big haul. Hm. Bigger than my biggest fish. Almost. It was this big.
dlg.sale.marcus.d.0: Good sale. A farm that pays can build. Think about the barn.
inventory.confirm_discard: Throw this whole stack away for good? (Selling it in the shipping bin pays gold instead.)
